  SCV's spline failures were loud there (KSPLINT printed and stopped, [ksplint.f:20-23](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/ksplint.f#L20-L23)); they became silent with [ecce23f0](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/ecce23f0) (2026-10-29, numerics' one error contract). The run-log-only errors came with eos's one message module, [077d26a5](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/077d26a5) (2026-10-29), and lir's optional `ierr`, which the MHD calls did not pass, with M15's fix ([df8a8487](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/df8a8487)).
- **Now:** `eos_log` and `eos_report`, [eos_messages.f90:27-36](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/eos/eos_messages.f90#L27-L36); lir's status at MHD's calls, [mhd_eos.f90:653-654](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/eos/mhd/mhd_eos.f90#L653-L654), [:821-835](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/eos/mhd/mhd_eos.f90#L821-L835); `report_spline_failure`, [scv_eos.f90:342-351](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L342-L351).
- **What was wrong:** the 35 errors eos returns `ierr` for (β ≤ 0, MHD and OPAL points off their tables, failed searches, bad compositions) went to the run log only, so a run that stopped on one said nothing on the terminal; lir's failures went unreported at MHD's three calls; SCV's two splint failures returned `ierr` without a message.
- **What we did:** every error goes through `eos_report`, terminal and run log; `eos_log` keeps the notes. lir's `ierr` is passed at the three MHD calls and up to `compute_mhd_eos`, and SCV's splint failures are reported before they return. `test_eos` checks lir's status. Byte-identical.

### M74. blend_eos's OPAL step returned from blend_eos

- **Status:** fixed in [2b671c3a](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/2b671c3a) (2026-10-29). The re-evaluation's issue 1. Byte-identical.
- **In the original F77?** Yes, harmlessly. Each OPAL block of EQSTAT2 leaves with `GOTO 998`, the routine's end ([eqstat2.f:270-312](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqstat2.f#L270-L312), [:409-412](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqstat2.f#L409-L412)):
  ```fortran
           IF(.NOT.LTAB)GOTO 998  ! Point is not in OPAL 1995 EOS table, so exit.
  ...
   998  CONTINUE
        Z = Z0
        RETURN
  ```
  Nothing followed the OPAL blocks, so the jump skipped nothing. It became a defect when eos/README.md's recipe ([6927b7ce](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/6927b7ce), 2026-10-29) offered "a step in blend_eos ... after [OPAL] otherwise".
- **Now:** `blend_eos`, [blended_eos.f90:156-179](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L156-L179), and `opal_step`, [:271-302](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L271-L302).
- **What was wrong:** the OPAL step's early returns left `blend_eos` itself, so a step a newcomer placed after it, as the README said, would never run.
- **What we did:** `blend_eos` calls four step subroutines in order (`zone_mixture`, `radiation_share`, `gas_eos`, `opal_step`); OPAL's returns leave `opal_step` only. `test_eos`'s pin is unchanged.

### M75. The Fermi-Dirac and OPAL readers trusted their tables, and an OPAL vintage without an open table read unit 0

- **Status:** fixed in [771557ec](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/771557ec) (2026-10-29). Byte-identical.
- **In the original F77?** Partly. The readers' reads had no `IOSTAT`, and their layout errors stopped without closing the table ([setups.f:164-167](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/setups.f#L164-L167), [readco.f:54-87](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/readco.f#L54-L87), [readcoeos01.f:64-97](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/readcoeos01.f#L64-L97), [readcoeos06.f:61-95](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/readcoeos06.f#L61-L95)):
  ```fortran
        OPEN(UNIT=IFERMI,FILE=FFERMI,FORM='FORMATTED',STATUS='OLD')
        READ(IFERMI,150)  (DVAL(I), I = 1,43)                    ! setups.f
  ```
  The read of unit 0 is 2026: each F77 OPAL reader opened its own table ([readco.f:48](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/readco.f#L48)); the YREC-team commit [bbdfa0f6](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/bbdfa0f6) (2025-08-22) moved the open to PARMIN, and [c00a9a20](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/c00a9a20) (2026-10-11) into `eos_init` on a `newunit`, so a vintage installed without `eos_init` found its unit at 0.
- **Now:** `read_fermi_table`, [yale_eos.f90:1104-1159](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/eos/yale/yale_eos.f90#L1104-L1159); `readco` (1995), [opal95_eos.f90:947-1106](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/eos/opal/opal95_eos.f90#L947-L1106); `readcoeos` (2001, 2006), [opal_eos.f90:821-979](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/eos/opal/opal_eos.f90#L821-L979).
- **What was wrong:** a truncated Fermi-Dirac or OPAL table ended the run in a runtime error, although `eos_init` promises `ierr`; the layout errors left the unit open; a vintage counted as loaded before its table was read; and a vintage switched on by `set_eos_settings` alone (test code) read unit 0.
- **What we did:** every read has an `iostat`; a failed read or a layout error is `ierr = 1` with a message naming the table, and closes it; a table counts as loaded once it is read; a reader with no table open says so and returns `ierr = 1`. `test_eos` checks a missing and a truncated table of each kind.

### M76. The Saha solver started from the last solve anywhere

- **Status:** fixed in [be874f6c](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/be874f6c) (2026-10-29). The first evaluation's F6. Results change in 14 of the 56 decks, at the solver's tolerance.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. EQSAHA's three unknowns start from DATA values and are SAVEd, so each solve starts from the previous call's solution, whichever caller made it ([eqsaha.f:25-27](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqsaha.f#L25-L27), [:155-158](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqsaha.f#L155-L158)):
  ```fortran
        DATA E,SAHEX1,SAHEX2/0.1D0,0.0D0,0.0D0/
        DATA STOLEE/1.0D-09/
        SAVE
  ```
- **Now:** `compute_saha_eos`, [yale_eos.f90:198-233](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/eos/yale/yale_eos.f90#L198-L233), and the record's `saha_*` fields, [eos_results.f90:54-55](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/eos/eos_results.f90#L54-L55).
- **What was wrong:** a zone's result depended, within the solver's tolerance (1e-9 in E), on which EOS call had come before it anywhere in the code.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the same input gives the same output; a warm start is the caller's choice.
- **What we did:** the three unknowns (E and the He⁺ and He⁺⁺ fractions) are fields of `eos_result`, which the solver starts from and returns its solution in, as the fully ionized iteration does with the density: a record the caller carries from zone to zone warm-starts from the zone before, and a new record starts from E = 0.1 with no ionized helium, the old first start. The numerical derivatives' shifted evaluations leave the caller's record as it was. `yale_eos` keeps no state of the solver.
  - EOS2's measurement (the series' end against the readers' commit): 42 decks byte-identical; six move by 4e-14 to 3e-12 in final log L, the 0.03 Msun deck by 3e-9, six settling solar decks by 8e-8 to 1.5e-5 (each one model more or fewer), and `rv_sbm2` by 8e-6 (age-matched 4e-4; 900 models for 896). On the merged tree 12 decks move, the settling solar decks by up to 2.4e-5.

### M77. GYRE's ε and its derivative columns described different ε

- **Status:** fixed in [9168a576](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/9168a576) (2026-10-29). The net re-evaluation's possible bug 1. Results change in the GYRE and GSM files only, above log T 7.5.
- **In the original F77?** Partly. The F77 had no GYRE writer, but its pulse model file wrote the same pair: COEFFT's `SESUM`, the five chains without the thermal neutrino loss, beside ENGEB's derivatives, from which the loss's are subtracted above `TCUT(5)` = 7.5 ([coefft.f:347](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/coefft.f#L347), [:414-415](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/coefft.f#L414-L415), [engeb.f:1227-1228](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/engeb.f#L1227-L1228), [wrtmod.f:217-219](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/wrtmod.f#L217-L219)):
  ```fortran
              SESUM(IM) = EG(1)+EG(2)+EG(3)+EG(4)+EG(5)          ! coefft.f
              PQED(IM) = QED
              PQET(IM) = QET
           PET = PET - QETNX                                    ! engeb.f
           PEP = PEP - QEDNX
  ```
  The GYRE writer came with [9df62b7e](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/9df62b7e) (2026-08-20) and kept the pairing.
- **Now:** `deps_nuc_dlnrho` and `deps_nuc_dlnt`, taken in `compute_nuclear_energy` before the thermal neutrino loss is added ([nuclear_energy.f90:139-140](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/net/nuclear_energy.f90#L139-L140)), and `store_pulse_derivatives` ([structure_equations.f90:309-324](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/core/structure/structure_equations.f90#L309-L324)).
- **What was wrong:** the GYRE and GSM files write ε = `eps_total`, the chains' sum without the thermal neutrino loss, but `eps_eps_T` and `eps_eps_rho` were the Henyey's dε/d ln T and dε/d ln ρ, which subtract the loss's derivatives. Above log T 7.5, where the loss is computed, the two described different ε: in a neutrino-cooled layer ε was zero while `eps_eps_T` was not, and negative.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** GYRE's nonadiabatic equations use ε with its derivatives, so they must be one ε's. MESA's `pulse_gyre.f90` writes `eps_nuc` with `d_epsnuc_dlnT` and `d_epsnuc_dlnd`, all three without the thermal neutrinos (MESA keeps those in `non_nuc_neu`).
- **What we did:** the derivative columns are ε_nuc's; ε and the Henyey derivatives are unchanged, and FGONG has no derivative columns. On the 1 Msun ZAHB-to-TAHB deck with GYRE files every 150 models (41 files) only `eps_eps_T` and `eps_eps_rho` change, at the points above log T 7.5: at the centre (log T 8.07 to 8.26) `eps_eps_T` by 3e-5 to 3e-3 relative; in the cooler layers where the loss dominates, the old column was negative at 162-413 points and nonzero at 82-133 points where ε = 0, the new one at none. No shipped deck writes GYRE files, and the solar baselines' (log T < 7.5) are unchanged. MESA's convention is a revisable choice (under "Decisions needed").

### M78. The interior GYRE file computed its own N²

- **Status:** fixed in [86b3fa63](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/86b3fa63) (2026-10-29). The io re-evaluation's issue 12. Results change in that file's N² column only.
- **In the original F77?** No. The F77's pulse model file had no N² column; it left N² to the pulsation code ([wrtmod.f:217-220](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/wrtmod.f#L217-L220)). The interval file's writer came with [9df62b7e](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/9df62b7e) (2026-08-20), its own thermal-form N², and its second copy of the gradient form with [2ed398ca](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/2ed398ca) and [67b36131](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/67b36131) (2026-08-30).
- **Now:** `write_interior_gyre`, [yrec_output.f90:202-215](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/io/yrec_output.f90#L202-L215), writes the stitched model's first `nz` pulse points through the one GYRE text writer, `write_gyre_pulse` ([pulsation_output.f90:234-254](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/io/pulsation_output.f90#L234-L254)).
- **What was wrong:** `write_gyre_pulse` (the file every `pulse_gyre_interval` models) recomputed every column from the star's arrays, among them a second copy of `build_pulse_points`' N² with its operands in another order, and copied point nz−1's N² to the last point. It took the star and six of the star's own arrays (`docs/GUIDELINES.md` star rule 3), and the luminosity under the name `log_luminosity` although it held L/L☉.
- **What we did:** the interval file is the stitched model's interior points (the interior always comes first), with the outermost interior shell's M, R and L as its globals, as before; the one GYRE text writer takes the name `write_gyre_pulse` (it was `write_gyre_ext`). On the solar deck (17 interval files) and the ZAHB deck (11) only N² changes: at points 2 to nz−1 by round-off (at most 3.5e-12 and 1.5e-12 of the file's largest |N²|), and the last point is its own value now, 4.2% and 4.9% from its neighbour's. No shipped deck sets `pulse_gyre_interval`. O22 (the profile's N² column) is unchanged.

### M79. An empty starting model ended in a runtime error

- **Status:** fixed in [55cf35e5](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/55cf35e5) (2026-10-29). The io re-evaluation's possible bug 6. Error path only.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. STARIN rewinds the model unit and reads the four-character tag with no `IOSTAT` ([starin.f:167-169](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/starin.f#L167-L169)):
  ```fortran
        REWIND IREAD
        READ(IREAD,10) ATEMP
   10   FORMAT(A4)
  ```
- **Now:** `read_model_format_tag`, [model_files.f90:129-140](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/io/model_files.f90#L129-L140), called by `read_starting_model_file` ([starting_model.f90:284](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L284)).
- **What was wrong:** the format tag was read without `iostat`, so an empty starting model stopped the run with "Fortran runtime error: End of file" and exit status 2. M23's fix had checked every other read of the model file.
- **What we did:** `model_files` reads the tag with `iostat` and reports "cannot read the format tag of the starting model <path>: <reason>", terminal and run log; the run exits 1. `test_error_exit`'s malformed-model test has an empty case, and `test_io` checks it too.

### M80. The profile's chain fractions do not add up to 1 where the α captures burn

- **Status:** decided and documented in [aca05304](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/aca05304) (2026-10-29); no output changes. The state re-evaluation's possible bug 5.
- **In the original F77?** No. COEFFT's fractions are of the five chains' own sum, so they add up to 1, and the α captures go to the luminosity budget only ([coefft.f:347-357](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/coefft.f#L347-L357)):
  ```fortran
              SESUM(IM) = EG(1)+EG(2)+EG(3)+EG(4)+EG(5)
  ...
              DO J = 1,5
                 SEG(J,IM) = EG(J)*ESUMI
  ```
  The case came with M1's fix ([ee268284](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/ee268284), 2026-10-29), which put the α captures into the total and kept the five fractions.
- **Now:** `store_zone_energy_channels`, [structure_equations.f90:242-267](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/core/structure/structure_equations.f90#L242-L267), and the profile's `interior_value`, [stitched_model.f90:514-525](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/core/diagnostics/stitched_model.f90#L514-L525).
- **What is the case:** since M1, the profile's `eps_nuc` (`eps_total`) includes the α captures, while `eps_ppI` … `eps_he3` (`eps_channels` rows 1-5) are the fractions of the five chains that have a slot; the α captures have none, so where they burn the five add up to 1 minus their share. On the 1 Msun ZAHB deck they add up to 1 on the ZAHB; in core helium burning the α captures' share at the centre is 3.6% at Y_c = 0.76, 18% at 0.30, 42% at 0.087 and 99% at 0.002, and close to all of ε_nuc toward the convective core's edge, where ¹²C(α,γ) outruns the triple α.
- **What we did:** each column stays its own chain's share; the α captures' is 1 minus the sum (folding it into `eps_he3` would lose the triple α's). The comments where the fractions are made say so, as do `io/README.md` and `star_info`'s member comment. A column of its own would need an `eps_channels` row; it is left to the authors.

### M81. log10 G was 0 until run_setup set it

- **Status:** fixed in [454014c0](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/454014c0) (2026-10-29). The state re-evaluation's possible bug 3. Latent: every run set it before any reader.
- **In the original F77?** Yes, in kind. `CGL` is a member of `COMMON /CONST2/`, assigned only in SETUPS, which MAIN calls right after PARMIN; nothing initializes it ([setups.f:51](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/setups.f#L51), [:106-107](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/setups.f#L106-L107)):
  ```fortran
        COMMON/CONST2/CGAS,CA3,CA3L,CSIG,CSIGL,CGL,CMKH,CMKHN
  C log of Gravitational constant G=6.67259D-8
        CGL = -7.17571D0
  ```
  The F77 had no kernel that ran without SETUPS. The module variable without an initializer came with [a7f1bee4](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/a7f1bee4) (2026-08-20).
- **Now:** `cgl`'s initializer, [physical_constants.f90:69](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/state/physical_constants.f90#L69); the kernels read `log10_gravitational_constant` from their records (rotation's settings, the envelope kernel's `envint_config`, the shell equations' `structure_settings`).
- **What was wrong:** `physical_constants`' `cgl` had no initializer, so it was 0 until `set_up_constants_and_tables` assigned it. Star-blind kernels read it (the envelope integrands and kernel, the shell equations, rotation's shape, stability coefficients and magnetic braking), so a kernel test that did not run `run_setup` computed with G = 1 without a word; rotation's tests set the literal −7.17571 by hand to avoid it.
- **What we did:** `cgl` starts at `log10_newton_g_default`; rotation's settings record and the envelope kernel's and shell equations' configuration records carry log10 G, which those kernels read instead of the global, copied by their builders from the same function; `tools/check_boundaries.py` fails when a physics domain, rotation or a star-blind kernel reads `cgl`. The tests' hand-set values are gone. Byte-identical: the rotating decks, the unit tests, and the full set with the next commits.

### M82. The neutrino table printed a stale X(⁷Be) for shells it did not compute

- **Status:** fixed in [33760aa0](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/33760aa0) (2026-10-29). Latent: no deck reaches it.
- **In the original F77?** No. MAIN's table fills every shell with log T ≥ 6, with no cutoff gate, and prints only the shells with T ≥ 5e6 K, so every printed shell was filled; the table was also switched off in the source ([main.f:324](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L324), [:353](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L353), [:370](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L370), [:393](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L393)):
  ```fortran
        LNUTAB = .FALSE.
           IF(TL.LT.6.0D0)GOTO 666
           BE7M(I) = BE7MASSFRACTION
           IF(T6.LT.5.0D0)GOTO 141
  ```
  [9be2a129](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/9be2a129) (2026-10-10) added the cutoff to the fill loop's exit, on a star member that kept its values from card to card since [732cf038](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/732cf038) (2026-08-21).
- **Now:** `write_neutrino_flux_table`, [neutrino_flux_output.f90:39-140](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/core/diagnostics/neutrino_flux_output.f90#L39-L140).
- **What was wrong:** the table fills a shell's X(⁷Be) only for shells with log T ≥ 6 above the burning cutoff, and its profile loop prints every shell with T ≥ 5e6 K. With the cutoff control `nuclear_logT_cutoffs(1)` above log T = 6.7 (the default is 6.5), the shells between were printed with whatever an earlier card's table had left in the star member, or 0.
- **What we did:** the per-shell arrays are locals of the procedure, zeroed at entry, as its fluxes already were, so such a shell prints 0, "not computed"; the two star members are gone. Byte-identical on every deck and on a variant of `cm_base` that writes the table.

### M83. check_star_contracts told procedures apart by name only

- **Status:** fixed in [f5a88324](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/f5a88324) (2026-10-29). The state re-evaluation's issue 7. A tool; no output.
- **In the original F77?** No; `tools/check_star_contracts.py` is 2026 (since [758cab27](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/758cab27), 2026-10-10).
- **Now:** `tools/check_star_contracts.py` ([check_star_contracts.py](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/tools/check_star_contracts.py)).
- **What was wrong:** the checker kept one procedure per name, so the second of two procedures with the same name (`secular_transport`'s `wind_now`, the second `write_gsm_pulse`) was never checked, and a callee's intents came from whichever was found first; it also counted `read(...) s%x` as a read of `s%x`.
- **What we did:** procedures are keyed by module and host, calls are resolved by scope and `use`, and a read statement's target or an (de)allocated member is a write; `gen_star_docs.py` reuses the keys and the resolution. A contract on `secular_transport`'s `wind_now` is now checked, and a wrong one fails, where the old checker passed it.

### M84. The sample_cases/LowM_HB decks name a starting model that does not exist

- **Status:** open (found 2026-10-29 by the controls package, measuring M47). A deck fix; no code changes.
- **In the original F77?** No; the F77 import has no sample_cases/ and no ZAHB model. The decks came with the YREC-team commit [3f057e31](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/3f057e31) (2026-02-23), whose `FFIRST` named `../../input/models/zahb/...`; the ZAHB models were added straight to `startmodels/zahb/` ([e1fd39c8](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/e1fd39c8), 2026-03-05), and [029f978d](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/029f978d) (2026-08-29) carried the path into the inlists.
- **Now:** `first_model_file` in each of the 28 decks of `sample_cases/LowM_HB/` (for example [Solar_m1p0feh+0p0_PARSEC_TAHB.inlist:68](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/sample_cases/LowM_HB/Solar_m1p0feh+0p0_PARSEC_TAHB.inlist#L68)).
- **What is wrong:** 27 of the decks name `../../input/models/zahb/<mass>preZAHB.last` and one an absolute path on an author's machine; none of those files exists, so every deck stops at the open. The models ship as `startmodels/zahb/<mass>preZAHB.last`, which `sample_cases/TAHB`'s decks reach as `{YREC_START}/zahb/...`. `sample_cases/TAHB/Solar_m1p0feh+0p0_GN93_MESA_TAHB.inlist` names `{YREC_INPUT}/models/zahb/100mSOLpreZAHB.last`, missing too.
- **Proposed fix:** `first_model_file = "{YREC_START}/zahb/<mass>preZAHB.last"` in the 29 decks, then a run of each to its first card's end. No code changes.

### M85. After a later card's Z rescale, the EOS mixture keeps the first card's metals

- **Status:** fixed in round 2B (2026-11-13, core's B list item 11, with M96; measured below). Found 2026-10-29 by the EOS package.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. STARIN computes the envelope mixture (`XENV`, `ZENV`, `AMUENV`, `FXENV`) on the first card only, and on a later card RSCALE sets `ZENV` to the new Z and leaves the rest ([starin.f:781](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/starin.f#L781), [rscale.f:80-84](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/rscale.f#L80-L84)):
  ```fortran
        IF(NK.GT.1) GOTO 630                                   ! starin.f
              ZENV0 = RESCAL(3,NK)                             ! rscale.f
  C DBG 4/95 BUG FIX ZENV IS USED IN MANY ROUTINES AND NOT ZENV0 SO CHANGE
  C     ZENV WHENEVER Z IS CHANGED.
              ZENV = ZENV0
  ```
- **Now:** `rescale_interior_z`, [model_rescaling.f90:140-170](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/core/model/model_rescaling.f90#L140-L170), calls `eos_set_mixture` with the new Z and the old inverse weight and number fractions ([:158-160](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/core/model/model_rescaling.f90#L158-L160)); `update_surface_mixture` recomputes the mixture only on the first card ([starting_model.f90:958](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L958)).
- **What is wrong:** from the second card on, eos's mixture has the new Z_env but the metals of the first card's Z, so 1/μ_ion and the Saha abundances are the old Z's. `testsuite/Test_m0p7feh-0p75_GN93_TAHB` rescales Z on ten cards, nine after the first; it rescales X too, so its zones take the excess branch with Z − Z_env = 0, still with the first card's metals.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the EOS's mixture is the model's.
- **Proposed fix:** `rescale_interior_z` recomputes the envelope mixture with `update_surface_mixture`'s algorithm (one shared routine) before `eos_set_mixture`; then `eos_set_mixture` can check that the metals add up to Z (Σ fx_i A_i times the inverse weight). One measured commit, in core/model; the decks with a later card's Z rescale move. Until then `eos_set_mixture` checks nothing about the mixture, since this case would trip such a check in a shipped deck.
- **Round 2 (2026-11-12/13):** core's B list (`audit/module-evaluation-7-2026-11-10/B_LIST_CORE.md`, item 11, with M96), measured in round 2 (scratch, `--set all`): one deck moves, Test_solarcal_noGS_norot (pinned): 442 models both, log L -5.4e-11, log Teff -2.0e-11, ages in the 9th digit; M85 alone gives the whole change. testsuite/Test_m0p7feh-0p75_GN93_TAHB cut to 300 models: at most 1.3e-6 in a history column. Recommended, with M96 in one commit.
- **What we did:** round 2B (2026-11-13), with M96: the envelope mixture's arithmetic (`update_surface_mixture`'s, AMUENV's) is one star-free kernel, model_rescaling's `compute_envelope_mixture` (Y_env, Z without C, N and O, 1/mu_ion and the number fractions, from X_env, Z_env and He3 and the controls' metal weights, in the old order, so the first card is bit for bit as before). `update_surface_mixture` calls it on the first card; `rescale_interior_z` calls it on a card after the first that rescales Z, with that card's Z and the first card's X_env and He3 (X_env stays the Yale EOS's reference, MHP 7/99), and installs the whole mixture (`install_surface_mixture_settings`: convection's Z without C, N and O, M96's floor, and the EOS mixture, M85's metals). Measured on the 56-deck set and the 35 pins against the previous commit's baseline: RESULT: 1 NOT IDENTICAL; pins 34 OK, 1 DIFF: `examples/run_standard_solar_model/Test_solarcal_noGS_norot` (.log, its pin, and .mod), the deck whose cycles' first card rescales Z to the calibrated Z/X: 442 models both, the same final age, log L -5.4e-11, log Teff -2.0e-11, final timestep 1.585122e7 to 1.585124e7 yr; its log's progress lines differ in the age alone (the first at model 250 by 5.7e-9 relative, the largest 1.9e-8 at model 300); the final profile at most 1.6e-5 in log rho and 8.5e-3 in Li7 at one zone (Be9 7.0e-3), as round 2 found. Pin re-seeded: `Test_solarcal_noGS_norot.log`. The decks of round 2's measurement, run alone again, reproduce it: `testsuite/Test_m0p7feh-0p75_GN93_TAHB` cut to 300 models on card 11 (Z 0.020 to 0.003 over cards 2-10): 300 models both, final log L +4.3e-9, log Teff -5.2e-10, age +6.7e-9 relative; history at most 1.26e-6 relative (cz_bot_mass, model 282), the final profile's O16 1.6e-3 at one zone of the convective core's edge; `examples/run_from_seed_to_start/m10000gs98z001000_prems` (Z 0.002 to 0.001 on card 2): 10 models, log L -1.7e-9, log Teff -3.1e-10. M85 carries the change; M96's floor (0.99e-3 (Z - Z_noCNO) on O16 in convection zones) binds in no deck run (round 2 measured each alone). Test: `test_model_kernels` checks `compute_envelope_mixture` on a ten-metal mixture of unequal weights (Y, the number fractions' sum, the mass fractions they give back, 1/mu_ion, Z without C, N and O), six checks, each caught by a mutation.

### M86. Before the first card's update_surface_mixture, the EOS mixture holds the run plan's values

- **Status:** fixed in round 2B (2026-11-13, core's B list item 12; two logs moved, below). Found 2026-10-29 by the EOS package. Round 1B found that it causes every Saha non-convergence of M293 (below).
- **In the original F77?** Yes. On the first card STARIN's envelope refit evaluates the EOS of the new last shell ([starin.f:554-556](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/starin.f#L554-L556)) and integrates a shallower envelope ([starin.f:609-611](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/starin.f#L609-L611)) before its mixture block sets `XENV`, `AMUENV` and `FXENV` ([starin.f:795-820](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/starin.f#L795-L820)); `ZENV` is PARMIN's, the last card's rescale Z ([parmin.f:1378](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/parmin.f#L1378)):
  ```fortran
           IF(RESCAL(3,NKIND).GE.0.0D0)  ZENV=RESCAL(3,NKIND)    ! parmin.f
  ```
- **Now:** `set_run_plan_envelope_z`, [run_setup.f90:59-71](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/core/run/run_setup.f90#L59-L71), called by `prepare_run`; in `read_starting_model` the first card's `rescale_and_refit_envelope` ([starting_model.f90:189](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L189)) runs before `update_surface_mixture` ([:194](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L194)).
- **What is wrong:** `prepare_run`'s `eos_set_mixture` passes X_env = 0 and an inverse weight and number fractions not yet set (zero storage: the star members have no initializer), as the read-time call did before [498cb8c7](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/498cb8c7) moved it. An envelope refit on the first card (`change_envelope_mass_flag`) evaluates the EOS with them, and a Z rescale on the first card passes them on again.
- **Measured in round 1B (2026-11-12, eos's hand-back §5, item 6):** at 1395075b `read_starting_model` still calls `rescale_and_refit_envelope` ([starting_model.f90:224](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1395075b/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L224)) before `update_surface_mixture` ([:229](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1395075b/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L229)); the refit's `integrate_envelope_to_new_fit` ([:684](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1395075b/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L684)) integrates the envelope and atmosphere through `eos_get` ([envelope_integration_kernel.f90:425-427](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1395075b/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L425-L427)) with the run plan's mixture (X_env 0 and the envelope's 1/A sum 0; star_info_lib's comment on `envelope_hydrogen_fraction` notes the early 0). A probe in `Test_m10000_feh0_noGSstdcno_ZAMS` found 3,772 EOS calls there with a He number fraction of −0.336, and every Saha non-convergence the 56-deck set reaches comes from them: 2,212 in that deck and 5 in `Test_m0030_feh0_noGS_ZAMS` (M293). Three of the 56 decks refit on their first card: those two and `Test_m1000_feh0_noGSstdpp_ZAMS`. `test_convection` meets the same mechanism through its own setup (M308).
- **Proposed fix:** compute `update_surface_mixture`'s mixture before the refit (`eos_set_mixture` from the model's surface composition), or skip `prepare_run`'s call while the star's mixture is unset. Results change for the decks that refit the envelope on their first card. Round 1B proposes it as a measured fix in core's round 2 (PLAN.md section 6, f).
- **Round 2 (2026-11-12/13):** core's B list (`audit/module-evaluation-7-2026-11-10/B_LIST_CORE.md`, item 12), measured in round 2 (scratch, `--set all`): `update_surface_mixture` called once, right after `rescale_model` in `rescale_and_refit_envelope`, moves two run logs only, Test_m0030_feh0_noGS_ZAMS (pinned) and Test_m10000_feh0_noGSstdcno_ZAMS: their Saha non-convergence lines go, 5 and 2,212 to 0 (M293's 2,217); every other byte identical. Recommended.
- **What we did:** round 2B (2026-11-13): `update_surface_mixture` (the star's envelope mixture: the EOS's and convection's, and kap's surface tables for X_env) is called once, right after `rescale_model` in `rescale_and_refit_envelope`, before the refit evaluates the EOS and the opacities, instead of after the refit in `read_starting_model` (round 2's form C). On the first card the refit's envelope integration now sees the model's mixture, not the run plan's partial one (X_env 0, its weights unset). Measured on the 56-deck set and the 35 pins against the previous fix's snapshot: RESULT: 2 NOT IDENTICAL; pins 34 OK, 1 DIFF. The two run logs, and in them only the Saha non-convergence lines: `Test_m0030_feh0_noGS_ZAMS.log` (pinned) loses its 5, `Test_m10000_feh0_noGSstdcno_ZAMS.log` its 2,212 (2,243 lines to 31); their .mod files and every other file are byte-identical, as round 2 found (the table EOS stages replace the Saha result at every refit point). On the shipped decks outside the set (M293's count, each card capped at 5 models): 41,128 non-convergences in 35 decks before, none after. No test: the order is `read_starting_model`'s, private; `test_eos` checks the non-convergence the old order caused (M293).

### M87. test_eos's Debye-Hückel check cannot see a wrong charge

- **Status:** fixed (test) in [8a2a5602](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/8a2a5602) (2026-11-10, round 1's eos). The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** No; the check came with M37's fix ([15af2ef3](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/15af2ef3), 2026-10-29).
- **Now:** `debye_huckel_checks`, [test_eos.f90:1428-1478](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/eos/test/test_eos.f90#L1428-L1478); the check is [:1456-1457](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/eos/test/test_eos.f90#L1456-L1457).
- **What is wrong:** "it raises ρ, the more with the envelope's heavier metals as Fe" asks only that the second rise exceed the first and the first be positive. The EOS package reports that it passes a mutation that gives every metal C's charge, because the base gas's 1/μ_ion moves the comparison (that mutation is not in the recorded mutation lists and was not re-run).
- **What we did:** as proposed, a new check compares the two density rises' ratio with the correction's charge-weighted factor's, to 3e-3; `mutate.py eos` catches a mutation of every `test_eos` check (67 of 67).

### M88. SCV's table edge is a step

- **Status:** fixed in round 1B ([a0039581](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/a0039581), 2026-11-12, eos item 2; measured below: 31 of the 56 decks and 13 of the 35 pins move, through the low-pressure edge, the only one a deck reaches).
- **In the original F77?** Yes. EQSTAT2 solves Saha first and then calls EQSCVE, which overwrites the result where its table covers the point and returns without touching it outside, with no weight at the edge ([eqstat2.f:150-155](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqstat2.f#L150-L155), [eqscve.f:36-39](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqscve.f#L36-L39)):
  ```fortran
        IF(TL.LT.TLOGX(1) .OR. TL.GT.TLOGX(NTS) .OR. PP.LT.4.0D0)THEN
           LCALC = .FALSE.   ! Error exit - no valid table entry
           RETURN
        ENDIF
  ```
- **Now:** `gas_eos`, [blended_eos.f90:223-260](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L223-L260), which takes SCV's result whole where `find_scv_cell` says the table covers the point ([scv_eos.f90:549-606](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/810a552c/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L549-L606)).
- **What is wrong:** outside SCV's table the Saha result stands, inside it SCV's, with no ramp between, so the EOS jumps where a model crosses the edge (the re-evaluation's "falls back without a word").
- **What we did:** round 1B (2026-11-11): SCV's table source has an edge weight, `scv_edge_weight`, and its own blend, `blend_scv_over_saha`, as OPAL's edges have (the descriptor's `edge_weight` now takes log T and the lookup's result, so that a source finds its edge in P_gas, SCV, or in ρ, OPAL). Within one table interval of each edge the weight falls linearly to 0 at it, the four edges' factors multiplied: log P_gas above the first column, 4.0, and below the cells' top at the point's T (0.2 dex each; the top is linear in log T between its values at the two rows around the point, a row's value being the highest log P_gas of the cell `find_scv_cell` uses for the interval above it, so the edge is continuous in T and never above what the lookup covers, where that steps from 11.4 to 13.6 at log T 3.70); log T above the first row and below the last (one row). Near an edge SCV's density, ionization fractions and first derivatives are blended into the Saha result, and R/μ and 1/μ_e follow from the blended density, as in the Saha ramp. `test_eos`: four new ok/FAIL checks, each caught by a mutation: every blended field is continuous at both ends of the low-pressure ramp (log P_gas 4.0 and 4.2 at log T 3.5) and of the high-pressure one (11.4 and 11.2 at log T 3.33); no pinned value moves. Measured with an instrumented build on the 56-deck set (lookups counted in each ramp): 53 decks reach the low-pressure ramp, from about 512 lookups (`m0030gs98z018804_prems`) to 2 million (`ZAHB_m1p0feh+0p0_TAHB`); none reaches the high-pressure edge or either T edge; the other three decks (the two Kurucz-atmosphere testsuite decks and the Yale-EOS one) make no SCV lookup there. A probe in seven of them found OPAL then setting or blending the density at every such point, so the ramp's density (up to 1.4e-3 dex from SCV's in `cm_base`, 0.24 dex in the 0.03 Msun deck) is OPAL's after it; its ionization fractions stay and reach the conductive opacity. 31 decks move and 13 pins (`Test_solar_noGS_norot`, the other three standard solar models, eight testsuite solar decks and `Test_m0030_feh0_noGS_ZAMS`). Outside the families that amplify, the final log L moves by 6e-14 to 1.0e-7 (`Test_solar_GS_rot_gray_OPALSCV_SF2_GS98_OP_CF10`; the others 6.3e-10 at most), with the same model counts and log P by 4.5e-7 relative at most; 22 decks that reach the ramp do not move at all. The path-sensitive decks move as much as item 5's control moved them: the testsuite by 1.2e-6 to 3.5e-5 (`Test_solarGS98_base` 822 to 821 models, `Test_solarGS98_dif` 816 to 817), the rv_ decks by 4.6e-7 to 4.8e-5 (`rv_sbm2` 923 to 898 models, `rv_gsf2` and `rv_zahn` ±1), `o24_rescale_rotating` by −5.9e-4.

## 9. Found in the third evaluation (2026-10-30)

On 2026-10-30 the five reviews of sections 7 and 8 were repeated a third time, at [6e058523](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/6e058523), after round 2, on the same scale (`audit/module-evaluation-3-2026-10-30/SUMMARY.md`; `docs/ROADMAP.md`, "Third evaluation"). Besides scoring the modules, each review listed the defects it found: bugs, tests that check less than they say, documentation a newcomer would act on wrongly, and the state of CI. These items are those defects. Each entry records what is wrong, the proposed fix and whether it would change results. Round 3 (2026-10-31/11-01, section 11) fixed M95, M98, M109, M110, M116 and M120, M113 in part, and M125 locally (its first GitHub run needs a push); their entries say how, with M95's measurement. The others are open.

- M89-M98 are the items whose fix would change results, the physics first (M95's only for multi-run Monte Carlo decks, none shipped; M98's the run log of a run that fails at an open). M99-M118 are latent defects and error paths (M103, M113 and M117 documentation of the code's behaviour, M116 the star tools), M119-M120 tests that check less than they say, M121-M124 documentation traps and M125 CI.
- **How they were checked.** M89 was checked in the code by hand when the list was drawn up; every item was read again in the code at 6e058523 and against the F77 import before its entry was written. M90's, M91's and M121's numbers were recomputed, and the cases of M99-M103 and M124 run on scratch copies of numerics/ and math/. No deck was run, so the drifts a fix would cause are not measured. Where the check corrected a review (a line, a number, a claim, where it reaches), the entry gives the corrected account and says so; no item failed the check.
- Current-code links point at [6e058523](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/tree/6e058523/src). For an item round 3 fixed, they show the code before the fix; its "What we did" says where the fix is.

### M89. The deuterium burn starts from the start-of-step X and He3, and so undoes the step's other changes to them

- **Status:** open. The net review's item; checked in the code by hand before this list was written. Results change when fixed.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. DBURN takes the region's X, D and He3 from `HCOMPP`, the composition MAIN stores at the start of the step, writes the start value plus the deuterium change, and MIX calls it last, after KEMCOM's burning, the homogenization, GRSETT's settling and the renormalization ([dburn.f:17-20](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/dburn.f#L17-L20), [:104-119](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/dburn.f#L104-L119), [main.f:560-567](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L560-L567), [mix.f:442-466](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/mix.f#L442-L466)):
  ```fortran
           X = HCOMPP(1,IBEGIN)                                ! dburn.f
           XN = X + 0.5D0*DXH2
           XHE3N = XHE3 - 1.5D0*DXH2
           HCOMP(1,I) = XN
           HCOMP(4,I) = XHE3N
  C MHP 5/02 ADDED DEUTERIUM BURNING                            ! mix.f
                 CALL DBURN(IBEGIN,IEND,M,HS2,HCOMP,DT)
  ```
- **Now:** `burn_deuterium_region`, [light_elements.f90:212-309](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/net/light_elements.f90#L212-L309) (the start-of-step reads at [:238-265](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/net/light_elements.f90#L238-L265), the writes at [:306-308](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/net/light_elements.f90#L306-L308)), called with `s%xa_start` by `burn_deuterium` ([burn_step.f90:723-743](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/step/burn_step.f90#L723-L743)), step 9 and the last of `advance_composition` ([composition_step.f90:183-186](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/step/composition_step.f90#L183-L186)); `xa_start` is stored after the mass change ([step_driver.f90:323-330](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/step/step_driver.f90#L323-L330)). The rotation sub-steps call it the same way, and their comment says so ([mid_timestep_model.f90:250-254](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/rotation/mid_timestep_model.f90#L250-L254)).
- **What is wrong:** in every burn region whose deuterium (with the accreted gas, under inflow) is at least `min_deuterium_step` = 1e-11 (1e-14 in the sub-steps), X and He3 are reset to their start-of-step values plus the deuterium change, so the step's network burning, homogenization, settling and clipping of X and He3 are lost there. Y, set before the deuterium step, keeps the network's gain, so the abundances no longer add up to 1 by the discarded change. Where it reaches:
  - the pre-main-sequence decks: the starting models carry X_D = 2.78e-5 in every shell and are fully convective, so the whole star is one region above the threshold until its deuterium burns; at T ~ 1e6 K the network changes X and He3 very little, and settling has no radiative zone to act in;
  - intermediate and high masses on and after the main sequence: the outer layers keep deuterium (the 3 Msun TAMS starting model has 30 shells hotter than log T 5.5 with X_D ≥ 1e-11, 3.5e-8 at the surface; the 10 Msun one 9.7e-8 in its outermost shell), and there settling's and the clipping's changes are lost at every step and sub-step;
  - accretion of deuterium-rich gas: the surface region stays above the threshold at every step, and a fully convective accreting star, whose one mixed region holds the centre, would lose each step's hydrogen burning. No shipped deck accretes (only the two mass-loss decks of `run_config_matrix` change the mass).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** each stage of the composition step acts on what the stage before it left. D + p → ³He removes half the deuterium burned from X and adds three halves to ³He, and changes nothing else; its change belongs on top of the burned, settled and renormalized composition.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: `burn_deuterium_region` keeps its start-of-step D and rates but applies its changes of X and He3 to the region's current composition (the mass-weighted `composition` it is given), in the main step and the sub-steps. Results change: slightly for the pre-MS decks, in the outer layers of the 3 and 10 Msun and rotating giant decks, and most under accretion; to be measured on those and on an accreting deck built to reach it.
- **Round 3 (2026-11-18):** measured in scratch (the core1 agent's B list B3, `scratch_r3_core1/patches/B_m89.patch`: `burn_deuterium_region` takes the region's X and He3 from `composition`, keeps the start-of-step D and rates): 17 of the 18 quick decks move, 16 pinned, all at round-off: no final model, log L or log Teff changes at the logs' 6 decimals; the first differences are in the 9th to 11th digit (cm_env_overshoot and Test_solar_noGS_norot: the age at model 50, 1.94776390E-03 -> 1.94776391E-03; the mass-loss decks' mass change in its 11th digit; the rotating decks' total J in its 14th; seven decks in their .mod alone). The full set was not run. The owner's choice: the fix, or the F77's behaviour stated in `burn_deuterium_region`'s header.

### M90. The screening's mixture leaves out the metals the Itoh et al. mixture counts

- **Status:** open. The net review's item; its estimate recomputed (below), not measured in a run. Results change when fixed.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. ENGEB fills the screening's isotope fractions from the tracers and sets Ne20 and Mg24 to zero ([engeb.f:409-412](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/engeb.f#L409-L412), [:424-425](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/engeb.f#L424-L425); the same in rates.f):
  ```fortran
  C  THE ABUNDANCES OF NEUTRONS, H2, H3, NE20,AND MG24, WHICH ARE,
  C  RESPECTIVELY, XFRAC(I) FOR I = 1,3,4,12,13, ARE NO LONGER USED.
        XFRAC(1) = 0.0
        XFRAC(2) = X
        XFRAC(12) = 0.0
        XFRAC(13) = 0.0
  ```
- **Now:** `screening_mass_fractions`, [network.f90:362-377](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/net/network.f90#L362-L377), which takes the network's species ([:105-113](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/net/network.f90#L105-L113)) and deuterium; the Itoh et al. mixture, [nuclear_energy.f90:76-94](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/net/nuclear_energy.f90#L76-L94), with the metals no slot holds at [:362-363](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/net/nuclear_energy.f90#L362-L363).
- **What is wrong:** the screening sees H, D, He3, He4, C12, C13, N14, O16 and O18, and nothing for N15, O17, Li, Be or the metals no slot holds (Z less its tracers), while M60's fix ([e1d89c2f](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/e1d89c2f)) made the Itoh et al. mixture count every nucleus the composition carries and those metals, as Ne20. The comment at [nuclear_energy.f90:79-80](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/net/nuclear_energy.f90#L79-L80) calls Ne20 "the screening's stand-in for the heavier metals", but the screening leaves it at zero. The review's estimate, recomputed for the solar centre (X = 0.34, Z = 0.018 in the GS98 mixture, C12 burned to N14, ρ = 150, T9 = 0.0157): the missing metals are 31% of Z by mass, z̃ comes out 1.35% low and the weak-screening exponent 1.37% low, so pp is 0.066% slow, ¹⁴N(p,γ) 0.46%, ¹²C(p,γ) 0.39% and ³He+³He 0.26% (1.5% and 0.50% on ¹⁴N(p,γ) with Z = 0.0198). Every shipped deck sets `weak_screening_threshold = 30`, so all screen weakly.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the weak-screening exponent depends on Σ Z²X/A and Σ ZX/A over every ion in the plasma; a metal leaves the screening only if it is not there.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: `screening_mass_fractions` fills `iso_ne20` with the metals that have no screening slot (Z less C12, C13, N14, O16 and O18), so that they screen as Ne20, as in the Itoh et al. mixture (M60's decision). Results change for every deck (at the solar centre about +0.07% on pp and +0.4-0.5% on the CNO rates).

### M91. The S-factor law's constant carries a CODATA 1973 Avogadro number

- **Status:** open. The net review's item (low confidence); recomputed (below). Results change when fixed.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. ENGEB's comment gives the constant, and the seven S-factor rows' Q7 all use it ([engeb.f:252](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/engeb.f#L252), [:303](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/engeb.f#L303)):
  ```fortran
  C  Q7 = 70.62860 + ((LN(Z0*Z1/A))/3) -LN(A0*A1) - LN(S SUB 0)
       6Q7/20.8964,76.6003,67.8036,69.130,70.3809,69.8517,70.8012/,
  ```
- **Now:** the seven `s_factor_fit` rows of the reaction table ([network.f90:199](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/net/network.f90#L199) to [:241](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/net/network.f90#L241)), the law `compute_s_factor_rate` ([reaction_rates.f90:322](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/net/reaction_rates.f90#L322)), the constant in its Sources ([:534](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/net/reaction_rates.f90#L534)) and the file's one Avogadro number ([:62-69](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/net/reaction_rates.f90#L62-L69)).
- **What is wrong:** 70.62860 is ln(N_A C), where C = 7.83205e6 (for S in keV b) is the non-resonant rate's numerical prefactor, built from e, ħ, k, c and m_u. With CODATA 1986's constants, those of `physical_constants`, and N_A = 1/m_u, the constant is 70.628634; 70.62860 is what CODATA 1973's give (70.628604), the vintage of `amu_cgs_legacy`. So the seven S-factor rates (pp, ³He+³He, ³He+⁴He, p+¹²C, p+¹³C, p+¹⁴N, p+¹⁶O) carry N_A = 6.021933e23, 3.4e-5 below the 1/m_u that M59's fix ([dbb5f570](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/dbb5f570)) gave every other rate, while the file says one N_A serves all of them. The same derivation reproduces the τ coefficient (4.24870) and the rows' q6, which supports the reading.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** one Avogadro number, N_A = 1/m_u, for every rate (M59's decision), so that the per-amu composition rates are ρN_A⟨σv⟩/(A₁A₂) exactly.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: add ln(6.0221367/6.021933) = 3.38e-5 to the seven q7 values, or compute the constant from `physical_constants`. Results change for every deck, at the level of M59's fix (6.9e-5 on the Caughlan & Fowler laws; the solar deck's noise floor near the ZAMS is 1e-4 in log L, `docs/ROADMAP.md`, round 2).

### M92. SCV's general path before the envelope table is built gives NaN c_P and ∇_ad

- **Status:** fixed in round 1B ([346e1af2](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/346e1af2), 2026-11-11, eos item 3; measured below: one pinned deck moves at 1e-8). The eos review's item, with an addition (the X = 0 build, below); `test_eos` runs under the devel flags past it now.
- **In the original F77?** Partly. EQSCVG has the same formula, with the mixing entropy built at the envelope's X by SETSCV ([eqscvg.f:212-217](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqscvg.f#L212-L217), [setscv.f:39-40](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/setscv.f#L39-L40)), but before SETSCV it searched `TABLENV`'s still empty column, so the point fell outside and the LOG10 was never reached ([eqscvg.f:58-59](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqscvg.f#L58-L59), [:74-83](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqscvg.f#L74-L83)):
  ```fortran
        QSMT = FTD(1)*LOG10(TEMP(1,3)) + FTD(2)*LOG10(TEMP(2,3))      ! eqscvg.f
        IF(PP.LT.TABLENV(IDT,JJJ+1,1))THEN
           LCALC = .FALSE.
              Y = 1.0D0-XENV                                          ! setscv.f
  ```
  The build moved into `eos_set_mixture` with [c00a9a20](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/c00a9a20) (2026-10-11), and M64's fix ([4a06cd08](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/4a06cd08), 2026-10-29) made the general path's lookups cover the point before a build.
- **Now:** `compute_scv_eos`'s mixing entropy and its derivative, [scv_eos.f90:489-500](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L489-L500), feeding c_P and ∇_ad ([:514-531](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L514-L531)); `smix`, a module array without an initializer ([scv_eos_tables.f90:31-33](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/scv_eos_tables.f90#L31-L33)), filled only by `build_scv_envelope_table` at the envelope's X ([scv_eos.f90:709-710](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L709-L710), [:731-763](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L731-L763)); the first card's refit before `update_surface_mixture`, [starting_model.f90:189-194](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L189-L194), whose `set_new_last_shell_convection` calls `eos_get` at [:751](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L751).
- **What is wrong:** until the envelope table is built every zone takes the general path ([scv_eos.f90:97-102](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L97-L102)), where `smix` is zero, so the stencil's log10 is −∞ and its product with the zero mixing entropy is NaN: c_P and ∇_ad come out NaN (the mixed signs of the derivative weights do not matter; 0 × ∞ is NaN alone). Under `make devel`'s `-ffpe-trap=invalid,zero,overflow` it traps. It is reached on the first card: the refit's `eos_get` (and the shallower envelope's integration, [:649](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L649)) runs before `update_surface_mixture` builds the table; and with a Z rescale on the first card, `rescale_interior_z` builds it before the refit with the X_env = 0 that M86 describes ([model_rescaling.f90:158](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/model/model_rescaling.f90#L158)), which makes `smix` zero everywhere ([scv_eos.f90:731-733](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L731-L733)) and sends every zone to the general path just the same. Where OPAL adopts the point its c_P and ∇_ad replace the NaN ([blended_eos.f90:474-475](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L474-L475)); OPAL's edge blend ([:500-503](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L500-L503)), the Saha ramp ([:430-432](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L430-L432)) and the two SCV-only decks (`testsuite/Test_m0p3feh+0p0GS98_scv_ZAMS`, `Test_m0p08feh+0p0GS98_allardscv_15Gyr`) keep it, and it reaches the new last shell's convective flag. After a build, the general path still uses the envelope's X for the mixing entropy at any zone's X (the F77's too). The test `check_scv_general_path` ([test_eos.f90:362-368](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/test/test_eos.f90#L362-L368)) compares log ρ only, and the c_P of its before-the-table result is NaN.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the general path is meant for any composition; its mixing entropy must be the zone's, and finite.
- **What we did:** round 1B (2026-11-11): `compute_scv_eos` takes the stencil's mixing entropy at the zone's X, from `scv_mixing_entropy` (SETSCV's formula at one node of the H and He tables, for a pure H/He gas of the given X), which `build_scv_envelope_table` now fills `smix` with at the envelope's X (byte-identical there); a pure gas (X = 0 or 1), whose mixing entropy is zero at every node, takes no mixing term instead of log10(0). Probed on the shipped tables: the mixing entropy is positive at every node for X from 1e-6 to 0.999999 and zero at X = 0. So the general path's c_P and ∇_ad are finite before the envelope table is built, and after it they are the zone's X's rather than the envelope's. `test_eos`: a new ok/FAIL check, caught by a mutation that reads `smix` again: before the build c_P and ∇_ad are what they are after it (both finite); its other lines do not move (no pinned value is a general-path lookup at another X). Measured on the 56-deck set and the 35 pins: one deck moves, `examples/run_from_dbl_to_zams/Test_m0030_feh0_noGS_ZAMS` (pinned): an instrumented run finds no lookup before the table's build there, and at least 262,144 general-path lookups after it at the zone's X 0.71960625 against the envelope's 0.71962 (1.4e-5 apart, past the table's 1e-5 tolerance), whose mixing entropy is now the zone's X's; its final model moves by 2.2e-8 in log L and 7.0e-9 in log Teff, its last timestep by 1.8e-6 relative, the same 52 models (log ρ by 1.0e-7 at most, P and T by 2e-8), and its log's six RHOOFP06 fallback lines by their last digits. Under the devel flags `test_eos` no longer traps here; it stops later, at its check of a fully ionized iteration started 100 dex off (M93's), where the iteration's second-order step overflows (yale_eos.f90:914, the F77's EQRELV formula), which `devel_tests.py`'s known failure then named. Round 1B capped that step (M305, [1bd927eb](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/1bd927eb)): `test_eos` runs clean under the devel flags, and its known failure is gone.

### M93. The fully ionized density iteration's failure returns success with the caller's guess

- **Status:** fixed in [4d4683ee](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/4d4683ee) (2026-11-10, round 1's eos), byte-identical on the 56 decks and 35 pins; the message's routing to the terminal is on the B list (eos item 7), and round 1 found that the iteration diverges from a fresh record (M290). The eos review's item. Latent: whether a deck reaches it is unknown (no committed output holds its message). The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. EQRELV writes a line to the run log and returns before it stores the density, with no error argument ([eqrelv.f:165-177](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqrelv.f#L165-L177)):
  ```fortran
        IF(DABS(CORR).GE.1.0D-08) THEN
         IF(NDEN.LE.20) GO TO 10
         WRITE(ISHORT,40) TL,PL,PTL,DML,CORR
         RETURN
        ENDIF
        DL = DL8
  ```
- **Now:** `iterate_fully_ionized_density`, [yale_eos.f90:765-906](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/yale/yale_eos.f90#L765-L906) (the failure at [:892-902](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/yale/yale_eos.f90#L892-L902)), and `compute_fully_ionized_eos`, [:683-704](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/yale/yale_eos.f90#L683-L704), which returns at [:694](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/yale/yale_eos.f90#L694); the Saha ramp's use, [blended_eos.f90:254-259](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L254-L259).
- **What is wrong:** after 20 iterations without convergence the message goes to the run log only and the record keeps its input log ρ (the caller's guess) and whatever density and derivatives it held (the previous call's, or zeros for a new record), with `ierr` 0 all the way up. In the Saha ramp the record starts as a copy of the Saha result, so the blend r + f(saha − r) silently becomes the Saha result. `eos_result`'s header and `eos/README.md` say every other field is overwritten.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** an EOS that did not converge says so through `eos_report` and `ierr`, as the Saha solver does; a guess is not a result.
- **What we did:** `compute_fully_ionized_eos` returns `ierr = 1` when its density iteration does not converge; the message keeps its text and the run log (its routing to the terminal is on the B list).

### M94. The OPAL 1995 EOS reads past its arrays

- **Status:** fixed in round 1B ([e6a317cf](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/e6a317cf), 2026-11-11, eos item 4; measured below: no shipped deck moves, `test_eos`'s OPAL 1995 lines do). The eos review's item, corrected (below). Latent for the decks: no deck uses OPAL 1995; `test_eos` runs it.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. ESAC's coverage sums run four X columns and, in the lowest temperature interval, to `K4 = K3 + 1` = NT + 1 ([esac.f:181](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/esac.f#L181), [:193-196](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/esac.f#L193-L196), [:209-211](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/esac.f#L209-L211)):
  ```fortran
          K4=K3+1
        DO M=MF,MF+3
          DO IR=L1,L1+3
            DO IT=K1,K1+3
              SUM33=SUM33+XZ(M,1,IT,IR)
  ```
- **Now:** `esac`, [opal95_eos.f90:287-667](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/opal/opal95_eos.f90#L287-L667): the X search ([:396-407](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/opal/opal95_eos.f90#L396-L407)) and the coverage loops ([:472-497](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/opal/opal95_eos.f90#L472-L497)); `t6rinterp`, [:678-768](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/opal/opal95_eos.f90#L678-L768); the note at [opal_eos_tables.f90:22-28](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/eos/opal_eos_tables.f90#L22-L28).
- **What is wrong:** for any X above 0.6 (the solar X included) the X search leaves the lowest index at 3, and the coverage loops read X column 6 of a table with 5 (`n_eos_mx`); the interpolation itself stops at column 5. In the lowest temperature interval the coverage sums, the interpolation and `t6rinterp` read temperature row nt + 1. A `-fcheck=all` build (`make devel`) stops at the first such lookup; a release build reads the next members. The review's "documented only" in `opal_eos_tables` holds for the X part: `docs/ROADMAP.md`'s list of inherited guards records the temperature part.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a lookup reads only its table.
- **What we did:** round 1B (2026-11-11): the 1995 interpolation clamps its stencils to its table, as the 2001 and 2006 ones do (`clamped_coverage`): `unclamped_coverage`, the emulation of the reads past the table in `stencil_entry` (now gone, the table read directly) and the T6-node line of `interpolate_opal_eos` are deleted, and with every vintage clamping, `opal_layout`'s `clamps_stencil` is read by nothing and is deleted too. Measured: `test_eos`'s OPAL 1995 lines at log T 3.70, log P 4.5 move, as round 1 measured: log ρ −7.003744496938856 to −7.003746870870781 (2.4e-6 dex), ∂ln ρ/∂ln T −1.008424198538272 to −1.008422387052862, ∂ln ρ/∂ln P 1.000766519974713 to 1.000766386687491, c_P 1.654169288215148e8 to 1.654159662638051e8 and ∇_ad 0.3879820441844603 to 0.3879857038549883 (6e-6 relative and less), through the 2.4% OPAL ramp weight there; no other line moves. On the 56-deck set and the 35 pins: byte-identical (no deck uses OPAL 1995). The `-fcheck=all` build no longer has reads past the table to emulate.

### M95. A stop threshold disarmed in one Monte Carlo run stays disarmed in the later runs

- **Status:** fixed in [ecb084fd](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/ecb084fd) (2026-10-31, round 3). Results change only for multi-run Monte Carlo decks, none shipped; measured on three (below). The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. MAIN calls PARMIN once and loops over the Monte Carlo runs; inside, each card negates a central stop the starting model is already below, and nothing re-arms it for the next run ([main.f:206](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L206), [:228](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L228), [:296-299](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L296-L299)):
  ```fortran
        CALL PARMIN
        DO 500 NN = I0,I1
           IF(LENDAG(NK))THEN
              IF(END_DCEN(NK).GT.0.0D0 .AND.
       *           HCOMP(12,1).LT.END_DCEN(NK))THEN
                 END_DCEN(NK)=-END_DCEN(NK)
  ```
  (Its X branch negated `END_DCEN` with `END_XCEN`'s value, [main.f:307](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L307), so the F77 never disarmed an X stop; the table-driven code has done it right since [366180c8](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/366180c8).)
- **Now:** `run_yrec`'s Monte Carlo loop, [run_driver.f90:153-239](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/run/run_driver.f90#L153-L239), after the one `yrec_run_prologue` ([:126](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/run/run_driver.f90#L126)); `init_stop_conditions`, [stop_conditions.f90:284-305](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/run/stop_conditions.f90#L284-L305) (the negation at [:295](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/run/stop_conditions.f90#L295)).
- **What is wrong:** each run resets the Monte Carlo parameters, the network settings and the calibration's cards, but not the central D, X and Y stops of `star%job`. A threshold negated in one run, because that run's starting model was already below it, stays negated in every later run, even when a later run's model starts above it. The review's second half holds only in part: `begin_calibration` saves `use_structure_dt_limits` at each run's start ([run_driver.f90:261-262](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/run/run_driver.f90#L261-L262)), but `end_of_card_calibration` restores it at every verdict ([:294](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/run/run_driver.f90#L294)), so a solar-calibrating run hands the next one the deck's value; without the solar calibration (or with `calibrate_star_flag` on as well) the latch carries from run to run, M31 across runs as across cards. Of the same kind: `setup_solar_calibration` multiplies `timestep_override(2)` and `(3)` by the age factor in every run, so they compound ([calibration.f90:384](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/run/calibration.f90#L384), [:386](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/run/calibration.f90#L386); SETCAL did the same, [setcal.f:50](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/setcal.f#L50), [:53](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/setcal.f#L53)), which matters when the sampled age target is not 1.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** each Monte Carlo run is the deck run again with other parameters, so it starts from the deck's stops, switches and timesteps.
- **What we did:** since round 2's controls split the values the run changes are run copies of their controls (the stops `init_stop_conditions` disarms are `card_*_stop`, the fixed timesteps `card_fixed_timestep_yr`, the latches `structure_dt_limits_active` and `mass_change_active`), and `begin_monte_carlo_run` (`core/run/monte_carlo.f90`), now the first call of every Monte Carlo run, re-arms every run copy from its control (`arm_run_copies`), derives the run range again and then applies the run's samples. Measured with three two-run decks: a solar calibration with S11 × 1.01 in run 2 (every file identical: the calibration restores the latches per cycle, and its age factor is 1); `cm_monte_carlo` with two identical samples, card 2 to 400 models and a central D stop the starting model is already below (before: run 2 inherited the structure limits run 1 switched off and the disarmed stop, took a 6.06e3 yr first step instead of 1.63e3 yr and failed in card 2, exit 1; after: exit 0, and run 2 repeats run 1 to about 1e-15 relative, M169); fixed timesteps on cards 2 and 3 and an age factor of 1.02 in both runs (before: run 2's compounded to 2.0808e6 and 5.202e7 yr; after: 2.04e6 and 5.1e7 yr, as in run 1; run 2's calibrated α 1.7139 → 1.7138, Y_init 0.26303 → 0.26302). The 56-deck set is identical; the merged code gives the package's files on all three decks.

### M96. After a later card's Z rescale, the convection zones' O16 floor keeps the first card's metals

- **Status:** fixed in round 2B (2026-11-13, core's B list item 11, with M85; its floor binds in no deck run). The state review's item; M85's sibling.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. STARIN computes `ZENVM`, Z without C, N and O, on the first card only; RSCALE changes `ZENV` and not `ZENVM`; MIXCZ floors O16 with it ([starin.f:781](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/starin.f#L781), [:804-805](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/starin.f#L804-L805), [rscale.f:80-84](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/rscale.f#L80-L84), [mixcz.f:95](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/mixcz.f#L95)):
  ```fortran
        IF(NK.GT.1) GOTO 630                                          ! starin.f
        ZENVM = ZENV*(VSUM -V(6)-V(8)-V(9))/VSUM
           HCOMP(9,I) = DMAX1(HCOMP(9,I),0.99D-3*(HCOMP(3,I)-ZENVM))  ! mixcz.f
  ```
- **Now:** `update_surface_mixture` sets `envelope_metals_no_cno` on the first card only ([starting_model.f90:958](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L958), [:978-982](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L978-L982)); `install_card_settings` ([settings_install.f90:84-96](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/setup/settings_install.f90#L84-L96), from [run_driver.f90:345](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/run/run_driver.f90#L345)) re-installs it at every card ([microphysics_settings.f90:226](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/setup/microphysics_settings.f90#L226)); the floor is in `homogenize_convection_zones`, [convection_zones.f90:537-538](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/convection/convection_zones.f90#L537-L538).
- **What is wrong:** after a later card rescales Z, the floor 0.99e-3 (Z − Z_noCNO) on O16 in the convection zones uses the first card's Z_noCNO. `testsuite/Test_m0p7feh-0p75_GN93_TAHB` rescales Z from 0.020 to 0.003 over cards 1-10 and evolves at 0.003: Z_noCNO stays 0.00536 (27% of 0.020), so from card 9 (Z = 0.004) on the floor is negative, that is off, where it should be about 2.2e-6 at Z = 0.003. The four `run_from_seed_to_start` pre-MS decks rescale Z on card 2 too, where O16 is unburned. It binds only where O16 has burned below about 7e-4 Z.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the floor is a fraction of the zone's CNO; Z_noCNO must be the current mixture's, as the EOS's mixture must (M85).
- **Recorded:** not fixed then. Proposed fix: with M85's, recompute the envelope mixture, `envelope_metals_no_cno` included, in one routine at every Z rescale. Results change only for decks with a later card's Z rescale, and only where the floor binds (not measured). It is convection's B list item 5, approved on 2026-11-11 and left for round 2, with core's M85.
- **Round 2 (2026-11-12/13):** core's B list (`audit/module-evaluation-7-2026-11-10/B_LIST_CORE.md`, item 11, with M85), measured in round 2 (scratch): M96 alone is byte-identical on the 56 decks and on the two decks run alone with a later Z rescale (its floor binds in none). Recommended with M85 in one commit.
- **What we did:** round 2B (2026-11-13), with M85: the envelope mixture's arithmetic (`update_surface_mixture`'s, AMUENV's) is one star-free kernel, model_rescaling's `compute_envelope_mixture` (Y_env, Z without C, N and O, 1/mu_ion and the number fractions, from X_env, Z_env and He3 and the controls' metal weights, in the old order, so the first card is bit for bit as before). `update_surface_mixture` calls it on the first card; `rescale_interior_z` calls it on a card after the first that rescales Z, with that card's Z and the first card's X_env and He3 (X_env stays the Yale EOS's reference, MHP 7/99), and installs the whole mixture (`install_surface_mixture_settings`: convection's Z without C, N and O, M96's floor, and the EOS mixture, M85's metals). Measured on the 56-deck set and the 35 pins against the previous commit's baseline: RESULT: 1 NOT IDENTICAL; pins 34 OK, 1 DIFF: `examples/run_standard_solar_model/Test_solarcal_noGS_norot` (.log, its pin, and .mod), the deck whose cycles' first card rescales Z to the calibrated Z/X: 442 models both, the same final age, log L -5.4e-11, log Teff -2.0e-11, final timestep 1.585122e7 to 1.585124e7 yr; its log's progress lines differ in the age alone (the first at model 250 by 5.7e-9 relative, the largest 1.9e-8 at model 300); the final profile at most 1.6e-5 in log rho and 8.5e-3 in Li7 at one zone (Be9 7.0e-3), as round 2 found. Pin re-seeded: `Test_solarcal_noGS_norot.log`. The decks of round 2's measurement, run alone again, reproduce it: `testsuite/Test_m0p7feh-0p75_GN93_TAHB` cut to 300 models on card 11 (Z 0.020 to 0.003 over cards 2-10): 300 models both, final log L +4.3e-9, log Teff -5.2e-10, age +6.7e-9 relative; history at most 1.26e-6 relative (cz_bot_mass, model 282), the final profile's O16 1.6e-3 at one zone of the convective core's edge; `examples/run_from_seed_to_start/m10000gs98z001000_prems` (Z 0.002 to 0.001 on card 2): 10 models, log L -1.7e-9, log Teff -3.1e-10. M85 carries the change; M96's floor (0.99e-3 (Z - Z_noCNO) on O16 in convection zones) binds in no deck run (round 2 measured each alone). Test: `test_model_kernels` checks `compute_envelope_mixture` on a ten-metal mixture of unequal weights (Y, the number fractions' sum, the mass fractions they give back, 1/mu_ion, Z without C, N and O), six checks, each caught by a mutation.

### M97. A Monte Carlo run's solar luminosity is 3.844e33 erg/s times its target, whatever the deck sets

- **Status:** fixed in round 2B (2026-11-13, core's B list item 13; moved `cm_monte_carlo`, below). The state review's item, checked against the F77 (below). Results change when fixed.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. MAIN's own constant scales the sampled target, while PARMIN's `CLSUN` is 3.8515e33 ([main.f:195](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L195), [:237-239](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L237-L239), [parmin.f:464](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/parmin.f#L464)):
  ```fortran
        DATA SUNAGE,SUNL/4.57D09,3.844D33/                   ! main.f
           CLSUN = SUNL*FLUM(NN)
        DATA CLSUN,CRSUN/3.8515D33,6.9598D10/                ! parmin.f
  ```
- **Now:** `apply_monte_carlo_parameters`, [monte_carlo.f90:101](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/run/monte_carlo.f90#L101), [:114-116](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/run/monte_carlo.f90#L114-L116), which overrides `run_setup`'s `s%solar_luminosity_cgs = s%ctrl%solar_luminosity_cgs` ([run_setup.f90:103](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/core/run/run_setup.f90#L103)).
- **What is wrong:** under Monte Carlo the run's L☉ is 3.844e33 times `luminosity_target`, and the deck's `solar_luminosity_cgs` (default 3.8515e33, [controls_buffer.f90:67](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6e058523/src/io/controls_buffer.f90#L67)) is ignored. With target 1 a deck at the default runs 0.195% lower than without Monte Carlo; the shipped `cm_monte_carlo` sets 3.828e33 and runs at 3.844e33, 0.42% higher. The run is consistent with itself (the convection and rotation settings take the Monte Carlo value per card), but it is a fourth source of solar units beside the three the re-evaluation counted (`audit/module-reevaluation-2026-10-29/state_setup.md`, item 9).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the sampled target scales the deck's L☉, so a deck means the same thing with and without Monte Carlo.
- **Recorded:** not fixed then. Proposed fix: `s%solar_luminosity_cgs = s%ctrl%solar_luminosity_cgs*luminosity_target`, and the constant goes. Results change for every Monte Carlo deck, `cm_monte_carlo` (in the deck set) by its 0.42% in L☉.
- **Round 2 (2026-11-12/13):** core's B list (`audit/module-evaluation-7-2026-11-10/B_LIST_CORE.md`, item 13), measured in round 2 (scratch): cm_monte_carlo's log L +1.809e-3 dex (log10(3.844/3.828)), log Teff -4.9e-7, same 12 models; its progress lines then equal cm_base's. Recommended; re-pins cm_monte_carlo.log.
- **What we did:** round 2B (2026-11-13): `apply_monte_carlo_parameters` sets the run's L☉ to the deck's (`physics%solar_luminosity_cgs`) times the sample's luminosity factor; the constant 3.844e33 erg/s (MHP 3/96) goes. Measured on the 56-deck set and the 35 pins against M293's tree: RESULT: 1 NOT IDENTICAL; pins 34 OK, 1 DIFF: `examples/run_config_matrix/cm_monte_carlo` (.log, its pin, .mod; its L☉ 3.828e33): 12 models both, the same ages and timesteps; final log L +1.809e-3 dex (log10(3.844/3.828), the unit), log Teff -4.89e-7; the final profile's L/L☉ 4.2e-3 relative (the unit's ratio), log P 1.8e-7 at the surface, the rest <= 4e-8; its two progress lines are now cm_base's to the last digit, as round 2 found. `test_run_contracts` checks a Monte-Carlo run's start with a luminosity factor of 1.01 on the deck's 3.828e33 erg/s: L☉ and log10 L☉ are the product's; the mutation back to 3.844e33 is caught (22 checks). Pin re-seeded: `cm_monte_carlo.log`.

### M98. The run log is opened after the starting and final models, so a failed open leaves no run log

- **Status:** fixed in [1a8a4155](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/1a8a4155) (2026-10-31, round 3). Results change for failing runs' logs only: every shipped and pinned log is unchanged (the 56-deck set, 35 pins). The links below show the code before the fix.
- **In the original F77?** No. PARMIN opened the run log (`ISHORT`) before the starting and final models ([parmin.f:858-859](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/parmin.f#L858-L859), [:877-879](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/parmin.f#L877-L879)):
  ```fortran
        OPEN(ISHORT,FILE=FSHORT,FORM='FORMATTED',STATUS='UNKNOWN')
           OPEN(UNIT=IFIRST,FILE=FFIRST,FORM='FORMATTED',STATUS='OLD')
        OPEN(UNIT=ILAST,FILE=FLAST,FORM='FORMATTED',STATUS='UNKNOWN')
  ```
  The order came with [2b067d75](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/2b067d75) (2026-08-22), whose MESA output mode opened the run log after the models, and [adb23da8](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/adb23da8) (2026-08-28), which made that mode the only one.
