### M271. The C entry cuts a path over 256 characters silently, and the C entry and the re-entry prologue close the host's units 7-99

- **Status:** fixed in [350c9186](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/350c9186) (2026-11-12, round 2, core agent M; the plan's C-4). The core evaluation's finding 4. Byte-identical. Left, io's: the run's `newunit` files after a C call (M312).
- **In the original F77?** No: the C entry came with [18db37b9](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/18db37b9) (2026-08-22) and the prologue's sweep with [d5798fd7](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/d5798fd7) (2026-08-21).
- **Now:** `c_string_value`, [yrec_capi.f90:71-81](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/bfb50705/src/core/run/yrec_capi.f90#L71-L81), into the 256-character overrides ([star_info_lib.f90:1239-1240](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/bfb50705/src/state/star_info_lib.f90#L1239-L1240)); `close_open_units`, [yrec_capi.f90:57-69](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/bfb50705/src/core/run/yrec_capi.f90#L57-L69), after every run; `yrec_run_prologue`'s loop, [yrec_reset.f90:47-51](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/bfb50705/src/core/run/yrec_reset.f90#L47-L51), before every run after the first.
- **What is wrong:**
  - A namelist path from C or Python (pyyrec) longer than 256 characters is cut without a word, and the run opens, or fails to open, a path the caller never named. M179 fixed the same class for the control paths.
  - Both sweeps close every open unit 7-99, so a Fortran host that keeps one of those units open across `run_yrec` calls (two calls from a program like `examples/other_energy`) has its file closed under it.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a path that does not fit is an error naming it (M179's rule); the engine closes what it opened.
- **What we did:** `yrec_run` takes the strings' addresses (`type(c_ptr)`, the `char *` ABI) and their `strlen`, and refuses a namelist path longer than the override slots (256) with status 1 before anything runs; `yrec_run` and the re-entry prologue close only the run's units by number (the run log and the final model; `yrec_reset`'s `close_run_units`). `test_run_contracts` checks a missing deck, the host's unit open across calls and re-entries, the run's units closed after a run, a 256-character path running the cm_env_overshoot deck and a 257-character one (control or physics) refused, eight checks, each caught by a mutation.

### M272. evolve_step's header says its saved locals carry state between steps alongside evolve_state; none does, and evolve_state does not exist

- **Status:** fixed in [846f34d8](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/846f34d8) (2026-11-12, round 2, core agent E; the plan's C-7), the flag deleted at the merge ([8d7feee2](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/8d7feee2)). The core evaluation's finding 7. Byte-identical.
- **In the original F77?** No: the header, the `save` with its reset block and `evolve_step_reset_pending` came with the 2026 extraction of `evolve_step` and re-entrancy ([c58da748](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/c58da748), [d5798fd7](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/d5798fd7), 2026-08-21); `evolve_state` ([d66ec03b](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/d66ec03b)) is gone.
- **Now:** the header, [step_driver.f90:46-51](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/bfb50705/src/core/step/step_driver.f90#L46-L51); the `save` and the reset of 19 locals, [:138-168](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/bfb50705/src/core/step/step_driver.f90#L138-L168); the flag, [star_info_lib.f90:1241](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/bfb50705/src/state/star_info_lib.f90#L1241), armed at [yrec_reset.f90:48](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/bfb50705/src/core/run/yrec_reset.f90#L48).
- **What is wrong:** the header says "several carry state from one step to the next (the convergence bookkeeping, the surface convection zone's base zone of the previous step) ... alongside evolve_state". Each local is assigned in the call before it is read: `new_atmosphere_fit_needed` is cleared before `change_mass` sets it and `target_envelope_mass` ([:316-322](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/bfb50705/src/core/step/step_driver.f90#L316-L322)) and only then gates the rebuild that reads it ([:210-212](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/bfb50705/src/core/step/step_driver.f90#L210-L212)); `envelope_cz_zone_prev` is set at [:396](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/bfb50705/src/core/step/step_driver.f90#L396) under the extended composition, the only case in which `burn_li_be` and rotation's sub-steps read it; the rest per the report's trace. M169's bisection likewise found that the saved locals did not matter. A reader of the header looks for cross-step state that is not there, and the reset machinery is dead.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** comments describe the code as it is now; state that does not exist needs no reset.
- **What we did:** `evolve_step`'s blanket `save`, its reset block and its use of `evolve_step_reset_pending` are gone, and its header says the locals live for the step; a poison build (every local NaN, -999999 or `.true.` at each entry) ran `--set all` byte-identical. The flag's declaration (state/star_info_lib.f90) and its arming in `yrec_reset` went in [8d7feee2](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/8d7feee2), with the locals C-8 left unused.

### M273. The shell kernel's inverse year is not its year's inverse, the structure timestep limit's ln 10 is 2.3026, and the solar calibration's card loops end at literals

- **Status:** fixed: the loops in [0c7f4a51](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/0c7f4a51) (2026-11-12, round 2, core agent M); the year's inverse and ln 10 in round 2B (2026-11-14, core's B list item 17; measured: 46 decks and 27 pins at the constants' 1e-5 size). The core evaluation's finding 10, its concrete defects (the named values are the plan's); the first number recomputed (below). Kind B for the year and ln 10 (every deck, at the 1e-5 level in ε_grav's floor and the L limit); Kind A for the loops (latent: they agree while `max_runs` = 50).
- **In the original F77?** Yes for the values ([coefft.f:97-98](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/coefft.f#L97-L98), [:264](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/coefft.f#L264), [ptime.f:96-97](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/ptime.f#L96-L97)) and for the loops, which matched SETCAL's 48 runs ([setcal.f:28](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/setcal.f#L28), [:36](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/setcal.f#L36), [:54](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/setcal.f#L54)):
  ```fortran
           TIME = 3.1558D7                                    ! coefft.f
           TIMEI = 3.1688D-8
        IF (HMAX(4)/(ATIME(11)*2.3026D0).GT.FAC) THEN         ! ptime.f
        NUMRUN = 48                                           ! setcal.f
        DO I = 4,46,3
  ```
  The count became `max_runs - 2` with [a648258c](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/a648258c) (2026-09-04); the loops kept their literals.
- **Now:** [shell_equations.f90:146-147](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/bfb50705/src/core/structure/shell_equations.f90#L146-L147), used at [:285-286](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/bfb50705/src/core/structure/shell_equations.f90#L285-L286); [timestep_control.f90:331-332](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/bfb50705/src/core/step/timestep_control.f90#L331-L332); `setup_solar_calibration`, [calibration.f90:360-364](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/bfb50705/src/core/run/calibration.f90#L360-L364), [:373](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/bfb50705/src/core/run/calibration.f90#L373), [:392](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/bfb50705/src/core/run/calibration.f90#L392), against [:402](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/bfb50705/src/core/run/calibration.f90#L402).
- **What is wrong:**
  - `one_year_sec_inv = 3.1688d-8` is not 1/`one_year_sec` = 3.16877e-8: 9.9e-6 relative (correction to the review's 7e-6). It is the 1/Δt of ε_grav in zones with X > 0.01 when the step is shorter than a year; `one_year_sec` itself is `physical_constants`' `seconds_per_year` written again.
  - The limit on the luminosity change divides by `2.3026d0` for ln 10 (2.302585...), 6.5e-6 relative.
  - The rescale and settling cards are laid out by `do i = 4,46,3` and `do i = 5,47,3`, while the card count and the solar-age cards' loop follow `num_calibration_runs = max_runs - 2`. Should `max_runs` change, the later triples keep the deck's cards, and `check_max_runs` (M192) does not read loop bounds.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** each constant once and exact (`docs/GUIDELINES.md`, "Code style" rule 2); a layout from one count.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: `seconds_per_year` and its exact inverse; `ln10`; the loops to `num_calibration_runs - 2` and `- 1`. The first two are measured commits; the loops are byte-identical.
- **Round 2 (2026-11-12/13):** the loops: `setup_solar_calibration`'s rescale and settling loops end at `num_calibration_runs-2` and `-1` ([0c7f4a51](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/0c7f4a51)), byte-identical. The year's inverse and ln 10 are on core's B list (`audit/module-evaluation-7-2026-11-10/B_LIST_CORE.md`, item 17: both in one measured commit, most pins at the 1e-6 level; not measured).
- **What we did (round 2B, 2026-11-14):** shell_equations' year and inverse year are `physical_constants`' `seconds_per_year` and `1/seconds_per_year`, and timestep_limits' L criterion divides by `physical_constants`' `ln10`. Measured on the 56-deck set and the 35 pins: 46 decks move (.log and .mod or .first), 27 pins with them; 10 decks are identical (`cm_atm_krishnaswamy`, `cm_base`, `cm_core_overshoot`, `cm_massloss_reimers`, `cm_monte_carlo`, `cm_semiconvection`, `cm_settle_he`, `cm_settle_he_z`, `cm_accretion` and `ZAHB_m1p0feh+0p0_TAHB`). The path-sensitive decks' first visible change is at their first progress line (model 50): 6.6e-6 to 1.1e-5 relative (age, dt, log L) in the 12 testsuite solar decks, the 15 `rv_` decks and `o24_rescale_rotating`, the constants' own size; their ends are the decks' amplification: the testsuite's final log L within 2.7e-5 (`Test_solarGS98_SF3`, one model more; `Test_solarGS98_kurucz` one more), the `rv_` decks' within 1.8e-5 (`rv_nobg`; `rv_sbm2` 898 to 917 models, `rv_gsf2`, `rv_nodisk` and `rv_sbm1` one fewer, `rv_zahn` one more), `o24_rescale_rotating` +1.1e-3 (its age at the model stop +7.6%). The rest, the largest change per family: the configuration matrix |d log L| 6.6e-7 (`cm_env_overshoot`; the rotating decks' ages 4.6e-6), the four standard solar decks 9.4e-6 (`Test_solar_GS_norot_gray_OPALSCV_SF2_GS98_OP_CF10`; `Test_solar_noGS_norot` +2.5e-7), the start decks 2.6e-5 (`Test_3Msolar_GS_rot_gray_OPALSCV_SF2_GS98_OP_CF10_TAMS`) but for `Test_m0030_feh0_noGS_ZAMS`, O3's 0.03 Msun deck, whose OPAL 2006 density searches fall back at other points (6 fallbacks to 15) and whose final log L moves by 4.3e-3 (age -1.5%, 52 models both). `test_timestep_limits` expects ln 10 from `log(10)` (its check fails with 2.3026, mutation `timestep-06`); no test reaches the year's floor (dt < 1 yr with X > 0.01). `test_element_diffusion`'s output does not move.

### M275. test_numerics' one-equation NaN case ran the three-equation callback past its arrays

- **Status:** fixed in [60286022](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/60286022) (2026-11-10, round 0). Test only: the pinned output is byte-identical.
- **In the original F77?** No: the test is from 2026.
- **What was wrong:** the one-equation NaN case of `test_numerics` called `bsstep` with `harmonic_derivatives`, which reads `y(2)` and writes `dydx(2)` and `dydx(3)`; `bsstep`'s midpoint step passes one-element arrays, so the release test read and wrote past them on the stack. Round 0's devel build (`-fcheck=all`) stopped there: "Index '2' of dimension 1 of array 'y' above upper bound of 1".
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a callback works on the components its call has.
- **What we did:** `harmonic_derivatives` works on `size(y)` components (the rotation on two, the decay on the third; a one-component call has dy1/dx = 0 before its NaN). Three-component calls compute what they did, and `mutate.py numerics` still catches 71 of 71.

### M276. check_boundaries and four generators failed under `python3 -I`

- **Status:** fixed in [b0cc5321](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/b0cc5321) (check_boundaries) and [995e7888](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/995e7888) (the generators), 2026-11-10, round 0. Tools only.
- **In the original F77?** No: Python tools of 2026.
- **What was wrong:** `src/tools/check_boundaries.py` imports `check_star_contracts`, and gen_controls_state.py, gen_inlist.py, gen_controls_dump.py and gen_star_docs.py import sibling modules; `python3 -I` leaves the script's directory off `sys.path`, so each stopped with ModuleNotFoundError. CI runs them without `-I` and was not affected.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the checks run the same way however they are started; the project's own rule runs Python over the tree with `-I`.
- **What we did:** each script puts its own directory on `sys.path` before its sibling imports. The generators' `--check` output is unchanged; `make check` runs every checker under `-I`.

## 15. Found in round 1 (2026-11-10)

Round 1 of the seventh evaluation's plan (`audit/module-evaluation-7-2026-11-10/PLAN.md`) brought kap, atm, convection, element_diffusion and eos to the plan's standard, one package agent each, with byte-identical commits only; yrec-next merged the five branches in [d942e2f3](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/d942e2f3) (convection), [50958b1c](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/50958b1c) (element_diffusion), [42abf994](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/42abf994) (kap), [7c259740](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/7c259740) (atm) and [2c9a6ec4](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/2c9a6ec4) (eos). Besides the 42 older items the round fixed (section 1's summary gives each its commit), the agents' hand-backs listed the new defects they found, and the round's integrator found four more. These items are those defects, in the order of the round's packages: kap (M277-M282), atm (M283, M284), convection (M285, M286), element_diffusion (M287-M289), eos (M290-M293), then the integrator's (M294-M297). M281, M282 and M297 were fixed in the round; the rest are open. Round 1B (2026-11-11/12) then fixed M277, M283, M285 and M290-M292 from the B lists; each entry's status gives its commit. Each entry records what is wrong, the proposed fix and its kind, as the plan uses the word (A, byte-identical on every deck and pin; B, a change of results or of pinned text), and, where one carries it, the item of the round's B lists: the measured fixes, one list per package, that wait for the owner's approval (PLAN.md section 7).

- **How they were checked.** Each was found by an agent in its own package and checked again for its entry: the lines in the code at 2c9a6ec4, the F77 at 6cd56739. The numbers are the agents' measurements where an entry gives them; no B fix was run for this registration.
- **Not entered here.** A find that belongs to an older entry is in that entry: M225's second X node, M241 (not latent: a shipped sample stops), M247 (its fix moves a pinned deck), M234's handling of the all −999 row, and the description M239's fix left stale. Not entered at all: the round's own slips, caught before the merges (an SCV array constructor that stopped `-fcheck=all`, fixed in [b8172f3f](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/b8172f3f); an internal name that tripped M295's checker, renamed before atm's merge); and semiconvection's search at one radius (convection's hand-back), which enters only the mixing-length cubic, so no result depends on it, and which the agent kept and documented.
- Current-code links point at [2c9a6ec4](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/tree/2c9a6ec4/src).

### M277. OPAL95's high-R density shift looks for each row's last filled column in the Z = 0 table, whatever the run's Z

- **Status:** fixed in round 1B ([758819a0](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/758819a0), 2026-11-11, kap item 7; measured below: no shipped deck moves). Found by round 1's kap agent (hand-back §5, item 1), checked in the code. It acts only on stencils near the tables' empty high-R corner at a Z far from 0. Kind B, size S (one array name).
- **In the original F77?** Yes. GETOPAL95 tests the fixed-Z table `CAPPA` and searches the full set's `CAPPA2` ([getopal95.f:163-165](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/getopal95.f#L163-L165)):
  ```fortran
            IF(CAPPA(IXX,ITT,IDD+3).GT.9.9D0)THEN
               DO J = IDD+2,1,-1
                  IF(CAPPA2(IXX,ITT,J).LE.9.9D0)THEN
  ```
- **Now:** `compute_opal95_opacity`, the test at [opal95_opacity.f90:365-366](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/kap/opal95/opal95_opacity.f90#L365-L366) and the search at [:367-368](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/kap/opal95/opal95_opacity.f90#L367-L368).
- **What is wrong:** for each of the stencil's four T rows, when the fixed-Z table `tbl%fixed_z_opacity` has no value at the stencil's top log R column, the loop looks for the row's last filled column in `tbl%full_opacity(x_table_index, ...)`, the full table set's slot for X index `x_table_index` at Z = 0, and shifts the stencil there. So the empty corner is taken from the Z = 0 table whatever Z the fixed-Z table was built at; where the two tables' corners differ, the stencil ends at the wrong column.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the search reads the table it tests, which is the table the interpolation then uses.
- **What we did:** round 1B (2026-11-11): the search reads `tbl%fixed_z_opacity`, the table tested and interpolated. Measured on the 56-deck set and the 35 pins: byte-identical, as the tables predict. In every shipped OPAL 1995-format table but one the empty corner is the same in every table of the file (the reader's shorter rows from log T 7.2 on, and in the AAG21, Lodders and Magg22 tables the 9.999 rows at log T 8.1-8.7 too), so the Z = 0 slot and the fixed-Z table have the same last filled column. The exception, `op05/GS98alpha02.OP17`, which no shipped deck uses, has corners that differ by X and, at X = 0.2 and 0.35, by Z (its Z = 0.1 tables are one column narrower). No `test_kap` check: only that table shows the difference, and the shift's tests read the X stencil's first index left by the previous lookup (the X stencil is located after the shift; the F77's `JX(1,1)` too), which no shipped table's corner depends on (M298).

### M278. The conductive opacity weights each species by its ionized number fraction without normalizing, so a less ionized mixture conducts better

- **Status:** fixed in round 2B (2026-11-14), option B, the owner's decision of 2026-11-13 (core's B list item 28; kap's code). Measured: every one of the 56 decks and 25 of the 35 pins move; the ZAHB deck's run 2.6% shorter (within the limits the owner set before adoption: 6% in age, 15% in models). Found by round 1's kap agent (hand-back §5); researched in round 1B (below).
- **In the original F77?** Yes: CONDOPACPINT (LLP's, 5/31/04) has the same weights and sum ([condopacpint.f:32-34](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/condopacpint.f#L32-L34), [:57](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/condopacpint.f#L57)):
  ```fortran
         WtH1 = WtH1Base * FXION(1) ! (FXION(1)/1D0 is the fraction
         WtHe4 = WtHe4Base * (FXION(2) + 2D0*FXION(3))/2D0
             CONDL = -LOG10(WtH1*CONDX + WtHe4*CONDY + WtOx*CONDZ)
  ```
- **Now:** `compute_conductive_opacity`, the weights at [conductive_opacity.f90:110-112](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/kap/conductive/conductive_opacity.f90#L110-L112) and the mixture at [:143-144](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/kap/conductive/conductive_opacity.f90#L143-L144).
- **What is wrong:** the mixture combines the species' conductive opacities harmonically with weights that are each species' number fraction times its ionized fraction, not normalized. As the ionization falls the weights fall with it, and the mixture's conductive opacity drops: at log T 7.3 and log ρ 4.5, κ_c is 0.137 fully ionized and 0.0013 with `ion_fraction` = 0. Neutral atoms should not conduct; the formula ignores that the electron density falls with the ionization.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** fewer free electrons conduct less, not more; the weights should follow the published mixing rule the routine implements, which round 1 did not check (round 1B did: below).
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. A decision for the owner: renormalize the weights, or weight by the electrons each species gives. The rule is to be checked first, then the change measured, next to M222's.
- **Round 1B's research (2026-11-11, kap's hand-back §4; no commit):**
  - **The source and its rule.** The routine is LLP's CONDOPACPINT (5/31/04), "based on Chris Burke's conductive opacity code and calling Potekhin code and table": Potekhin's conductivities (Potekhin, Baiko, Haensel & Yakovlev 1999, A&A 346, 345; Potekhin 1999, A&A 351, 787). Potekhin et al. (1999), §3.3's last paragraphs, give the rule for a mixture of ions: Z²n_iΛ_ei becomes Σ_j Z_j²n_jΛ_ej in the electron-ion collision frequency, and the mean-ion approximation "can be used also in the regime of partial ionization"; Cassisi et al. (2007, ApJ 661, 1094, §2) use the same. For tables of pure species it reads 1/K_mix = Σ_j x_j/K_j(n_e), with x_j = Z_j n_j/n_e the electron fractions (Σ x_j = 1) and each K_j at the mixture's electron density. The F77's earlier formula, kept as a comment (kap/retired/conductive_opacity.f90.txt: K = ((1+X)/2)/(X/K_H + Y/(2K_He) + Z/(2K_Z))), is these weights for a fully ionized mixture, with the K_j at the mixture's ρ.
  - **Does the code follow it?** No. Its weights n_j f_j (number fraction times ionized fraction) (a) lack the charge Z_j and the normalization by n_e, so in a fully ionized mixture H takes its number fraction where the rule gives its electron fraction, and He and the metals are underweighted by about 2 and 8; (b) sum to less than 1 in a partly ionized gas, so the mixture conducts better as the ionization falls (this entry's symptom); and (c) read each K_j at the mixture's mass density, which is the pure species' own electron density, not the mixture's.
  - **Recommendation (B):** x_j = Z̄_j n_j/Σ_k Z̄_k n_k with the mean-ion charges from the EOS's `ion_fraction` (Z̄_H = f(H⁺), Z̄_He = f(He⁺) + 2f(He⁺⁺), Z̄_O = 8), and each K_j looked up at log ρ_j = log ρ + log10((A_j/Z_j) Σ_k X_k Z̄_k/A_k) (A/Z = 1, 2, 2 for the table's isotopes), clamped to the table; the derivatives keep their form. The minimal alternative (A) changes the weights alone; A and B agree in helium cores. The branch below log ρ = −6 takes the same weights. About 15 lines in `compute_conductive_opacity`; `test_kap`'s "Potekhin mixture" check, which pins today's weights, changes with it.
  - **Expected effect, measured in scratch** (the work directory's `scratch_b_kap/m278/` and its control tree, against kap's final base). κ_c at representative points: the solar centre +8.8% (A +8.3%), r ≈ 0.25 R☉ +5.7%, the base of the convection zone +4%, a degenerate helium core +3.4% (A = B), a ZAHB core +1.6%, a half-ionized helium core ×1.9 (A ×1.4), the photosphere ×600, where conduction stays negligible. On the 56 decks every deck and all 35 pins move: the pre-main-sequence decks by |Δ log L| ≤ 4e-11 (the 0.03 Msun ZAMS deck 5e-9); the solar models at 4.568 Gyr (B) by −1.5e-5 to −1.8e-5 (`Test_solar_noGS_norot` −1.66e-5, log Teff −1.3e-6, X by up to 1.0e-5 in any zone; the calibration −6.1e-6 after recalibrating), the 1 Msun ZAMS deck −1.2e-5, the 3 Msun TAMS deck −1.3e-5, 10 Msun −7e-8 (A within 10% of these): the linear response, since a control with κ_c × 1.001 moves `Test_solar_noGS_norot` by −3.2e-7; the path-sensitive decks by 1e-6 to 2e-3 with their usual ±1 model. `ZAHB_m1p0feh+0p0_TAHB`'s run lasted 3.7% longer (0.2302 to 0.2386 Gyr; A 5.5%), 1516 to 1649 models (A 1723), ending at log L +0.029: not the linear response (the 1.001 control lengthened it by 4.9e-6 relative) but a change of its late core-mixing history, which the owner should look at before adopting the rule.
  - **The ZAHB numbers are to be measured again.** They were taken on kap's base, before convection's M285 fix and the rezone's overshoot base (f80adb7b, 4cf4e0ac) changed that deck's core mixing: its baseline is now 1865 models, not 1516. Neither change moved another deck, so the other numbers stand.
- **Round 2 (2026-11-12/13):** core's B list (`audit/module-evaluation-7-2026-11-10/B_LIST_CORE.md`, item 28) carries the question to the owner again.
- **The owner's decision (2026-11-13):** option B (core's B list item 28): each species weighted by its share of the electrons, each table read at its own density. The fix is the next core agent's item of round 2B, so the entry stays open until it lands; the ZAHB trial is to be measured again on that tree.
- **What we did (round 2B, 2026-11-14):** `compute_conductive_opacity` follows Potekhin et al.'s rule (option B): 1/K = Σ xⱼ/Kⱼ(ρⱼ), xⱼ = Z̄ⱼnⱼ/Σₖ Z̄ₖnₖ with Z̄ = f(H⁺), f(He⁺) + 2f(He⁺⁺) and 8, and each Kⱼ read at log ρⱼ = log ρ + log10((Aⱼ/Zⱼ) Σₖ Xₖ Z̄ₖ/Aₖ) (A/Z = 1, 2, 2), clamped to the table; the derivatives keep their form. Below the table's lowest density the lookups take the shifted densities of the lowest one, so that κ_c stays continuous at log ρ = −6 (test_kap's continuity check; the round 1B trial had left them unshifted, which moves no compared deck's file but broke continuity by 3.4e-7). The trailing comment of M300 goes with the old weights.
  - **ZAHB first (the owner's condition):** on today's base (after round 2B's other items; M273 does not move this deck), `ZAHB_m1p0feh+0p0_TAHB` with option B: 1865 to 1726 models (−7.45%), final age 0.249705 to 0.243117 Gyr (−2.64%), final log L −0.0253, log Teff +4.6e-4; its first visible change is at model 0 (1.9e-6 in log L and log R). The run now ends shorter, where round 1B's trial on the older base (1516 models, before M285's merge) ran 3.7% longer: the trial's direction followed that base's core-mixing history. Within the limits (6% in age, 15% in models), so committed.
  - **The 56 decks and the 35 pins:** every deck moves, 25 pins with them (`cmp_09_m278.log` in the work directory's scratch). The solar models at 4.57 Gyr: `Test_solar_noGS_norot` log L −1.66e-5 (round 1B's trial: −1.66e-5), log Teff −1.3e-6; the gray OPAL/SCV decks −1.58e-5 and (rotating) −1.77e-5; the calibration −6.1e-6. The testsuite's solar decks −2.4e-6 to −6.1e-5 in final log L (`Test_solarGS98_dif`), `Test_solarGS98_base` one model more and `_kurucz` one fewer; the `rv_` decks −2.3e-6 to −2.2e-5 (`rv_sbm2` 917 to 901 models; `rv_gsf2`, `rv_nodisk` and `rv_notrans` one more), `o24_rescale_rotating` −3.0e-4 (age −1.9%); the path-sensitive decks' first visible change at model 50-150, 1.3e-9 to 1.5e-8 in age (`Test_solarGS98_dif` 3.8e-6 at model 150). The pre-main-sequence decks within 1e-10 (`cm_env_overshoot`, which runs to 1e7 yr, −1.3e-6); the 1 and 3 Msun start decks −1.2e-5, the 10 Msun −7e-8, the 0.03 Msun 1.6e-8.
  - **Tests:** test_kap's mixture check takes the rule (1/K = Σ xᵢ/Kᵢ(ρᵢ) against pure, fully ionized species at their own densities, 6.7e-16), with three mutations (the He charge, the normalization, the electrons per mass unit); its seven grid points where conduction acts and its continuity and derivative lines re-pinned. test_structure's three pins (qt and its partials at the TAMS deck's centre and middle shells, two derivative lines of the Yale case) and test_envelope_integration's retry line (the starting optical depth at a density of 1e-2 g/cm³, 6.2 to 8.4 past the photosphere's) re-pinned; `test_element_diffusion` passes unchanged.

### M279. Two shipped opacity data defects: an empty OPAL 1992 table, and 14 Kurucz 1990 tables with a third header line

- **Status:** open (data). Found by round 1's kap agent (hand-back §5, item 6). Since round 1 both are read safely: `kap_init` refuses the empty table (M220, [53164594](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/53164594)), and the Kurucz reader skips unreadable lines only before the first row (M229, [28e1298a](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/28e1298a)). No shipped deck uses OPAL 1992 or Kurucz 1990. Kind A. Not on the B lists.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: the import holds the same files, the OPAL 1992 one empty ([input/opacity/opal92/z01947.opaln](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/input/opacity/opal92/z01947.opaln), 0 bytes; [input/opacity/kurmol/](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/tree/6cd56739/input/opacity/kurmol)), and SETKRZ read on past a record it could not parse ([setkrz.f:51-63](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/setkrz.f#L51-L63), M229).
- **Now:** [input/opacity/atomic/legacy/opal92/z01947.opaln](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/input/opacity/atomic/legacy/opal92/z01947.opaln) (0 bytes) and the 33 tables of [input/opacity/molecular/legacy/kurmol/](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/tree/2c9a6ec4/input/opacity/molecular/legacy/kurmol); the readers, [opal92_reader.f90:54](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/kap/opal92/opal92_reader.f90#L54) and [kurucz_reader.f90:89](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/kap/kurucz90/kurucz_reader.f90#L89).
- **What is wrong:** `z01947.opaln`, the OPAL 1992 table at Z = 0.01947, is empty: before M220 a deck that named it read no table and `kap_init` returned success. Of the 33 Kurucz 1990 tables, 14 have three header lines where the reader skipped two; the third was skipped as an unreadable row, without a word (M229).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a shipped table is usable, or it is not shipped.
- **What we did:** recorded. The readers handle both since round 1, and the Kurucz reader's header says that some tables have three header lines. Proposed: restore `z01947.opaln` from its source, or remove it.

### M280. LAOL89's derivatives are secants of the table's knots, 6% off the derivatives of the interpolated κ

- **Status:** open (documented). Found by round 1's kap agent (hand-back §5, item 7). No shipped deck uses LAOL89. Kind B if changed (the Jacobian of LAOL89 decks). Not on the B lists (the kap round: a B item if wanted).
- **In the original F77?** Yes: GTLAOL takes the secants of the bracketing knots ([gtlaol.f:97-98](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/gtlaol.f#L97-L98), [:111-114](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/gtlaol.f#L111-L114)):
  ```fortran
              DODTX(NUMXS) = (TOP1(KHI)-TOP1(KLO))/(TT(KHI)-TT(KLO))
           QOT = DODTX(1) + SLOPE*(X-XX(1))
  ```
- **Now:** `laol_column_opacity`, [laol_opacity.f90:285-374](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/kap/laol89/laol_opacity.f90#L285-L374), whose header says so ([:277-281](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/kap/laol89/laol_opacity.f90#L277-L281)); `test_kap`'s check, [test_kap.f90:427](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/kap/test/test_kap.f90#L427).
- **What is wrong:** κ is a spline through the knots, but d ln κ/d ln T and d ln κ/d ln ρ are the secants of the knots around the point, not the derivatives of that spline: at `test_kap`'s point they differ by 6%, and the check compares them with differences to 10%.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the derivatives are the interpolant's, so that the Jacobian matches the residual (O1's reasoning).
- **What we did:** documented in the routine's header and checked to 10% in round 1. Proposed, if wanted: the splines' own derivatives, a measured change for LAOL89 decks.

### M281. kap's warm-start search indices outlived kap_init, so a second run's derivatives at a grid node differed from the first's

- **Status:** fixed in [ece48592](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/ece48592) (2026-11-10, round 1's kap). Found by the kap agent (hand-back §5, item 4). Byte-identical: each deck calls `kap_init` once per process.
- **In the original F77?** No: a second `kap_init` in one process came with the 2026 re-entrant `run_yrec` (M219's second case is of the same kind).
- **What was wrong:** the lookups' warm-start search indices were module state that `kap_init` did not reset, so a second run in one process started its searches where the first had ended. At an exact grid node the bracket depends on the start, and the derivative with it: d ln κ/d ln T at log T 3.70 was 1.794 in the second run, 1.941 in the first.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a second run in one process is the first run again (`test_reentry`, pyyrec).
- **What we did:** the tables are one instance private to kap_lib, beside a never-written copy of their initial state, and `kap_init` starts from that copy ([kap_lib.f90:60](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/kap/kap_lib.f90#L60), [:255](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/kap/kap_lib.f90#L255)).

### M282. The surface-table refresh built Alexander 1994's table whenever its switch was on, also with Alexander 2006 in use and the 1994 tables unread

- **Status:** fixed in [1987136a](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/1987136a) (2026-11-10, round 1's kap), with the families' precedence list. Found by the kap agent (hand-back §5, item 5). Byte-identical: the lookups took Alexander 2006 first, so nothing read the table.
- **In the original F77?** No. SURFOPAC also tested `LALEX95` alone, but PARMIN turned it off when `LALEX06` was set ([surfopac.f:32-34](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/surfopac.f#L32-L34), [parmin.f:832-835](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/parmin.f#L832-L835)):
  ```fortran
        IF(LALEX06)THEN
           LALEX95 = .FALSE.
  ```
- **Before the fix:** `refresh_surface_tables`, [kap_lib.f90:549-564](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/916ee23a/src/kap/kap_lib.f90#L549-L564), against the load's and the lookup's `else if (kap_settings%use_alex95_tables)` ([:533](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/916ee23a/src/kap/kap_lib.f90#L533), [:141](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/916ee23a/src/kap/kap_lib.f90#L141)).
- **What was wrong:** with both `use_alex06_tables` and `use_alex95_tables` set, the load read only Alexander 2006 and the lookup used only it, but the refresh at every change of the envelope X built Alexander 1994's surface table from the unread (zero) 1994 tables.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a family's state is built only when the family is in use, as one precedence list decides for the load, the refresh and the lookup alike.
- **What we did:** the families are `kap_source` descriptors in one precedence list (`opacity_families`); the load, the refresh and the lookup take the first selected family of each role.

### M283. atm_init keeps the tables a previous run in the same process read

- **Status:** fixed in round 1B ([67cd7815](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/67cd7815), 2026-11-11, atm item 5; measured below: no shipped deck moves). Found by round 1's atm agent (hand-back §4, item 6), checked in the code. Latent for the shipped decks (one run per process); it matters for two-run processes such as `test_reentry` and pyyrec, and more with O19's fix, under which accretion asks whether the Allard tables are loaded (an Allard run, then an accreting gray run, would find them loaded). Kind A for the decks, none of which moves; size S.
- **In the original F77?** No: the F77 read its tables once per process; a second `atm_init` came with the 2026 re-entrant `run_yrec`.
- **Now:** `atm_init`, [atm_lib.f90:73-97](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/atm/atm_lib.f90#L73-L97), which reads the selected choice's tables only ([:88-95](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/atm/atm_lib.f90#L88-L95)); the loaded flag a lookup tests, [:153-154](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/atm/atm_lib.f90#L153-L154).
- **What is wrong:** `atm_init` reads the tables of the deck's choice and resets none of the others, so a second run in one process finds the first run's tables still loaded.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** each run starts from a clean state, as `kap_init` does since round 1 (M281).
- **What we did:** round 1B (2026-11-11): after the choice check, `atm_init` returns the three tables to their unread state, their types' defaults (not loaded; the Allard tables' limits 0), and then reads its choice's, as `kap_init` starts from `initial_tables` (M281). Measured on the 56-deck set and the 35 pins: byte-identical (one `atm_init` per run). `test_atm` checks it (Allard, Kurucz, Castelli/Kurucz and Allard again read in turn: after each, the table read before is not loaded), with two mutations (the surface-pressure tables' reset, the Allard tables'); its other checks now read the Allard tables their switch checks use.

### M284. Shipped Kurucz atmosphere tables hold rows the lookup cannot interpolate

- **Status:** open (data). Found by round 1's atm agent (hand-back §5, items 2 and 3). Since M234's fix ([18c56741](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/18c56741)) the lookup refuses such a stencil with `ierr` 1, where it read −999 entries or past the row. No shipped deck uses these tables (the 12 Kurucz decks use `atmk1990p00.tab`, whose rows are complete). Kind A. Not on the B lists.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: the import holds the same tables ([input/atmos/kurucz/](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/tree/6cd56739/input/atmos/kurucz)), and SURFP's search read their rows as they are ([surfp.f:84-87](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/surfp.f#L84-L87), M234).
- **Now:** [input/atmos/kurucz/](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/tree/2c9a6ec4/input/atmos/kurucz); the refusal, as `interpolate_surface_pressure`'s header states it, [kurucz_atmosphere.f90:43-49](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/atm/tables/kurucz_atmosphere.f90#L43-L49).
- **What is wrong:**
  - `atmk1990p01.tab`'s row 29 (log Teff 4.041) is −999 throughout: the F77's search, and the port before M234, read columns 11-14 of 11 for a stencil on it.
  - In `atmk1990m23.tab` to `atmk1990m50.tab` the cool rows (1-6) end below log g 5.0 (their last valid column is 9 or 10); before M234 a log g above such a row's second-to-last valid column fell to the row's low end or read −999 entries.
  - Several tables from `atmk1990p012.tab` to `atmk1990p10.tab` have rows 47-57 (log Teff 4.4-4.6) with fewer than four valid columns, which in the spline branch (log Teff ≤ 4.5) the F77 interpolated through −999.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a shipped table holds the values its lookup needs over the range it covers, or its documentation says where it does not.
- **What we did:** recorded. The lookup refuses these points since M234; the tables are as shipped. Proposed: say in atm/README which tables have holes and where, or fill them from the source models.

### M285. The overshoot merge can shrink a region: the merged region ends at the upper region's top even when the lower one reached higher

- **Status:** fixed in round 1B ([f80adb7b](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/f80adb7b), 2026-11-11, convection item 7; measured below). Found by round 1's convection agent (hand-back §5, item 2), checked in the code. Not latent, as round 1B found: `examples/run_from_zahb_to_tahb/ZAHB_m1p0feh+0p0_TAHB` (in the 56-deck set, unpinned) reaches it in 234 of its 330 overshoot merges, from the first, and the other horizontal-branch decks with core overshoot (about 75, in `examples/run_from_zahb_to_tahb`, `sample_cases/LowM_HB` and `sample_cases/TAHB`) likely do too; the B list's "no deck is known to reach it" was wrong. Kind B, size S. Since the union lengthens that deck's core helium burning by 9.8%, the fix goes to the owner to confirm (keep it, or restore the F77's merge).
- **In the original F77?** Yes: CONVEC's merge gives the merged region the lower region's bottom and keeps the upper region's top ([convec.f:129-141](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/convec.f#L129-L141)):
  ```fortran
        IF(MXZONE(J,2).GE.MXZONE(J+1,1))THEN
           MXZONE(J+1,1) = MXZONE(J,1)
  ```
- **Now:** `merge_overlapping_zones`, [convection_zones.f90:211-239](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/convection/convection_zones.f90#L211-L239), the merge at [:228](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/convection/convection_zones.f90#L228).
- **What is wrong:** when region k's top, with its overshoot, reaches region k+1, the merged region runs from region k's first shell to region k+1's last (`bounds(k+1,1) = bounds(k,1)`, then the rows above move down). If region k reached past region k+1's top, as a core whose overshoot covers an intermediate zone entirely does, the shells between the two tops leave the mixed region.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a merge is the union of the two regions.
- **What we did:** round 1B (2026-11-11): `merge_overlapping_zones` gives the merged region region k's first shell and the higher of the two last shells, `max(bounds(k,2), bounds(k+1,2))`, before the rows above move down, for both causes (overshoot and semiconvection); `log_zones_merged` prints that merged region (the caller passes it). Measured on the 56-deck set and the 35 pins: one deck moved, `ZAHB_m1p0feh+0p0_TAHB` (no pin). Its old run made 330 overshoot merges, 234 of them with the core's overshoot reaching 1 to 20 shells past a small convective shell's top just above it (the log printed those indices as `***`, M254), shells the old merge left out of the mixed core; the first is the run's first merge (`[1-2303]` with `[2298-2299]`, which became `[1-2299]`), and the two runs' logs agree up to it. With the union the mixed core keeps those shells, the run takes an extra breathing pulse or two, and core helium lasts longer: the run reaches central Y < 1e-4 at model 1917 instead of 1517, at 0.2527 Gyr instead of 0.2302 (+9.8%), final log L +7.8e-2 and log Teff −1.9e-3; matched by model number, log L agrees within 1.2e-4 at model 50, 4.1e-3 at 200 and 1e-2 at 400, and the pulses then shift. (atm's 3e-9 dex control moved this deck by one model and 5.7e-4 in final log L.) No other deck moved; the two UpperMS semiconvection samples (shortened copies) give identical files. The next convection commits moved the same deck again: the rezone's overshoot base in radius ([4cf4e0ac](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/4cf4e0ac), the plan's CD-14 part B) took it from 1917 to 1865 models (0.2527 to 0.2497 Gyr, core helium 1.2% shorter; a mesh control, a zoning tolerance times 1.00005, keeps 1917 models and log L within 2e-6), so its baseline is now 1865 models. `test_convection` checks it: a core [1, 5] whose overshoot reaches shell 10 merges with an intermediate zone [7, 8] into [1, 10], where the old merge gave [1, 8] (the new check "overshoot merge: the union, the lower region reaching higher (M285)", caught by a mutation that restores the upper region's top); its pin gains the case's lines.
- **Round 2 (2026-11-12/13):** core's B list (`audit/module-evaluation-7-2026-11-10/B_LIST_CORE.md`, item 29) carries the question to the owner again; keeping the fix recommended.
- **The owner's decision (2026-11-13):** keep the merged fix (core's B list item 29, its recommendation): the union of the two regions is what a merge means; `ZAHB_m1p0feh+0p0_TAHB`'s longer core helium burning stands.

### M286. homogenize_convection_zones mixes a central run of one shell that find_convection_zones does not count as a zone

- **Status:** open (noted; no fix proposed). Found by round 1's convection agent (hand-back §5, item 3), checked in the code. A no-op but for rounding: the mix of one shell is Σ(x dm)/Σ dm over that shell. Kind B if changed (shell 1's composition at round-off). Not on the B lists.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: CONVEC records a run only when it is longer than one shell, and MIXCZ mixes a run of one at the centre ([convec.f:67-71](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/convec.f#L67-L71), [mixcz.f:69](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/mixcz.f#L69)):
  ```fortran
           IF(I1.NE.I-1)THEN                                    ! convec.f
    903    IF(I1.NE.1 .AND. I1.GE.I2) GOTO 100                  ! mixcz.f
  ```
- **Now:** `homogenize_convection_zones`' test, [convection_zones.f90:299](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/convection/convection_zones.f90#L299), against the zone list's, [:190](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/convection/convection_zones.f90#L190).
- **What is wrong:** the two scans disagree about a convective centre shell with a radiative shell above it: the homogenization mixes it, and the zone list has no zone there. The mix changes nothing but rounding.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** one rule for what a zone is, as the one scan since M248's fix would allow.
- **What we did:** recorded only. If changed: skip the one-shell run in both, a change at round-off.

### M287. The settling grids get one point too few, so their intervals are wider than the narrowest zone

- **Status:** open; B list: element_diffusion item 8 (a decision; recommended: one more point). Found by round 1's element_diffusion agent (hand-back §5, item 1), checked in the code. Every settling deck runs it, so the fix moves every settling deck at the grid's resolution (not measured). Kind B.
- **In the original F77?** Yes, in both pipelines' grid builders ([microdiff_mte.f:32-35](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/microdiff_mte.f#L32-L35), [model_to_equal.f:28-31](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/model_to_equal.f#L28-L31)):
  ```fortran
  C  ASSIGN THE MINIMUM NUMBER OF EQUALLY SPACED GRID POINTS SUCH THAT
  C  DR <= DRMIN.
        NPT=INT(DRTOT/DRMIN)
        IF(MOD(DRTOT,DRMIN).NE.0.0D0)NPT=NPT+1
  ```
- **Now:** `size_equal_grid`, [diffusion_grid.f90:59-78](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/element_diffusion/diffusion_grid.f90#L59-L78) (the count at [:73-75](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/element_diffusion/diffusion_grid.f90#L73-L75)), whose header says so since round 1 ([:55-58](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/element_diffusion/diffusion_grid.f90#L55-L58)).
- **What is wrong:** ⌈span/narrowest⌉ is the number of intervals that "DR ≤ DRMIN" needs, but it is used as the number of points, so the grid has one interval fewer than meant and its spacing, span/(n − 1), is wider than the narrowest zone by n/(n − 1).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the grid the comment describes: no interval wider than the narrowest zone of the span.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed (the code's header now says so). Proposed fix: one more point, in one measured commit with the single-precision 2.2 (M257; B list: element_diffusion item 9).

### M288. The original settling routines never solve the metals' implicit diffusion term

- **Status:** open; B list: element_diffusion item 1, with M243-M246 (a decision; recommended: retire the routines). Found by round 1's element_diffusion agent (hand-back §5, item 2), checked in the code. No shipped deck selects the original routines (0 of 354 settling decks), so only `test_element_diffusion`'s "old:" cases see it. Kind B (those cases' pins).
- **In the original F77?** Yes: GRSETT builds and solves the implicit system for X only, and computes the metals' `ECOD2Z_H`, which nothing uses ([grsett.f:171-175](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/grsett.f#L171-L175)):
  ```fortran
           CALL GET_IMP_DIFFCO(ALPHA,ECOD2_H,EX_H,EQCOD2X_H,A,B,C,NPT)
           CALL TRIDIAG_GS(A,B,C,EX_PRIME,NPT,EX)
  ```
- **Now:** the metals' D2, set at [original_settling.f90:348-349](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/element_diffusion/original_settling.f90#L348-L349) and mapped to the grid at [settling_grid.f90:78-80](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/element_diffusion/settling_grid.f90#L78-L80); the implicit solve, `iterate_hydrogen_diffusion`, [original_settling.f90:143-199](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/element_diffusion/original_settling.f90#L143-L199), hydrogen's only.
- **What is wrong:** the routines compute the metals' D2 and its derivative (`zone_metal_coeff2`, `metal_coeff2_mid` and their X derivatives) but solve the implicit (diffusion) term for X alone, so their metals settle by the drift term alone.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** each species' equation has both terms, as microdiff solves them.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. It joins M243-M246 in the decision: retiring the routines removes it; fixing them needs the metals' implicit solve and a test.

### M289. settling_num_iterations below 1 skips the implicit solve and reports a non-convergence with change 0

- **Status:** open; B list: element_diffusion item 10 (recommended: the controls check rejects values below 1). Found by round 1's element_diffusion agent (hand-back §5, item 4), checked in the code. No shipped deck sets the control below 1, so no deck moves; the check is io's (`check_controls`). Size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: GRSETT's and MICRODIFF_RUN's iteration loops run zero times ([grsett.f:156](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/grsett.f#L156), [microdiff_run.f:111](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/microdiff_run.f#L111)) and report values never set (zero under `-finit-local-zero`).
- **Now:** microdiff's solve, skipped below 1 ([microdiff_run.f90:164](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/element_diffusion/microdiff_run.f90#L164)), and its pass count ([:190-197](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/element_diffusion/microdiff_run.f90#L190-L197)); the original routines' loop and report, [original_settling.f90:170](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/element_diffusion/original_settling.f90#L170) and [:195-198](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/element_diffusion/original_settling.f90#L195-L198).
- **What is wrong:** with `settling_num_iterations` 0 or below, both pipelines skip the implicit step, so settling is the drift alone, and print "FAILED TO CONVERGE" with change 0.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a value the solver cannot work with is refused when it is read, with a message naming the control.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: reject it in `check_controls` (or treat it as 1).

### M290. The fully ionized density iteration diverges from a fresh record at log T 8.4-9.35 and log P 21-23.5

- **Status:** fixed in round 1B ([46bcab10](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/46bcab10), 2026-11-11, eos item 9; measured below: no shipped deck moves, `test_eos`'s lines from new records in the fully ionized gas do). Found by round 1's eos agent (hand-back §5, first item), checked in the code; the region measured anew (below) is wider than round 1 found.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: EQRELV starts from the density its caller passes and gives up after 20 iterations ([eqrelv.f:63](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqrelv.f#L63), [:165-168](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqrelv.f#L165-L168)):
  ```fortran
        DML = DL + EMUL
           NDEN = NDEN + 1
           IF(NDEN.LE.20) GO TO 10
  ```
- **Now:** `iterate_fully_ionized_density`, [yale_eos.f90:793-933](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/eos/yale/yale_eos.f90#L793-L933), after `start_fully_ionized_solution` ([:740-779](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/eos/yale/yale_eos.f90#L740-L779)).
- **What is wrong:** from a fresh `eos_result`, whose log ρ is 0, the iteration diverges toward log ρ = −80 at log T 8.4 to 9.35 and log P 21 to 23.5; from a start near the answer it converges.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a solver converges from any start inside its table, or brackets the root first.
- **What we did:** round 1B (2026-11-11): `start_fully_ionized_solution` starts a new record (log10_density and density both zero, `eos_result`'s defaults) from the ideal gas's density, β P/((R/μ) T) with the record's R/μ; a record that holds a density (every production caller sets log10_density from the model before its call) starts from it, as before, so a start 100 dex off still does not converge (M93's check). Measured with a scratch driver (X 0.70, Z 0.016492, the production EOS): from a new record the iteration ran away toward the radiation pressure (log ρ to −80) at every log T from 7.45 to the probe's 9.6 and every log P from 18 to 26 where β > 0.05, and from log T 7.25 at the highest pressures, 2,874 of the probe's points, far beyond round 1's log T 8.4–9.35, log P 21–23.5; from the ideal gas's density it converges at every point of log T 5.7–9.6, log P 6–28 (β > 0.01), and at β down to 1e-12 at log T 7.5 and 8.5. The new start moves a lookup only where a new record reaches the fully ionized gas: production callers set the start, so no deck moves (measured on the 56-deck set and the 35 pins: byte-identical); `test_eos`'s evaluations from new records in the fully ionized gas move within the iteration's tolerance (values by about 1e-10 relative, the finite-difference columns' fifth digit by up to 2.4e-5), and a new ok/FAIL check, caught by a mutation of the new start, converges from a new record at log T 9, log P 22, to what a start near the answer gives. Under the devel flags `test_eos` still stopped at its check of a start 100 dex off (M93's), where the iteration's second-order step overflows far from its root (yale_eos.f90:925, the F77's formula), not at this start: that overflow is M305, capped in round 1B ([1bd927eb](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/1bd927eb)), and `test_eos` now runs to its end under the devel flags.

### M291. OPAL's table reader keeps the last X block's T6 grid and compares no grid across the blocks

- **Status:** fixed in round 1B ([03be24fe](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/03be24fe), 2026-11-11, eos item 10; measured below: no shipped deck moves). Found by round 1's eos agent (hand-back §5, second item), checked in the code. The shipped tables' blocks agree, so the check moves no deck. Kind A for the decks; `test_eos`'s pin moves (its new check).
- **In the original F77?** Yes: READCOEOS06 (and READCOEOS01 and READCO) reads each block's T6 column into the same list and takes the grid from it after the last block ([readcoeos06.f:87](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/readcoeos06.f#L87), [:99-104](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/readcoeos06.f#L99-L104)).
- **Now:** `readcoeos`, [opal_table_reader.f90:66-224](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/eos/opal/opal_table_reader.f90#L66-L224): each block's rows read into `t6_list` ([:206-211](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/eos/opal/opal_table_reader.f90#L206-L211)), and the grid taken from it after the read ([:126-135](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/eos/opal/opal_table_reader.f90#L126-L135)).
- **What is wrong:** each X block's T6 column is read into `t6_list` over the previous block's, so the grid is the last block's, and neither the T6 nor the density grid is compared across blocks: a block on another grid is read without a word.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a reader rejects a table it cannot use (M136's rule, which round 1 applied to the SCV tables).
- **What we did:** round 1B (2026-11-11): `readcoeos` compares each X block's density at every column with the first block's, and the T6 of every row it reads with the block before's (so with the first block's), and refuses a table off the first block's grid: ierr = 1, the unit closed, with a message (`report_opal_grid_mismatch`) naming the block, the column and the row and both values; the grids are kept from the first block. Checked on every shipped table: the 1995 and 2001 tables and the 206 complete 2006-format tables have each block on the first's grid (the 2001 table's fifth block has 77 rows in columns 114 and 115 where the others have 80, but the reader reads 77 there), and a probe read all 205 tables the reader accepts through the new check without a refusal. Measured on the 56-deck set and the 35 pins: byte-identical. `test_eos`: a new ok/FAIL check on two doctored copies of the 2006 table (a T6 of the X = 0.6 block made 1.0001, and a density of that block made 0.10000001), caught by a mutation of either comparison; the 1995 zero-T6 check now zeroes the T6 in all five blocks (a zero in one block alone is now off the first block's grid, so its own check would no longer be reached). Found on the way: six shipped 2006-format tables are unusable, and are refused, as before, by the reader's read check: `EOSOPAL06Z0.010264873` is empty, `EOSOPAL06Z0.001039811` and `EOSOPAL06Z0.002606204` hold one X block, and `EOSOPAL06Z0.090863722`, `0.118215775`, `0.600000000` and `0.001039811` hold fields Fortran wrote as asterisks (one to 447 of them); no shipped deck names any of them (M307).

### M292. In OPAL's X interpolation a huge entry with a negative Lagrange weight passes every range check, and a negative value comes back

- **Status:** fixed in round 1B ([4b9aecff](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/4b9aecff), 2026-11-11, eos item 11; measured below: no shipped deck moves). Found by round 1's eos agent (hand-back §5, third item), checked in the code. Not reachable with real tables: the coverage sums keep empty entries out of the stencil. Kind A for the decks; `test_eos`'s pin moves (its doctored-table checks).
- **In the original F77?** Yes: ESAC06, ESAC01 and ESAC test one way only ([esac06.f:429](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/esac06.f#L429), [:447](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/esac06.f#L447)): `if(esk(it,ir) .gt. 1.D+20) then`.
- **Now:** the two X checks of `interpolate_opal_eos`, [opal_eos.f90:723](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/eos/opal/opal_eos.f90#L723) and [:744](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/eos/opal/opal_eos.f90#L744), and `t6rinteos`' check, [:945](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/eos/opal/opal_eos.f90#L945); the thresholds `opal_x_interp_overflow` = 1e20 and `opal_range_overflow` = 1e15, [opal_eos_tables.f90:103](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/eos/opal_eos_tables.f90#L103).
- **What is wrong:** the checks find an empty entry (the 1e35 fill) by a result above a threshold. A huge entry that enters with a negative weight (the second quadratic's last node always has one, −1/8 at mid-interval) makes the result hugely negative, which passes all three, and a negative value is returned.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a check for a value that cannot be interpolated catches it whatever the sign of its weight.
- **What we did:** round 1B (2026-11-11): the X interpolation checks each node's value by its magnitude, at the three places one is made (the first quadratic, the second, and the copy of the one table at X below 1e-6, which had no check), and a value beyond 1e20 either way is now an error, ierr = 1, its message on the terminal and in the run log (`report_x_interpolation`, which names the X tables it read). Before, the X checks only wrote to the run log and the T6-rho check returned the error, so a huge node with a negative T6-rho weight slipped past it too. A test of the sign alone would refuse real values: dE/dRho is negative in 103,839 of the 117,440 rows of the 2006 table at Z = 0.016492, down to −3.7e14 over the 206 complete 2006 tables, and E is negative in 12 rows; the magnitude test's margin over the largest real value is 2.7e5. The T6-rho check stays one-sided, since that dE/dRho is within a factor 2.7 of its 1e15 and every node reaching it has passed the X check. Measured on the 56-deck set and the 35 pins: byte-identical. `test_eos`: three new ok/FAIL checks on doctored copies of the 2006 table (P/P0 at T6 = 1, ρ = 0.1 made +1e21 in the X = 0.6 table, which the second quadratic weights by −1/8 at X = 0.3; the same in the X = 0 table, which the first quadratic weights by −1/8; and −1e21 there, read alone at X = 0), each caught by a mutation that drops the `abs`; on the code before the fix the three returned ierr = 0 with P12 = −1.96e18, −1.96e18 and −3.14e19. The existing check of the −1e21 entry now names it on the terminal: its pinned line "T6RINTEOS06: Interpolation indices out of range" became the X check's two lines.

### M293. The Saha solver's non-convergence is only a run-log warning, and decks reach it

- **Status:** fixed in round 2B (2026-11-13, core's B list item 30: an error, the owner's decision of 2026-11-13, made after M86's fix and a count of the shipped decks outside the 56; no deck moves). B list: eos item 8. Found by round 1's eos agent (hand-back §4, item 8). Decks reach it: the pinned log of `examples/run_from_dbl_to_zams/Test_m0030_feh0_noGS_ZAMS` holds five "-----SAHA FAILURE" lines, and the run logs of the 10 Msun deck of `examples/test_nuclear_reaction_rates` and of the 3 Msun giant rotation decks (`examples/giant_differential_rotation`, outside the 56-deck set and not counted in round 1B) hold more. Counted in round 1B (below); the owner's decision is pending. Kind B if made an error (those runs would stop).
- **In the original F77?** Yes: EQSAHA writes the same line and carries on ([eqsaha.f:162-163](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqsaha.f#L162-L163)):
  ```fortran
        WRITE(ISHORT,99) TL,PL,E,DELTE
   99   FORMAT(' -----SAHA FAILURE (TL,PL)=',2F10.6,'  (E,DE)=',2F20.12)
  ```
- **Now:** the end of `solve_saha_system`, [yale_eos.f90:355-361](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/eos/yale/yale_eos.f90#L355-L361).
- **What is wrong:** after `max_saha_iterations` without convergence the solver writes the line to the run log, and its last iterate stands as the result with `ierr` 0. The fully ionized iteration's failure, the same kind of event, is an error since round 1 (M93).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a solver that did not converge tells its caller, which decides (M93's reasoning), unless the last iterate is known to be close enough.
- **Recorded:** not fixed then: a decision for the owner. Its message is reworded in eos's message commit (round 1B), "Saha solver: no convergence in 20 iterations at log T, log P ...; the last iterate stands". Counted in round 1B (2026-11-11, eos item 8) on the 56-deck set at the eos fixes' final tree: 54 decks never reach it, `Test_m1000_feh0_noGSstdpp_ZAMS` included; `examples/run_from_dbl_to_zams/Test_m0030_feh0_noGS_ZAMS` 5 times (log T 3.707, log P 7.78; E about 6.9e-7, its last step 5.3e-10, under the 1e-9 tolerance, so the charge residual missed it) and `examples/test_nuclear_reaction_rates/Test_m10000_feh0_noGSstdcno_ZAMS` 2,212 times (log T 4.06-5.19, log P 4.1-7.1), every time in the starting model's envelope refit, before the first model. There the EOS still holds the run plan's partial mixture: `read_starting_model` refits the envelope (`rescale_and_refit_envelope`, [starting_model.f90:224](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/a0039581/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L224)) before `update_surface_mixture` installs the star's ([:229](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/a0039581/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L229)), so X_env is 0 and the envelope's 1/A sum is 0; a scratch probe in the 10 Msun deck found every one of its 3,772 lookups there with a He number fraction of −0.336, whose E bound, 1 + n_He = 0.6636, holds E below its root, so the solver cannot converge. The F77's STARIN has the same order (ENVINT and EQSTAT before AMUENV, [starin.f:554](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/starin.f#L554), [:609](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/starin.f#L609), [:814](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/starin.f#L814)). Of the 56 decks only these two and `Test_m1000_feh0_noGSstdpp_ZAMS` refit their envelope. That order is M86, recorded since 2026-10-29 and proposed as a measured fix in core's round 2; the eos agent's probe found the solver converging at those points from fresh records with the envelope's mixture. So making the warning an error would stop these two decks in card 1 today, and most likely none once the refit sees the star's mixture. The counts are for the owner's decision.
- **Round 2 (2026-11-12/13):** core's B list (`audit/module-evaluation-7-2026-11-10/B_LIST_CORE.md`, item 30): M86's fix, measured in round 2, removes all 2,217 non-convergences of the compare set (item 12); an error after it is recommended, measured then.
- **What we did:** round 2B (2026-11-13), an error, after M86's fix and a count. The count: every shipped inlist of `examples/` and `testsuite/` outside the 56-deck set (275; the four `.nml1` pairs are all in the set), each run from a scratch copy of its directory with every card's `max_model_number` capped (relative `output/` paths sent to the run's output directory; the six `class_exercises/exercise_2` decks, which name `startmodels/` and `input/` beside them, pointed at `{YREC_START}/dbl` and `{YREC_INPUT}`), and every file each run wrote searched for the solver's line (the tool: `sweep.py` in the work directory's `scratch_b2_core1/tools`). With a cap of 5 models per card, 275 decks in 165 s (4 at a time; 619 s of CPU): before M86 (at its parent, 7f94a0b3) 41,128 non-convergences in 35 decks: 24 `run_from_dbl_to_zams` ZAMS decks (16 from 3.5 to 16 Msun, 1,890 to 3,084 each; 8 from 0.04 to 0.15 Msun, 1 to 4 each), the three 9 Msun class exercises (2,019 each) and 8 testsuite decks (2 to 6 each, and 92 in `Test_m1p4feh+0p0GS98_dif_TAMS`), all in the stretch M86 changes, the first card's model read; after M86, none. With a cap of 50, after M86, 275 decks in 504 s (3 at a time; 1,505 s of CPU): none. Not counted: four testsuite decks (`Test_m1p0feh+0p0GS98_base_HeIgnite`, `Test_m3p0feh+0p0GS98_std25_ZAHB`, `Test_m9p0feh+0p0GS98_base_TAHB`, `Test_m9p0feh+0p0GS98_yaleeos_TAHB`) start from another run's output and stop at the read; `run_from_seed_to_start/m3000gs98z040000_prems` and `run_from_start_to_dbl/m25000gs98z018804_Dbl` stop at their first model ("blend_eos: beta = P_gas/P is not positive"), before and after M86, after their refit; and `Test_m0040`, `Test_m0050` and `Test_m0060_feh0_noGS_ZAMS` stop before model 50 of card 1 before and after M86 (O3's low-mass family), after a refit that had 1-3 non-convergences before M86 and none after. So `solve_saha_system` now returns ierr = 1 when it does not converge, with its message through `eos_report` (the terminal and the run log; "the last iterate stands" goes), and `compute_saha_eos` and `gas_eos` pass it on, as the fully ionized iteration's failure does (M93). Measured on the 56-deck set and the 35 pins against M86's snapshot: ALL IDENTICAL. `test_eos` gains the case: with the run plan's partial mixture (X_env 0, its weights unset) at a point of the 10 Msun refit (log T 4.062, log P 4.123), ierr = 1 and the message; its pin gains those three lines, and a mutation (ierr 0) is caught (82 of 82 apply). eos/README.md says so; `test_eos.f90`'s pointer to the atomic weights follows them to `model_rescaling` (M85).
- **Two unit tests met it (round 2B, after the fix's commit):** `test_envelope_integration` and `test_convection` called the EOS without an envelope mixture (the run plan's unset one, X_env 0 and zero weights), where the Saha solver does not converge, so both stopped once it became an error (their release runs had passed with the warning, which `test_convection` pinned seven times). Each now installs the mixture a run's first model read gives (`test_envelope_integration`: model_rescaling's `compute_envelope_mixture` and `install_surface_mixture_settings` for its surface X and Z, its report byte-identical; `test_convection`: the default mixture seed at X = 0.70 and its Z, its pin re-pinned: the seven warnings go, and with the real H_P its cases' overshoot edges move by one shell, the M285 merge case's union now ending at shell 11, where it ended at 10). `mutate.py convection` 49 of 49 caught.

### M295. check_boundaries' name map ignores scope, so a contained procedure in one domain shadows another domain's procedure of the same name

- **Status:** open (tool). Found by round 1's atm agent (hand-back §5, item 1), checked in the code. No false report today: atm renamed its internal procedure, and `make check` passes. Kind A (tooling), size S. Not on the B lists.
- **In the original F77?** No: the checker is 2026's.
- **Now:** `main`'s name map, [check_boundaries.py:1402-1409](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/tools/check_boundaries.py#L1402-L1409), and the call check after it, [:1411-1422](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/tools/check_boundaries.py#L1411-L1422); `DEF_RE`, [:120-125](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/tools/check_boundaries.py#L120-L125).
- **What is wrong:** `defs` maps each procedure name to the last domain that defines it, internal (contained) procedures included, and the call check looks every `call` up there whatever its scope. So a contained procedure in one domain that has the name of a procedure another domain calls makes that call look cross-domain. In round 1 it did twice: atm's internal `report_outside_table` against eos/opal/opal_eos.f90's, and a test helper `write_lines` against rotation_messages'; atm rewrote its branch to avoid the name. The other half of the atm agent's report, that `DEF_RE` misses `pure` and `elemental` procedures, is M141.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a checker resolves a name as the compiler does; a false report sends a newcomer to rename correct code.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: skip contained procedures in the map (no other file can call them) and resolve a call by the caller's own procedures and `use` lines first; with M141's prefixes.
- **Round 1B:** it struck again. atm's new message procedure `report_spline_failure` made scv_eos's internal procedure of that name look like a cross-domain call into atm; atm named its own `report_table_spline_failure` instead (atm's hand-back §5, item 1). The checker's other blind spot, function references, is M304.

### M296. check_boundaries' scratch-module check reads a `use, intrinsic :: ...` line as a module variable

- **Status:** open (tool). Found by round 1's element_diffusion agent (hand-back §1, its note for the integrator), checked in the code. To pass, element_diffusion_scratch.f90 writes `use iso_fortran_env, only: dp => real64`, the only `use` of that module without `, intrinsic ::` in src/ (124 files have the intrinsic form). Kind A (tooling), size S. Not on the B lists.
- **In the original F77?** No: the check came with the 2026-10 scratch modules.
- **Now:** `check_scratch_types_only`, [check_boundaries.py:282-299](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/tools/check_boundaries.py#L282-L299), whose test is at [:297](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/tools/check_boundaries.py#L297); [element_diffusion_scratch.f90:14](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2c9a6ec4/src/element_diffusion/element_diffusion_scratch.f90#L14).
- **What is wrong:** outside a type block the check takes every line holding `::` that is not `public`, `private` or a parameter for a module variable, so `use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: dp => real64` is refused.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a `use` statement declares no variable.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: skip `use` statements in the check; element_diffusion_scratch.f90 can then take the intrinsic form again.
