## 16. Found in round 1B (2026-11-11/12)

Round 1B made the B lists' measured fixes (`audit/module-evaluation-7-2026-11-10/B_LISTS.md`) for kap, atm, convection and eos, one package at a time, each on its own branch from the previous package's merge; yrec-next merged them in [d66dd005](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/d66dd005) (kap), [c5dd0ab3](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/c5dd0ab3) (atm), [6fcc96cb](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/6fcc96cb) (convection) and [1395075b](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/1395075b) (eos). element_diffusion got no B work, by the owner's answer of 2026-11-11. The fixes are in their own entries, each status giving its commit. These items are the new defects the four agents' hand-backs listed, in the order of the round's packages: kap (M298-M300), atm (M301), convection (M302-M304) and eos (M305-M308). M302, M305 and M306 were fixed in the round, in the commits that met them; the rest are open, and none is on a B list (M308 was fixed after the round, on 2026-11-14).

- **How they were checked.** Each was found by an agent in its own package and checked again for its entry: the lines in the code at 1395075b (for a fixed item, also before its fix), the F77 at 6cd56739. The numbers are the agents' measurements.
- **Entered in older entries.** A find that belongs to an older entry is in that entry: M86 (the starting model's envelope refit before `update_surface_mixture`, which eos found to cause every Saha non-convergence of M293), M241 (round 1 misdescribed the TAHB sample's moves), M278 (kap's research of the mixing rule), M285 (not latent), M290 (its region wider than round 1 found), M293 (the counts) and M295 (struck again).
- **Not entered.** The round's own slips, caught before the merges: a devel `test_eos` trap that round 1 had attributed, from buffered output, to the wrong check (corrected in M92's commit message, 346e1af2, amended before the merge), and the eos agent's staged edit scripts (a mutation left on moved text, a test that M88's ramp made vacuous, fixed in [b8ecbef3](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/b8ecbef3), a format that printed asterisks).
- Current-code links point at [1395075b](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/tree/1395075b/src).

**Notes** (not defects in YREC):
- gfortran 15.2 stops with an internal compiler error on `log10` in a parameter's initializer when math_lib's crmath versions are in scope (`use math_lib` in a crmath build). So the two constants round 1B wrote as formulas, kap's log10(16σ/3) (KA-14, M222's entry) and atm's ¼ log10(3/4) (the gray T-τ constant, [c9e6ec4e](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/c9e6ec4e)), are computed at each call.
- gfortran 15.2 passed an array constructor with a computed character length, `[character(len=message_length) :: a // ': ' // trim(b)]`, to a procedure with a garbage length (a malloc trap in `_gfortran_string_trim` under -O3 and the devel flags); kap_lib's `report_reason` builds a local line instead. Other packages' messages modules may want the same care.
- `input/opacity/atomic/op05/GS98alpha02.OP17`'s data: unlike every other shipped OPAL 1995-format table, its empty high-T corner differs by X (two columns missing from log T 6.8 in the X = 0 tables, three or four from X = 0.35) and, in its Z = 0.1 tables at X = 0.2 and 0.35, by Z; at low R, 9.999 entries fill the first column at almost every log T. The fixed-Z table blends 9.999 with real values wherever its Z stencil mixes the two, and the ≥ 9.9 test does not catch the blend. No shipped deck uses the table, and the F77's import holds the same file (its copy in `input/opacity/atomic/legacy/opal95/` too). It is the only table M277 and M298 could show.
- The OPAL 2001 EOS table's fifth X block has 77 rows in columns 114 and 115 where the other blocks have 80; the reader reads 77 there (M291), so nothing is lost.

### M298. OPAL95's high-R density shift tests the X index the previous lookup left, before the lookup locates its own X stencil

- **Status:** fixed in round 3 (2026-11-18, [3e332488](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/3e332488), the kap agent; byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins, as predicted). At the registration: open. Found by round 1B's kap agent (hand-back §5, item 1) while fixing M277, checked in the code. No effect with the shipped tables but `op05/GS98alpha02.OP17`, which no shipped deck uses: in every other OPAL 1995-format table the empty high-T corner is the same at every X (M277), so which X index the shift reads does not matter. Kind B for that table only; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: GETOPAL95 tests and searches `CAPPA(JX(1,1),...)` before it locates `JX` ([getopal95.f:143](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/getopal95.f#L143), [:159](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/getopal95.f#L159), against the X search at [:229-273](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/getopal95.f#L229-L273)):
  ```fortran
        IF(CAPPA(JX(1,1),JT+3,JD(1)+3) .GE. 9.9D0) THEN
           IXX = JX(1,1)
           IF(X.GT.XXG(JX(1,1)+2))THEN
  ```
- **Before the fix** (at the registration): `compute_opal95_opacity`: the shift's tests and its search read `tbl%index_x(1,1)`, [opal95_opacity.f90:339-376](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1395075b/src/kap/opal95/opal95_opacity.f90#L339-L376); the X stencil is located after them, by `locate_opal95_x_stencil` at [:427](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1395075b/src/kap/opal95/opal95_opacity.f90#L427) (3D) and [:469](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1395075b/src/kap/opal95/opal95_opacity.f90#L469) (4D).
- **What is wrong:** the shift decides whether the stencil's top log R column is empty, and where each T row's last filled column is, in the fixed-Z table at X index `tbl%index_x(1,1)`, which at that point is the previous lookup's (the warm-start cursor), or 1 after `kap_init`. So the shift is taken at another X than the point's, and where a table's corner differs by X the stencil can end at the wrong column.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the shift reads the table at the point's X, as the interpolation that follows does.
- **Proposed at the registration:** locate the X stencil before the shift (or test each of its X rows); byte-identical with the tables the shipped decks use, a change for GS98alpha02.OP17 alone.
- **What we did:** round 3 (2026-11-18, [3e332488](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/3e332488)): the lookup chooses its path and locates its Z and X stencils before the corner test, and the test reads the fixed-Z table in every X table the point's interpolation in X uses (the 3D stencil's four; the four the surface table was built from, recorded by the build; the 4D path's at its first Z row): a cell empty in any of them shifts the row, and a row's last filled column is the last filled in all of them. test_kap, on a copy of GS98.OP17 whose X = 0.70 tables lack one cell: "OPAL95 high-R shift: independent of the previous lookup's X" (7.0 before, 0 after) and "... no empty cell of the stencil's X tables read" (0.013 from the unedited table's before, 2.1e-4 after); mutations `opal95-shift-stale-x`, `opal95-shift-first-x-table`, `opal95-shift-surface-tables`. Byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins.

### M299. Below log ρ = −6 the conductive opacity takes the H table's slope, and stops where log R crosses 0

- **Status:** open. Found by round 1B's kap agent (hand-back §5, item 2) while fixing M222, checked in the code; kap/README's "Kept by decision, or open" records the slope, not the stop. Reached in every deck's photosphere, where conduction is negligible since M222 (κ_rad/κ_c of 1e-9 to 1e-7), so a fix moves κ at round-off there and the path-sensitive decks by their amplification. Kind B (tiny), size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: CONDOPACPINT takes the slope and the T derivative from the H call alone at log ρ = −6, and extrapolates only where log R ≥ 0 ([condopacpint.f:45](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/condopacpint.f#L45), [:75-77](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/condopacpint.f#L75-L77)):
  ```fortran
         RL = DL - 3.0D0*(TL-6.0D0)
         IF (DL.LT.-6.0D0.AND.RL.GE.0.0D0) THEN
           CALL CondOpacP(1.0D0,TL,-6.0D0,CONDXL,QODC,QOTC)
  ```
- **Now:** `compute_conductive_opacity`'s branch below `conductive_logrho_min`, [conductive_opacity.f90:162-190](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1395075b/src/kap/conductive/conductive_opacity.f90#L162-L190): the H call returns the slope and dln κ/dln T ([:166-167](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1395075b/src/kap/conductive/conductive_opacity.f90#L166-L167)), the He and O calls discard theirs; the gate on `extrapolation_indicator`, log R ([:124](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1395075b/src/kap/conductive/conductive_opacity.f90#L124)), at [:165](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1395075b/src/kap/conductive/conductive_opacity.f90#L165); without it the default, no conduction, stands ([:117-122](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1395075b/src/kap/conductive/conductive_opacity.f90#L117-L122)).
- **What is wrong:**
  - The extrapolation's slope dln κ_c/dln ρ, and the dln κ_c/dln T the branch returns, are the H table's at log ρ = −6 (`condopacp` for charge 1), not the mixture's, which the main branch takes as the 1/K-weighted mean of the three species' ([:148-154](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1395075b/src/kap/conductive/conductive_opacity.f90#L148-L154)).
  - Below log ρ = −6 conduction is on only where log R = log ρ − 3(log T − 6) ≥ 0. Where log R crosses 0, κ_c goes from about 1e8 cm²/g to none, a jump in κ of κ_rad/κ_c, 1e-9 to 1e-8 relative since M222.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the branch is the main formula at log ρ = −6 carried to the point with the mixture's own slope (M222's rule), and conduction ends without a jump, so that κ and its derivatives are continuous (as at the opacity's other edges).
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: the mixture's slope and T derivative at −6 (the main branch's 1/K-weighted mean), and a smooth end in place of the stop at log R = 0; a measured change at round-off in every deck's photosphere.
- **Round 3 (2026-11-18):** M299 and M341 measured together in scratch, not committed (the kap agent's B list item 1; patch `scratch_r3_kap/patches/m299_m341_trial.patch` in the work directory): below the table the branch takes the mixture's derivatives (the 1/K-weighted mean) as the branch inside it does, and `species_conductivities` returns a zero density slope for a species whose own density is clamped at the table's edge; the smooth end in place of the stop at log R = 0 (M299's second half) is not in the trial. On 24 decks (the 16 configuration-matrix decks, cm_accretion, Test_solar_noGS_norot, Test_solarGS98_base and _dif, the 0.03 Msun ZAMS deck, the 1 Msun pp deck, ZAHB, rv_basic) all 24 move, and their 20 pins: Test_solarGS98_base log L -1.1e-5 dex, log Teff -1.3e-6, 821 models for 822; Test_solarGS98_dif log L +1.9e-5, log Teff +6.0e-6, 817 for 816; Test_solar_noGS_norot +2.2e-11; the configuration-matrix decks 1e-12 to 5e-11; Test_m0030_feh0_noGS_ZAMS -6.9e-9; ZAHB 1.7e-12; rv_basic -5.1e-11. Largest column changes: Li7 59% (a trace abundance in cm_env_overshoot), logRho 1.8e-4 relative, the rest below 1.4e-6. Every deck moves because conduction is evaluated in every zone's mixture branch; the solar decks' 1e-5 is the convergence path (one model fewer or more). Recommended: adopt both parts as measured; decide the stop at log R = 0 separately (`notes/R3_B_LIST.md`).

### M300. A comment on the conductive mixture's weights stops mid-sentence

- **Status:** fixed in round 2B (2026-11-14), with M278's change, which rewrote these lines. Found by round 1B's kap agent (hand-back §5, item 4). Text only; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: the comment is CONDOPACPINT's, cut the same way ([condopacpint.f:32](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/condopacpint.f#L32)):
  ```fortran
         WtH1 = WtH1Base * FXION(1) ! (FXION(1)/1D0 is the fraction
  ```
- **Now:** [conductive_opacity.f90:113](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1395075b/src/kap/conductive/conductive_opacity.f90#L113): `weight_h1 = number_fraction_h1 * ion_fraction(1) ! (FXION(1)/1D0 is the fraction`.
- **What is wrong:** the trailing comment ends mid-sentence and names the F77's `FXION`; the comment above the weights ([:110-112](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1395075b/src/kap/conductive/conductive_opacity.f90#L110-L112)) already says what `ion_fraction(1)` is.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a comment is a sentence, in the code's own names.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: drop the trailing comment, or with M278's change, which rewrites these lines.

### M301. compare_decks' version-line pattern accepts only a hexadecimal hash, so in a tree outside git every run log differs

- **Status:** open (tool). Found by round 1B's atm agent (hand-back §5, item 2) on its control tree, made with `git archive`. Numeric files compare normally; only the logs, and so the pins line, show false differences. Kind A (tooling), size S.
- **In the original F77?** No: compare_decks is round 0's (2026-11-10).
- **Now:** `VER`, [compare_decks.py:90](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1395075b/src/tools/compare_decks.py#L90), used by `same_file` ([:93-96](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1395075b/src/tools/compare_decks.py#L93-L96)); the Makefile writes `unknown` for the hash outside a git checkout ([Makefile:284-291](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1395075b/src/Makefile#L284-L291)).
- **What is wrong:** `VER`, `^# YREC v\S* \([0-9a-f]+(-dirty)?\)$`, matches the run log's version line only with a hexadecimal hash. A build outside a git checkout (an archive, an rsync copy) writes "# YREC v202602 (unknown)", so `same_file` counts that line as a difference: every .log differs from the base, and the pins line reports all 35 pins as DIFF.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the comparison sets the version line aside whatever hash it carries, as `same_file`'s docstring says ("byte-equal, the version line aside").
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed; the atm agent set aside the log differences of its control tree that were in the version line alone. Proposed fix: `\(([0-9a-f]+|unknown)(-dirty)?\)`.
- **Seen again in round 3 (2026-11-18):** the kap agent's first compare of an exported copy of its branch (no .git) printed "56 NOT IDENTICAL, 0 pins OK"; with the version line stripped every output and pin was identical. The pattern is unchanged at 7ea92ace ([compare_decks.py:90](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/tools/compare_decks.py#L90)). The integrator listed it as a new finding; it is this entry. Whoever compares an exported copy: git-init the copy, or apply the proposed fix first.

### M302. evolve_step dropped burn_light_elements' ierr

- **Status:** fixed in [4c1c730a](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/4c1c730a) (2026-11-11, round 1B's convection, in the commit that adds `envelope_overshoot_depth`'s EOS `ierr` there). Found by round 1B's convection agent (hand-back §5, item 1). Byte-identical: no compared deck fails there.
- **In the original F77?** No: the `ierr` is 2026's (CONVEC and LIBURN had no error return).
- **Before the fix:** `evolve_step`, [step_driver.f90:206](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/c5dd0ab3/src/core/step/step_driver.f90#L206) at c5dd0ab3: `call burn_light_elements` with no test after it, while the internal `burn_light_elements` returns `ierr` from the end-of-step `find_convection_zones` ([:602-603](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/c5dd0ab3/src/core/step/step_driver.f90#L602-L603)).
- **What was wrong:** when the end-of-step `find_convection_zones` failed (`convection_too_many_zones`, or an EOS failure in the overshoot's H_P), `burn_light_elements` returned with `ierr` set and the step went on.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a failure ends the step and reaches its caller, as every other call in `evolve_step` does.
- **What we did:** `if (ierr /= 0) return` after the call ([step_driver.f90:206-207](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1395075b/src/core/step/step_driver.f90#L206-L207)).

### M304. check_boundaries checks only `call` statements, not function references

- **Status:** open (tool). Found by round 1B's convection agent (hand-back §5, item 5). No missed violation today: core and rotation called convection's `envelope_overshoot_depth` and `pressure_scale_height` as functions while neither was in `PUBLIC["convection"]`; round 1B made the first a subroutine, now listed, and the second is used inside convection only. Kind A (tooling), size S.
- **In the original F77?** No: the checker is 2026's.
- **Now:** `CALL_RE`, [check_boundaries.py:122](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1395075b/src/tools/check_boundaries.py#L122), the only pattern `main`'s cross-domain check matches ([:1419-1425](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1395075b/src/tools/check_boundaries.py#L1419-L1425)).
- **What is wrong:** a cross-domain reference to a function (`x = f(...)`) is never compared with the domain's `PUBLIC` list, so a domain can use another's private function without a report; the first such use showed up only when the function became a subroutine.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the boundary check covers every way one domain uses another's procedures.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: also check the names of each cross-domain `use <module>, only: ...` list (or every name followed by `(` outside a declaration) against the domain's procedures, with M295's scope rule and M141's prefixes.

### M305. The fully ionized density iteration's second-order step overflows far from its root

- **Status:** fixed in [1bd927eb](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/1bd927eb) (2026-11-11, round 1B's eos; not on the B list). Found by round 1B's eos agent (hand-back §5, item 1), at `test_eos`'s check of a start 100 dex off (M93's). Byte-identical on the 56 decks, the 35 pins and `test_eos`'s release pin.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: EQRELV takes the term through DEXP with no bound ([eqrelv.f:158-159](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqrelv.f#L158-L159)):
  ```fortran
        FACTL=DLOG10(0.5D0)+PR9L+2.D0*PR8L
        FACT=DEXP(CLN*FACTL)
  ```
- **Before the fix:** `iterate_fully_ionized_density`, [yale_eos.f90:924-925](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/46bcab10/src/eos/yale/yale_eos.f90#L924-L925) at 46bcab10.
- **What was wrong:** the Newton step's second-order term, 0.5 |pr9| pr8², is taken through its log10 `factl` and `exp`. Far from the root (`test_eos`'s start 100 dex off) `factl` passed 308 and `exp` overflowed: a trap under the devel flags, so `devel_tests.py` skipped `test_eos` as a known failure (M297), and Inf in a release build, where the step was then clamped to `max_density_step_dex` (4 dex).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a solver's arithmetic stays finite; a start far off converges or fails, it does not overflow.
- **What we did:** `factl` is capped at `max_second_order_log10` = 300 ([yale_eos.f90:70](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1395075b/src/eos/yale/yale_eos.f90#L70), [:929-934](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1395075b/src/eos/yale/yale_eos.f90#L929-L934)); a term of 1e300 already takes the step to the same 4 dex clamp, so the iteration does what it did. Measured on a clone at the change: the 56-deck set and the 35 pins ALL IDENTICAL, the release `test_eos` identical to its pin. Under the devel flags `test_eos` now runs to its end (19 runtime warnings, `-fcheck=all`'s array temporaries), so its known failure is gone from `devel_tests.py`, and eos/README says that `test_eos` runs clean under the devel flags.

### M306. eos's message lines held 200 characters, so a missing table with a long path crashed the message

- **Status:** fixed in [e5a03a6f](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/e5a03a6f) (2026-11-12, round 1B's eos message commit, B list eos item 7). Found by round 1B's eos agent (hand-back §5, item 2). No shipped deck's path is that long. Kind A.
- **In the original F77?** No: eos_messages is 2026's.
- **Before the fix:** `message_length` = 200, [eos_messages.f90:25](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6fcc96cb/src/eos/eos_messages.f90#L25) at 6fcc96cb.
- **What was wrong:** a message is formatted into lines of `message_length` characters by an internal write, and a table path may hold 256 characters (the controls' length), so a missing table with a long path stopped the message's write with a Fortran runtime error ("End of record") instead of the reader returning `ierr` with its message.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** an error path reports the error.
- **What we did:** `message_length` = 400 ([eos_messages.f90:26](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1395075b/src/eos/eos_messages.f90#L26)), room for a 256-character path and the text before it, as the module's header says.

### M309. With no envelope to integrate, the "ENVELOPE INTEGRATION COMPLETE" diagnostics line reports the atmosphere's step counts and stale values

- **Status:** open. Found by round 2's core agent E (hand-back §6, item 1). Solver diagnostics only (`report_solver_diagnostics`); no result reads the event. Kind B in principle (a run-log line), but no pinned deck turns the diagnostics on. Size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes (agent E's hand-back says no; the closing agent's check found it). ENVINT's thin-envelope branch jumps to label 300 past the envelope's loop ([envint.f:410-421](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/envint.f#L410-L421)), and after 300 the line is written whichever way the code came, with the atmosphere's NOK and NBAD ([:745](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/envint.f#L745)):
  ```fortran
        IF(SENV.GT.-1.0D-12) THEN
  ...
  	 GOTO 300
  ...
        WRITE(ISHORT,215)NOK,NBAD,SDIF,Y(1),(ERRSUM(J),J=1,3)
  ```
  The modern code writes it only with the solver diagnostics on (round 2's events).
- **Now:** `integrate_envelope`, the thin branch at [envelope_integration_kernel.f90:697-701](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/8d7feee2/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L697-L701) and the event after both branches at [:712-714](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/8d7feee2/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L712-L714); its report, [envelope_integration.f90:290-298](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/8d7feee2/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration.f90#L290-L298).
- **What is wrong:** when `log_fit_point_mass_fraction` lies above `max_log_fit_point_mass_fraction` no envelope is integrated, but the `envint_envelope_done` event is still added, with `num_ok` and `num_bad` as the atmosphere's integration left them and `mass_diff_remaining` and `y(1)` from that integration (or unset), so the run log's "ENVELOPE INTEGRATION COMPLETE ... NUMBER OF STEPS ACCEPTED" line describes an integration that did not happen.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a diagnostics line reports what ran.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: add the event only after an envelope integration, or a thin-envelope event of its own; test_envelope_integration's thin case can check it.
- **Round 3 (2026-11-18):** patch ready, not committed (the core2 agent's B list item 2, `scratch_r3_core2/patches/M309_thin_envelope_event.patch`): the `envint_envelope_done` event is added only after an integration (it moves into `integrate_envelope`'s else branch), and test_envelope_integration gains "thin: no envelope event (the atmosphere's is the last)". Moves a run-log line only with the solver diagnostics on and a fitting mass above -1e-12; no deck or pin. The unit test with the patch differs from its expected output by the new line only. Since [d2ad07ac](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/d2ad07ac) the values the line reports are zero, not stale. The same branch leaves the previous integration's envelope points in place: M390.

### M310. The envelope integration's error tolerances bound bsstep's error estimate, not the error: a step can be 55 tolerances off

- **Status:** fixed (doc) in round 3 (2026-11-18, [998ecd59](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/998ecd59), the core2 agent; byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins). At the registration: open (doc). Found by round 2's core agent E (hand-back §6, item 2) while writing test_envelope_integration. Not a code defect: the tolerance controls mean less than their descriptions say. Kind A (the controls' descriptions and the generated defaults). Size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: ENVINT passed ATMERR and ENVERR to BSSTEP as its EPS, the same integrator ([envint.f:261](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/envint.f#L261), [:298](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/envint.f#L298), [:435](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/envint.f#L435)):
  ```fortran
        EPS = ATMERR
  	 CALL BSSTEP(Y,DYDX,NV,X0,H,EPS,YSCAL,HDID,
  ```
- **Before the fix** (at the registration): the descriptions, "Atmosphere integration: error tolerance" and "Envelope integration: error tolerance" ([controls_buffer.f90:859-860](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/8d7feee2/src/io/controls_buffer.f90#L859-L860), [:870-871](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/8d7feee2/src/io/controls_buffer.f90#L870-L871)); the kernel's use, [envelope_integration_kernel.f90:408](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/8d7feee2/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L408), [:739](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/8d7feee2/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L739); the measurement, [test_envelope_integration.f90:96-100](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/8d7feee2/src/core/test/test_envelope_integration.f90#L96-L100).
- **What is wrong:** `atm_error_tol` and `env_error_tol` are bsstep's tolerance on its own error estimate of each step. The integrands interpolate the EOS and opacity tables, so they are not smooth, and the estimate is no bound: test_envelope_integration compares every Bulirsch-Stoer step with an RK4 integration of the same equations between the kernel's points, and at `atm_error_tol` = 1e-9 the largest difference is 55 tolerances (in the atmosphere); the test allows 1000.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a control's description says what it controls.
- **Proposed at the registration:** describe each as "the Bulirsch-Stoer tolerance on each step's error estimate (with tabulated microphysics the step's error can be tens of times larger)", in the registry and the generated defaults, with the control descriptions' next commit.
- **What we did:** round 3 (2026-11-18, [998ecd59](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/998ecd59)): the descriptions of `atm_error_tol` and `env_error_tol` (io/controls_buffer.f90) say "the Bulirsch-Stoer tolerance on each step's error estimate, relative to the step's scale", and that a step's error can be tens of times larger; `physics.defaults` and `controls_registry.md` regenerated from them. No control added, renamed or re-defaulted.

### M311. Two comments said what the code did not do: mass_change's "The run log" for lines written to standard output, and envelope_integrands' "the same argument list"

- **Status:** fixed in [a5b4a03b](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/a5b4a03b) (2026-11-12, round 2, core agent E). Found by agent E (hand-back §6, items 3 and 4). Comments only. Where mass_change's lines should go is on core's B list (`B_LIST_CORE.md`, item 24).
- **In the original F77?** No: both comments are 2026's. MASSLOSS wrote those lines with `WRITE(*,...)` ([massloss.f:71](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/massloss.f#L71)), to standard output, as the code still does.
- **Before the fix** (at [8c1822ad](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/tree/8c1822ad/src)): mass_change.f90's "The run log: dM, dJ, omega(nz), the new and old J_cz, and the convective envelope's mass" and "The run log: the new mass and the step's change, in Msun" above `write(*,...)` statements ([mass_change.f90:575-578](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/8c1822ad/src/core/step/mass_change.f90#L575-L578), [:584-588](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/8c1822ad/src/core/step/mass_change.f90#L584-L588)); envelope_integrands.f90's header, "Both take the same argument list, so that the kernel's envelope_equations can call either" ([envelope_integrands.f90:7-8](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/8c1822ad/src/core/envelope/envelope_integrands.f90#L7-L8)), while the two integrands' argument lists differed.
- **What was wrong:** a reader looked for the lines in the run log and for one interface the integrands do not share.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** comments describe the code as it is.
- **What we did:** the comments say standard output, and the integrands' header describes each argument list (their unused dummies with it).
- **Round 2B (2026-11-14):** mass_change's lines go to the run log (`core_log`), in sentence case ("mass change: timestep reduced from ... s to ... s", "mass change: new mass ... Msun, change ... Msun", the wind's labelled line), and the 911 stop is an error through `core_report` (core's B list item 24); the comments say the run log again.

### M312. After a run, the C entry leaves the run's newunit files open

- **Status:** fixed in round 3 (2026-11-18, [a725a682](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/a725a682), the core1 agent; byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins). At the registration: open. Found by round 2's core agent M (hand-back §6, item 3) while fixing M271; not reproduced. A host that reads the Monte-Carlo files or the isochrone file after `yrec_run` may find their tails unflushed. Kind A. Size S.
- **In the original F77?** No: the C entry is 2026's ([18db37b9](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/18db37b9)), and the files' `newunit` numbers too.
- **Before the fix** (at the registration): `yrec_run` closes the run's units after the run with `close_run_units` ([yrec_capi.f90:74](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/8d7feee2/src/core/run/yrec_capi.f90#L74)), which closes the run log and the final model only ([yrec_reset.f90:57-78](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/8d7feee2/src/core/run/yrec_reset.f90#L57-L78)); `open_run_files` opens the starting model, the Monte-Carlo files and the isochrone file with `newunit` ([run_files.f90:94-117](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/8d7feee2/src/io/run_files.f90#L94-L117)), and its private `close_run_files` closes them only before a later run opens them again ([:150-170](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/8d7feee2/src/io/run_files.f90#L150-L170)).
- **What is wrong:** after `yrec_run` returns, the starting model's unit, the two Monte-Carlo files and the isochrone file stay connected until the next run or the process's end, so their last records may sit in the runtime's buffers when the embedding program reads the files. The old sweep of units 7-99 never reached them either (`newunit` numbers are negative).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the engine closes what it opened before it returns to its host (M271's rule).
- **Proposed at the registration:** io's run_files exports `close_run_files` (it resets each unit variable to -1, which a closer outside io must not skip, or a later `newunit` could reuse a number a stale variable still holds), and `close_run_units` calls it.
- **What we did:** round 3 (2026-11-18, [a725a682](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/a725a682)): `close_run_units` (core/run/yrec_reset.f90) also closes the five files with newunit numbers (the starting model, the Monte-Carlo samples, summary and model files, the isochrone file) and sets their unit variables back to -1, as `run_files`' own close does. test_run_contracts checks the five are -1 after a run through `yrec_run` (reset-03, -04, caught). Byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins. Not done: the one-call form, `close_run_files` exported by io/run_files.f90 (io was not this round's).

### M313. coverage.py runs each deck alone in a fresh directory, so a deck that reads a file beside it fails: cm_monte_carlo exits 1

- **Status:** open (tool). Found by round 2's core agent E (hand-back §6, item 6: "cm_monte_carlo exited 1 in the coverage build, not investigated"); its cause found by the closing agent's coverage run. It lowers core's measured coverage (monte_carlo.f90's sample read and summaries do not run). Kind A (tooling). Size S.
- **In the original F77?** No: coverage.py is 2026's.
- **Now:** `run_decks` copies the deck's inlist alone into a fresh run directory and runs it there ([coverage.py:73-85](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/8d7feee2/src/tools/coverage.py#L73-L85)); cm_monte_carlo reads `dynamics_file = "mc_input.dat"`, relative to its own directory ([cm_monte_carlo.inlist:86](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/8d7feee2/examples/run_config_matrix/cm_monte_carlo.inlist#L86)).
- **What is wrong:** in the run directory the Monte-Carlo parameter file is missing, and the run stops at once: "ERROR: cannot open the Monte Carlo dynamics file mc_input.dat" (exit 1). compare_decks runs each deck in its own directory and is not affected.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the coverage run sees the deck as compare_decks does.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: run each deck in a copy of its directory (or copy the files its relative paths name beside the inlist).
- **Seen again in round 3 (2026-11-18):** cm_monte_carlo exits 1 under coverage.py in the core2 and core3 agents' measures, which therefore leave out monte_carlo.f90's sample read and summaries (core/README §5). The test programs coverage.py runs have their own defect: M382.

### M314. Round 2 left an unused local in begin_kind_card and a stale sentence in yrec_reset's header

- **Status:** fixed in round 2's last closing commit, "core: M314 and M274's last comments: begin_kind_card's unused local, three stale headers" (2026-11-13). Found by the round's closing agent while checking core/README.md against the code. Kind A: compare_decks --set all ALL IDENTICAL, 35 pins.
- **In the original F77?** No: both follow from round 2's changes (C-8 and C-7).
- **Now:** `begin_kind_card`'s local `chosen_dt`, under the comment "compute_timestep's output this caller does not use" ([run_driver.f90:330-331](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/8d7feee2/src/core/run/run_driver.f90#L330-L331)); yrec_reset's header, "At every entry after the first it also tells the step/diagnostics routines to re-initialize their SAVEd locals" ([yrec_reset.f90:9-11](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/8d7feee2/src/core/run/yrec_reset.f90#L9-L11)).
- **What is wrong:** since C-8 `compute_timestep` takes the star alone, so `chosen_dt` is set by nothing and read by nothing; since C-7 and the merge's leftovers commit, nothing tells the step to re-initialize saved locals (`evolve_step` has none, and the flag is gone).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** no dead declarations; comments describe the code as it is.
- **What we did:** the local and its comment deleted; the header says that at a re-entry the prologue closes the units the last run left open.
