### M315. A deeper envelope refit of the starting model was always refused: each refit step had its own loop index (a round-2 regression)

- **Status:** fixed in [2de1d79e](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/2de1d79e) (2026-11-14, round 2B, its first core agent), outside core's B list. Found by the agent's count of the shipped decks for M293 (hand-back §5, item 1). None of the 56 decks refits deeper: compare_decks `--set all` ALL IDENTICAL, 35 pins, before and after the fix; 32 shipped decks outside the set ask for one.
- **In the original F77?** No. STARIN found the shell and refit at it with one index `I` ([starin.f:491-502](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/starin.f#L491-L502)):
  ```fortran
  	    DO 575 I = M-1,1,-1
  	       IF(HS(I).LT.HSEND)GOTO 580
   575        CONTINUE
  ...
   580        M = I + 1
  ```
  [6983b71f](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/6983b71f) (2026-11-12, round 2, "core/model: rezone's and read_starting_model's steps take their arguments; the mesh criteria as steps") made `rescale_and_refit_envelope`'s steps module procedures, which had shared their host's loop index `i`, and each declared its own.
- **Before the fix** (at [9059d0b1](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/tree/9059d0b1/src)): `find_shell_below_new_fit` found the shell in its own `i` and returned nothing ([starting_model.f90:801-809](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/9059d0b1/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L801-L809)); `rescale_and_refit_envelope` tested its own `i`, never set ([:739](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/9059d0b1/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L739)), and `interpolate_new_fitting_point` ([:830](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/9059d0b1/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L830)) and `set_new_last_shell_convection` ([:892](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/9059d0b1/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L892)) read theirs, unset too. gfortran -O2 -Wuninitialized, without the build's -finit-local-zero, flags the three reads.
- **What was wrong:** with -finit-local-zero the tested `i` was 0, so every refit to a deeper fitting mass (a requested log(m/M) below the model's) was refused as "ERROR IN SUBROUTINE STARIN / DESIRED ENVELOPE MASS ... TOO LARGE / ENVELOPE MASS NOT CHANGED", and the run went on with the model's envelope. 32 shipped decks ask for such a refit (M293's count, cards capped at 5 models): 23 of `examples/run_from_dbl_to_zams`'s ZAMS decks, `Test_m0300_feh0_noGS_ZAMS` to `Test_m3000_feh0_noGS_ZAMS`, and nine of testsuite's, `Test_m0p3feh+0p0GS98_{allard,base,scv,spot25,yaleeos}_ZAMS`, `Test_m0p3feh+0p0GS98_base_TAMS`, `Test_m1p0feh+0p0GS98_base_TAMS`, `Test_m1p0feh+0p0GS98_spot25_ZAMS` and `Test_m3p0feh+0p0GS98_std25_TAMS`.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the run fits its envelope at the mass the deck asks for, as the F77 did; a refusal belongs to a fitting mass inside the innermost shell.
- **What we did:** the shell index travels in `starting_model_state` (`fit_shell_index`), set by `find_shell_below_new_fit` and read by the three steps; `rescale_and_refit_envelope`'s unused `i` goes. Measured: the 56 decks ALL IDENTICAL, 35 pins; in the same count with the fix, the 32 decks refit ("NEW ENVELOPE MASS CALCULATED"), none refuses, and their results return to the refit their decks ask for. No test: the steps are private to `read_starting_model`; the -Wuninitialized compile is the check (no warning since).
- **Now:** `find_shell_below_new_fit` sets `sm%fit_shell_index` ([starting_model.f90:823](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1592edca/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L823)), which the refit tests ([:753](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1592edca/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L753)) and the two steps read ([:845](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1592edca/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L845), [:908](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1592edca/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L908)).

### M316. Two shipped decks stop at their first model: "blend_eos: beta = P_gas/P is not positive"

- **Status:** open in part. m3000gs98z040000_prems fixed (the convergence round, 2026-11-17): a limit on the Henyey correction, the control `solver_max_correction`, which the deck sets. m25000gs98z018804_Dbl stays open, diagnosed (below): its shipped starting model is the cause. Was: open, size unknown. Found by round 2B's first core agent (hand-back §5, item 2) in its count of the shipped decks for M293. Not caused by round 2B: both stop the same way before and after M86's fix. Neither deck is pinned or in compare_decks' set. Not on the B lists.
- **In the original F77?** Not determined: no F77 run. By the code, the F77 had the same test as a warning: EQSTAT2 wrote the point to the run log and went on with the negative beta ([eqstat2.f:126-134](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqstat2.f#L126-L134)):
  ```fortran
        BETA14 = CA3*(T**2)**2/P
        BETA = 1 - BETA14
        if(BETA .LT. 0d0) then
          write(ishort,*) 'EQSTAT2: BETA is negative: TL,PL,BETA,1-BETA',
       *        TL,PL,BETA,1D0-BETA
        endif
        BETAI = 1.0D0/BETA
  ```
  so the F77 did not stop at this point; the stop is M42's fix ([20d05da3](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/20d05da3), 2026-10-29). Whether the F77 met a negative beta on these decks, and what it did after, is not known. The import holds both decks' F77 forms (`examples/run_from_start_to_dbl/m25000gs98z018804_Dbl.nml1`; `examples/run_from_seed_to_start/m3000z0400start.nml1`) and their output models (`input/models/dbl/m25000gs98z018804_Dbl.first`, `input/models/start/m3000gs98z040000_prems.first`).
- **Now:** [examples/run_from_seed_to_start/m3000gs98z040000_prems.inlist](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1592edca/examples/run_from_seed_to_start/m3000gs98z040000_prems.inlist) and [examples/run_from_start_to_dbl/m25000gs98z018804_Dbl.inlist](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1592edca/examples/run_from_start_to_dbl/m25000gs98z018804_Dbl.inlist); the stop is `radiation_share`'s ([blended_eos.f90:211-217](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1592edca/src/eos/blended_eos.f90#L211-L217)).
- **What is wrong:**
  - m3000gs98z040000_prems, card 1 (a 2.8 Msun seed rescaled to 3 Msun, X = 0.659, Z = 0.04, then evolved), stops at its first model, at log T 15.70, log P 12.56, beta = -4.3e35, exit 1; its history holds model 1's row only.
  - m25000gs98z018804_Dbl, card 1 (its starting model evolved), stops at its first model, at log T 6.94, log P 13.06, beta = -0.24, exit 1, after three "ENVINT: X0>XLIM" retries of the envelope integration's starting density.
  - Neither point is a model's (log T 15.7 is no star's); each is a state the first step's solution reached on its way. Like M294, not traced.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a shipped deck runs to its stop.
- **What we did:** recorded, not traced; the first agent's runs are in the work directory's `scratch_b2_core1/sweep/` (`dbg_*.txt`). Proposed: find which solve reaches the point (the rescale, the envelope integration or the Henyey iteration) and whether the deck's inputs (the seed, Z = 0.04's tables, a 25 Msun model's radiation pressure) are the cause; with O3's convergence work if it is the solver.
- **What we did (the convergence round, 2026-11-17):** traced both (the work directory's `notes/CONV_DIAGNOSIS.md`, section 3). In both it is the Henyey iteration that reaches the state, by applying most of a correction of a dex or more; M42's stop is right (there is no gas pressure to solve for at the point).
  - **m3000gs98z040000_prems.** Model 1 converges (9 iterations). In model 2 the second iteration asks for d log T = -0.98 and d log R = -0.31 at the centre, of which 0.65 is applied; the third then has a temperature residual of 1.5e3 at shell 34 and asks for d log T = +5.6e3, and the next linearization meets beta < 0. Fix: a new control, `solver_max_correction` (`&physics`; 0 = no limit, the default): no corrector pass changes log P, log T or log R of any shell by more than it; a larger correction is scaled down to it, the luminosity's by the same factor (`set_henyey_correction_factor`; the run log's F shows the factor applied). The deck sets 0.1 and runs to its stop: 5 models, 1130.56 yr (the age of the F77's model of this deck, `startmodels/start/m3000gs98z040000_prems.first`), log L 1.85367 against the F77's 1.82270, log Teff 3.66365 against 3.66572 (its sibling m3000gs98z060000_prems, which always ran, differs from its F77 model by the same: 1.776 against 1.748). Limits of 0.05 to 0.2 give the same five models; 0.3 still fails. The default is 0 so that no deck that ran takes the new path: measured on the 56-deck set and the 35 pins against M357's snapshot, ALL IDENTICAL. `test_correction_limit.py` (new, in CI's list): the deck as shipped reaches its five models, and with the limit set to 0 stops with the error.
  - **m25000gs98z018804_Dbl.** The first iteration of the first model asks for d log P = -0.15 at every shell, d log T = -3.4 at the centre and dL = -6e4 Lsun (the surface's 9.0e4). The shipped starting model (`startmodels/start/m25000gs98z018804_prems.first`, the F77's, model 80, timestep 3.4e-3 yr) is hydrostatic to 1e-7 but in a deuterium flash: at the first iteration, before any correction gives eps_grav a value, its luminosity equation's residual is 2.5e5 Lsun in one pair of shells (3.0e4 for the 22.5 Msun sibling, which converges). The correction limit does not help (the later iterations ask for d log T of +-5e3: the Newton direction is useless from that state). With a starting model made by the current code's own `examples/run_from_seed_to_start/m25000gs98z018804_prems` (which runs, 45 models) the deck's first model converges (first corrections 1.6e-2) and it runs past model 300 (8.8e3 yr, log L 4.83, log Teff 4.13), where an envelope vertex's gray atmosphere meets beta = -4e-4 at log T 4.127, log P 1.91: the outer layers of a 25 Msun star at the Eddington limit. The F77 ran the deck (its output is `startmodels/dbl/m25000gs98z018804_Dbl.first`, 15 models on), with its EOS going on at a negative beta wherever it met one. Open, for the authors: whether the shipped massive starting models are regenerated with the current code, and what a model does at a super-Eddington atmosphere.

### M317. The solar starting models' total mass and the decks' solar mass differ by 5.0e-5

- **Status:** open, size small. Found by round 2B's second core agent (hand-back §5, item 1) while measuring O22: the profile's atmosphere points and the pulse files' took g from the two different masses. Not on the B lists. Not traced further.
- **In the original F77?** Yes, in its constant and its data: SETUPS set `CMSUN = 1.9891D33` ([setups.f:82](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/setups.f#L82)), and the shipped solar starting models store a total mass of 10^33.2986347831 = 1.98900e33 g with a stellar mass of 1.0. Whether an F77 output used both was not traced.
- **Now:** `solar_mass_cgs = 1.9891d33` ([controls_buffer.f90:452](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/83b30640/src/io/controls_buffer.f90#L452)); the profile's atmosphere points read `s%star_mass` ([stitched_model.f90:669](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/83b30640/src/core/diagnostics/stitched_model.f90#L669)), the pulse files' `s%log_total_mass` ([:827](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/83b30640/src/core/diagnostics/stitched_model.f90#L827)).
- **What is wrong:** a 1 Msun model read from those files has `log_total_mass` 33.2986347831 but `star_mass` × `solar_mass_cgs` = 1.9891e33 g, 5.03e-5 more. Anything that converts between the two (the profile's atmosphere g, the seismic scalings, a rescale to a mass in Msun) is off by that much.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** one mass for one star: the model's total mass in grams and its mass in Msun agree through the deck's solar mass.
- **What we did:** recorded. Proposed: find where `star_mass` is set from a model read and whether it should be `10**log_total_mass / solar_mass_cgs`; a measured change (every deck that reads these models).

### M318. A devel or debug build on x86 Linux stopped at the first model's output: the GYRE interval's mod by 0

- **Status:** fixed after round 2B (2026-11-14). Found by CI's devel-tests job on the round's push ([f0ed5045](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/f0ed5045), run 43630095755, Ubuntu x86-64): `test_run_contracts`, back in the battery since [9bef8fb0](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/9bef8fb0) took O4's four known failures out, stopped with "Program received signal SIGFPE" at `io/yrec_output.f90:222` in its first model step.
- **In the original F77?** No. The F77 has no GYRE interval. [9df62b7e](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/9df62b7e) (2026-08-20, before the divergence, "Add GYRE-format periodic pulsation output") added `if (pulse_gyre_interval.gt.0 .and. mod(model_number,pulse_gyre_interval).eq.0)` to WRTOUT, and the test moved with it to `output_write_model`.
- **Before the fix** (at [f0ed5045](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/tree/f0ed5045/src)): [yrec_output.f90:222-224](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/f0ed5045/src/io/yrec_output.f90#L222-L224):
  ```fortran
        if (s%control%pulse_gyre_interval > 0 .and. &
            mod(s%model_number,s%control%pulse_gyre_interval) == 0) &
             call write_interior_gyre(s, output, ierr)
  ```
- **What was wrong:** Fortran does not require `.and.` to skip its second operand when the first is false, and at -O0 gfortran 15 does not: it computes the mod, then combines the two tests (checked in the generated code). The devel and debug build modes have no -O (`src/Makefile`'s `MODE_FFLAGS_devel` and `GNU_DBG_FFLAGS`), and `pulse_gyre_interval`'s default is 0, so every model's output divided by 0. On x86-64 an integer division by 0 raises SIGFPE whatever the floating-point trap flags say; on arm64 it gives 0 and nothing is raised, which is why the local devel battery, on macOS/arm64, passed. A devel or debug build on x86 Linux could therefore not run a deck past its first model. Release builds (-O3) test the interval first: CI's solar-regression job and the users' Linux runs were not affected. Before round 2B the devel battery's one full run, `test_run_contracts`, was skipped as an O4 known failure, so CI never reached this line.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a deck runs under every build mode on every platform; a guard on a divisor must be a test of its own, not an operand of the same `.and.`.
- **What we did:** two nested tests, with a comment saying why ([yrec_output.f90:225-229](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/yrec-next/src/io/yrec_output.f90#L225-L229)). A scan of `src` for any statement that pairs `.and.` or `.or.` with `mod`, or with a division by a name the same statement tests against 0, found no other: the five other such `mod`s divide by 2 or by a parameter, or (`settling_substeps.f90`) are a real mod, which the local floating-point traps would catch (a deliberate 1/0 under the devel flags stops with SIGILL on the owner's macOS/arm64 machine). Measured: compare_decks `--set all` ALL IDENTICAL, 35 pins. No new test: CI's devel job running `test_run_contracts` is the check, and no local one can see it (arm64 does not trap an integer division by 0, and gfortran's `-fsanitize=integer-divide-by-zero` does not instrument Fortran).

## 19. Found in the eighth evaluation (2026-11-17)

The eighth evaluation (`audit/module-evaluation-8-2026-11-17/`) reviewed the six packages that rounds 0 to 2B worked on, at [1179afbf](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/1179afbf), and scored each (`SUMMARY.md`): atm, convection, element_diffusion, eos, kap and core (two reports, `core_a.md` and `core_b.md`). Besides their scores and their style and structure points, the six reports listed 59 new findings. These items are the defects and the stale or inexact texts among them, in the reports' order: core (M319-M333), eos (M334-M337), kap (M338-M344), atm (M345-M347), convection (M348-M351) and element_diffusion (M352-M355), all open. Each entry records what is wrong, the input that triggers it, the proposed fix, its kind (A, byte-identical on every deck and pin; B, a change of results or of pinned text) and its size (S, M or L, the reports').

- **How they were checked.** The reviewers read only and ran nothing. Every item was read again in the code at 1179afbf, and against the F77 at 6cd56739, before its entry was written; each entry's status says how it was checked. Run for the registration, on a scratch build of 1179afbf (`scratch_eval8/` in the work directory: `t_cond.f90`, `t_kurucz.f90`, `t_region.f90`, `deckscan.py`): the conductive opacity at X = 1, Z = 0 without ionization (M340) and its density derivative against centred differences (M341); the Kurucz lookup below a row's first valid column of `atmk1990p00.tab` (M345); the settling region and its grid's size for a helium-rich core (M354); and counts over the 1,198 shipped deck files (M319, M326, M338). No deck was run, so what the B fixes would move is not measured. Where the check corrected a report (a line, a number, a claim), the entry gives the corrected account and says so.
- **One entry for one defect.** The Allard and gray switch is core_a's finding 3 and atm's finding 2: M321. The docs-only and stale-text findings are grouped per package: core's in M333, with its messages in M332; eos's in M337; kap's in M344; atm's in M347; convection's in M351; element_diffusion's in M355.
- **Left out**, by section 10's rule: the reports' style and structure points (unnamed values, unused imports, loose intents, formulas written twice, long positional interfaces, `pure`, untested drivers and checks without a mutation). `SUMMARY.md`'s "What is left under 8" carries them as work lists, and `FINDING_MAP.md` names each. The convection report's finding 9 is not a new item: two stale rows of docs/TARGET_ARCHITECTURE.md, corrected with this registration, and M308's status, corrected in its entry (fixed by [ebf4d507](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/ebf4d507)).
- **element_diffusion** is frozen by the owner's decision of 2026-11-11: M352-M355 are recorded for the round that takes up its B list, and nothing is proposed for now.
- Current-code links point at [1179afbf](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/tree/1179afbf/src).

### M319. An accreting, disk-locked model older than the disk-locking age takes one step of negative length

- **Status:** fixed in round 3 (2026-11-18, [bb90b076](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/bb90b076), the core1 agent; byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins: no deck meets it, cm_accretion's disk-locking age is 1e5 Gyr). At the registration: open. The core_a evaluation's finding 1, confirmed by reading (no run). Latent for the shipped decks: one accretes, `src/tools/compare_decks/cm_accretion.inlist`, and its `disk_locking_age_gyr` is 1e5 Gyr (a count over the 1,198 deck files). Kind B for a deck that triggers it; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: MDOT clips the step to the disk-locking age without testing that the model is younger ([mdot.f:74-77](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/mdot.f#L74-L77)):
  ```fortran
        IF(LDISK .AND. DMDT.GT.0.0D0)THEN
           TEST = SAGE + 1.0d-9*DELTS/CSECYR
           IF(TEST.GT.TDISK)THEN
              DELTS = (TDISK-SAGE)*1.0D9*CSECYR
  ```
- **Before the fix** (at the registration): `apply_mass_change`'s `limit_mass_change_timestep`, [mass_change.f90:477-483](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/step/mass_change.f90#L477-L483); the mass change from the step, [:419-420](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/step/mass_change.f90#L419-L420); the switch-off after it, [:135](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/step/mass_change.f90#L135); the composition step and the age, [step_driver.f90:283-297](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/step/step_driver.f90#L283-L297); rotation's step, [:523](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/step/step_driver.f90#L523); the age the test reads, set at a model read ([starting_model.f90:372](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L372)) and after each converged model ([step_driver.f90:508](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/step/step_driver.f90#L508)); the control's default, 0 ([controls_buffer.f90:1087](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/io/controls_buffer.f90#L1087)).
- **What is wrong:** with accretion (`mass_accretion_rate > 0`) and `disk_locking_active`, a step that would pass `disk_locking_age_gyr` is set to `(disk_locking_age_gyr - disk_gate_age_gyr)*1e9*seconds_per_year`. Nothing tests that the model is younger than that age. For a model that is older (a run started from a model saved after the disk-locking age, or the age left at its default 0), the step is negative, by the model's age less the disk-locking age:
  - `delta_mass_cgs` is negative, so the "accretion" removes mass, and with rotation takes the wind's angular momentum branch;
  - `evolve_step` runs the composition step with the negative step, sets the age back to the disk-locking age and hands rotation the negative step;
  - the mass change then switches off (`disk_exhausted`), so one step is affected.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a model past the disk-locking age has no disk left to accrete from: the mass change is off and the timestep untouched.
- **Proposed at the registration:** in `change_mass`, when accretion is on with disk locking and `disk_gate_age_gyr >= disk_locking_age_gyr`, switch the mass change off and return before the rate is used; the limit and the clip as a small kernel (rate, masses and ages in; dt and `disk_exhausted` out) with a check in test_mass_change and its mutation.
- **What we did:** round 3 (2026-11-18, [bb90b076](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/bb90b076), on [b46af438](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/b46af438)'s kernels): `change_mass` asks the new kernel `disk_has_dispersed` (core/step/mass_change_kernel.f90) first: at or past the disk-locking age the mass change is switched off before anything changes, and the timestep is left alone; the limit and the clip are kernels (`mass_change_timestep_limit`, `clip_step_to_disk_locking_age`). test_mass_change gains two checks (the gate at, past and before the age; a younger model's clipped step is not negative), mutations mass_change-20 and -21, both caught. Byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins (`--set all` on the commit).

### M320. A non-positive luminosity at the core edge gives a negative burning limit, which becomes the next timestep by its magnitude

- **Status:** fixed in round 3 (2026-11-18, [94497de3](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/94497de3), the core1 agent; byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins: no deck meets it). At the registration: open. The core_a evaluation's finding 2, confirmed by reading (no run); whether a shipped deck meets the trigger was not checked. Kind B where it fires, byte-identical otherwise; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: XTIME and YTIME divide by the core edge's luminosity ([xtime.f:38](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/xtime.f#L38), [ytime.f:82](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/ytime.f#L82); the report cites ytime.f:68), and HTIMER takes the minimum and then the magnitude ([htimer.f:141](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/htimer.f#L141), [:178](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/htimer.f#L178)):
  ```fortran
  	    DELTSY = (5.85D17/CLSUN)*DELTSY*(HS1(JCORE)/HL(JCORE))
           DELTS = MIN(DELTS,DELTSH,DELTSY,DELTSW,PDELT,EDELT)
        DELTS = ABS(DELTS)
  ```
- **Before the fix** (at the registration): `hydrogen_burning_limit`'s core branch, [timestep_limits.f90:250-251](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/step/timestep_limits.f90#L250-L251), and `helium_burning_limit`'s, [:320-321](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/step/timestep_limits.f90#L320-L321); the helium shell branch's test of L, [:325](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/step/timestep_limits.f90#L325); `tightest_timestep`, [:395-404](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/step/timestep_limits.f90#L395-L404); the magnitude, [timestep_control.f90:92](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/step/timestep_control.f90#L92); the one check of a non-positive L, the shell's ([expected_test_timestep_limits.out:29](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/test/expected_test_timestep_limits.out#L29)).
- **What is wrong:** the core branches of the hydrogen and helium limits are proportional to `enclosed_mass(core_edge)/luminosity(core_edge)`, with no test of the luminosity's sign. With L <= 0 at the core edge (the centre, when there is no convective core: a core whose neutrino losses exceed its heating, or one that expands), the limit is negative. `tightest_timestep` takes `minval`, so the negative value beats every other limit and the growth limit, and `compute_timestep` makes it positive with `abs`, which is there for a stored model's negative step. The next timestep is then |E dX m/L|, arbitrarily long for a small |L|. L = 0 gives +Inf, which loses the minimum (and traps in a devel build).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a limit that cannot be formed sets no limit (`dt_unlimited`), as the helium shell branch does for L <= 0.
- **Proposed at the registration:** `dt_unlimited` where the core edge's L is not positive, in both kernels, each with a check and a mutation in test_timestep_limits; in `compute_timestep`, `abs` on the stored step only (the branch that skips the limits).
- **What we did:** round 3 (2026-11-18, [94497de3](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/94497de3)): `hydrogen_burning_limit` and `helium_burning_limit` return `dt_unlimited` where the core edge's L is not positive, as the helium shell branch did; `compute_timestep` takes the magnitude of a stored model's negative step only, in the branch that skips the limits. test_timestep_limits gains two checks (without the fix the hydrogen limit is negative and the helium one +Infinity), mutations timestep-36 and -37, caught. Byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins (`--set all` on the commit).

### M321. An Allard deck whose gravity leaves the tables while its Teff stays inside switches to gray and back at every model, with a new triangle each time

- **Status:** open. The core_a evaluation's finding 3 and the atm evaluation's finding 2, one defect, confirmed by reading (no run); whether a shipped deck reaches it was not checked (the 116 Allard decks are low-mass main-sequence and pre-main-sequence stars; no pinned log holds either message). Kind B for a deck that reaches it; size M.
- **In the original F77?** Partly. The two tests are the F77's: ENVINT latched the gray atmosphere when the lookup failed on Teff or on log g ([envint.f:146-153](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/envint.f#L146-L153)), and SURFBC switched back on Teff alone ([surfbc.f:75-77](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/surfbc.f#L75-L77)):
  ```fortran
           IF(LAlFail) then
              KTTAU=0
              LTTAU = .TRUE.
  ...
           ELSE IF(KTTAU0.EQ.4.AND.TEFFL.LT.AL_TEFFLmax)THEN
              KTTAU = KTTAU0
              LTTAU = .FALSE.
  ```
  The new triangle at each switch back is 2026's (S12's fix, [67d711a7](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/67d711a7)).
- **Now:** the lookup's failure, [atm_lib.f90:189](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/atm_lib.f90#L189); the kernel's fallback, [envelope_integration_kernel.f90:368-385](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L368-L385); the latch and its note, [envelope_integration.f90:176-180](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration.f90#L176-L180), [:354-359](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration.f90#L354-L359); the switch back, `switch_atmosphere_choice` ([surface_boundary.f90:137-150](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/structure/surface_boundary.f90#L137-L150)) through `on_gray_fallback` ([:31-34](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/structure/surface_boundary.f90#L31-L34)) and `atm_reenters_table` ([atm_lib.f90:246-251](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/atm_lib.f90#L246-L251), [:254-261](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/atm_lib.f90#L254-L261)); atm/README's sentence, [README.md:31](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/README.md#L31).
- **What is wrong:** two parts of the code decide when an Allard run is on the gray atmosphere, by different tests. The lookup fails for a log Teff above the tables, a log g outside them, or a log g outside a stencil row's range, and `atm_get` then sets `atm_choice_in_use` to gray. `switch_atmosphere_choice` switches back whenever the run is on the fallback and log Teff is below the tables' last row, whatever log g is, and a switch back starts a new triangle. So for an `atm_choice = 4` model whose log g is outside the tables while its Teff is inside (the Nextgen2 rows reach down to log g 1.5 or 2.0: a star on the red giant branch), every `compute_surface_boundary` switches back with its note, starts a new triangle, fails the first vertex's lookup again with atm's message and core's "note: Allard table lookup out of range; switching to a gray atmosphere", and integrates three envelopes where an unchanged triangle needs none. The run log gains three lines per model, and the boundary condition is refitted from a fresh triangle at every model. atm/README says the kernel integrates the gray relation "for that integration"; core's comment says "for this and all future calls"; neither describes the flip.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** one test for both directions: a point the lookup would refuse stays gray, and the run returns to the tables only when a triangle about the model would be inside them.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: an `atm_reenters_table(choice, log_teff, log_g)` that asks the kernel's range and stencil tests without a message, for the model and for the triangle's vertices; the kernel's own fallback then never fires in a run and can become an error. A check in test_atm (a point inside in log Teff and outside in log g does not re-enter), a unit test of the switch on a synthetic table range, and one sentence in atm/README section 2.
- **Round 3 (2026-11-18):** the core2 agent's B list item 1, the exact fix (no patch: atm_lib and structure/ had no owner this round): `atm_reenters_table(atm_choice, log10_teff, log10_gravity)` returns what `atm_get_surface_pt` would decide, without a message (for Allard, `interpolate_allard_surface` on the point and `.not. (teff_above .or. gravity_outside .or. row_outside > 0)`; for Kurucz the present Teff test); `switch_atmosphere_choice` returns to the deck's choice only when the model and the three vertices of a fresh triangle about it re-enter, and leaves the table when any vertex about to be integrated is outside; the kernel's own fallback (`find_table_surface`'s `allard_lookup_failed` branch) becomes an error, and `switched_to_gray` goes. Expected to move nothing in the 56 decks: none of the 57 baseline logs holds "switching to a gray atmosphere", an Allard out-of-range line or a switch note. Since [19dc8e8a](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/19dc8e8a) test_envelope_integration checks the tabulated surface and the fallback to gray on a synthetic Allard-layout file, through the kernel and through `atm_get`.

### M322. The envelope kernel reads locals that nothing set: they are zero only under gfortran's -finit-local-zero

- **Status:** fixed in round 3 (2026-11-18, [d2ad07ac](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/d2ad07ac), the core2 agent; byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins). At the registration: open. The core_a evaluation's finding 4, confirmed by reading (no run: a build without the flag is the fix's check). No effect in the GNU builds, where every run is the same. Kind A; size S.
- **In the original F77?** No, in this form: ENVINT had a blanket `SAVE` ([envint.f:108](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/envint.f#L108)), so the values were the previous integration's. The `SAVE` went in [1c510cc5](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/1c510cc5) (2026-08-22).
- **Before the fix** (at the registration): `integrate_envelope_atmosphere`'s locals `prev_tau`, `prev_opacity`, `prev_density` ([envelope_integration_kernel.f90:309-310](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L309-L310)), read at the first atmosphere point by `store_atmosphere_gradients` ([:656-663](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L656-L663)); `find_atmosphere_start`'s copies into `eos_res` before `eos_get` ([:461-482](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L461-L482)); the flag, [Makefile:124](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/Makefile#L124), and the Intel builds' flags without one, [:200-210](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/Makefile#L200-L210); the fully ionized solver's start from the record's density, [yale_eos.f90:785-788](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/eos/yale/yale_eos.f90#L785-L788).
- **What is wrong:**
  - `store_atmosphere_gradients` reads `prev_tau`, `prev_density` and `prev_opacity` at the first atmosphere point, before anything sets them. Its comment says the build's `-finit-local-zero` makes them zero, so that the first point's depth step is measured from tau = 0 with rho kappa = 0.
  - `find_atmosphere_start` copies 22 scalars into `eos_res` before the first `eos_get` of every integration; only `temperature` has a value then. (Corrected from the report, which calls the density "the density the EOS starts from": the Saha solver starts from the record's `saha_*` fields; only the fully ionized solver starts from the record's density, when it is not the default 0.)
  - With gfortran's flag the values are zero. The Makefile's ifort and ifx builds have no such flag: there the first `atmo_delta_depth`, from which the stitched model's atmosphere radii are built, and the record's inputs are stack contents. The devel builds keep the flag, so no test sees it. bug_sweep has this class for kap and eos (M104, M107, M223), not for core.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the code sets what it reads; a result does not depend on a compiler flag.
- **Proposed at the registration:** `prev_tau`, `prev_density` and `prev_opacity` set to zero at the start of the atmosphere integration; `eos_res` kept between tries (it is the host's variable) and the 44 lines of copies deleted, or the scalars zeroed at entry. Byte-identical under the GNU builds; confirm with a build without `-finit-local-zero` and with `-finit-real=snan`.
- **What we did:** round 3 (2026-11-18, [d2ad07ac](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/d2ad07ac)): `integrate_to_photosphere` starts `prev_tau`, `prev_density` and `prev_opacity` at zero; the 44 lines of copies around `eos_get` are gone (the record is the host's and keeps its values between tries, which is what they amounted to); `num_ok`, `num_bad`, `y`, `err_sum` and `mass_diff_remaining`, which the thin envelope's event also read unset, start at zero; since [a6ad2d7f](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/a6ad2d7f) every field of `integration_state` has a default of zero. Check: test_envelope_integration, "depth: the first step is measured from tau = 0" (and "depth: each step is dtau over the mean rho kappa"), with a mutation each. Confirmed with the kernel compiled under `-finit-real=snan`: before the fix the first check prints NaN FAIL, after it the report is byte-identical to the normal build's. Byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins.
- **Corrected (2026-11-18, round 3):** the first `atmo_delta_depth` enters no height of the stitched model: `accumulate_atmosphere_heights` sums the steps from the second on ([stitched_kernels.f90:43-55](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/core/diagnostics/stitched_kernels.f90#L43-L55)). What the unset locals could reach was the stored `atmo_delta_depth(1)` itself and the record handed to the EOS. Beyond the entry's list, the thin envelope's event read `num_ok`, `num_bad`, `y(1)`, `err_sum(2:3)` and `mass_diff_remaining` unset when a table gave the surface or no envelope was integrated (set in the same commit).

### M323. Accretion's entropy path is dead, but its atmosphere lookup and two EOS calls can still stop the run

- **Status:** open. The core_a evaluation's finding 5, confirmed by reading; the report's Stahler temperatures recomputed (log T 3.35 at 1e-9 Msun/yr on a solar-size star, 2.60 at 1e-12). Kind B (the EOS's carried state may move cm_accretion at round-off); size M.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: MASSLOSS's "experimental code ... valid for Allard atmospheres only" looks the surface up, calls EQSTAT twice and sets the entropy to zero on both branches ([massloss.f:136](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/massloss.f#L136), [:169-172](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/massloss.f#L169-L172)); MDOT leaves the mass term out too ([mdot.f:101-103](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/mdot.f#L101-L103)):
  ```fortran
              SCEN = 0.0D0
  C            SCEN = SACC2 - SACC
           ELSE
              SCEN = 0.0D0
  ```
- **Now:** `change_mass`, [mass_change.f90:118-128](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/step/mass_change.f90#L118-L128): `average_envelope_energies` ([:196-251](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/step/mass_change.f90#L196-L251)), `find_accreted_surface_state` ([:258-302](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/step/mass_change.f90#L258-L302)), `evaluate_stahler_surface` ([:307-336](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/step/mass_change.f90#L307-L336)), then the zero ([:127](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/step/mass_change.f90#L127)); `adjust_cz_for_accreted_entropy`, [:490-541](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/step/mass_change.f90#L490-L541); the members `delta_log_temperature` and `delta_log_pressure` in the structure equations, [structure_equations.f90:162-169](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/structure/structure_equations.f90#L162-L169).
- **What is wrong:** for accretion, `change_mass` computes the convection zone's mean thermal energy and entropy, looks up or integrates the surface the accreted matter joins (an Allard lookup, or since round 2B a gray atmosphere integration), calls the EOS there, and calls it again at Stahler's surface pressure and temperature. Then it sets the entropy to zero, so every shift `adjust_cz_for_accreted_entropy` applies is zero, and `new_thermal_energy` is "not used further"; the comments say so at each place. The results are read by nothing, but a failure ends the run: an Allard lookup below the tables, the gray integration, or either EOS call (a Saha non-convergence has been an error since M293). Stahler's temperature is far below a photosphere's for small rates.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a step does not fail in work whose result it discards.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed (O5 and O7, fixed in round 2B, are this path's live parts). Proposed fix: a measured commit that moves the path to step/retired/ with a header: `average_envelope_energies`' entropy sums, `find_accreted_surface_state`, `evaluate_stahler_surface`, `adjust_cz_for_accreted_entropy`, and the members `delta_log_pressure` and `delta_log_temperature` with their use in the structure equations. Measure cm_accretion.
- **Round 3 (2026-11-18):** `change_mass` keeps the path's three steps (`average_envelope_energies`' entropy sums, `find_accreted_surface_state`, `evaluate_stahler_surface`) as internal procedures, apart for the retirement ([b46af438](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/b46af438)). Measured in scratch (the core1 agent's B list B2; the three calls removed, nothing else, `scratch_r3_core1/patches/B_m323.patch`): 0 of the 18 quick decks move, cm_accretion included, so the EOS's carried state does not move it; the retirement as proposed is then likely Kind A, to confirm with `--set all` on the full patch. Recommended: retire it to `step/retired/accretion_entropy.f90.txt`.

### M324. The turnover time's innermost-point branch is overwritten by the bottom cell's crossing time (a 2026 regression, recorded in August and never registered)

- **Status:** open. The core_b evaluation's finding 1, confirmed by reading the code and the F77's nesting; which decks take the branch was not measured. Kind B (every model that takes it); size S.
- **In the original F77?** No. The bottom-cell code is inside the `ELSE` of the test, so the first branch kept its value ([tauintnew.f:142-147](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/tauintnew.f#L142-L147), [:192](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/tauintnew.f#L192), [:230-231](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/tauintnew.f#L230-L231)):
  ```fortran
           IF(VALTEST.GT.0.0)THEN
  ...
              TAUCZ = PSCA/CVEL
           ELSE
  ...
    110       CONTINUE
  ...
              TAUCZ = DELR/CVEL
    140       CONTINUE
           ENDIF
  ```
  The goto elimination ([7b8c2e1d](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/7b8c2e1d), 2026-08-22) made label 140 a flag that only the spline path sets. The first bug sweep found it ([atm_net_math.md:65-82](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/audit/bugsweep-2026-08-31/atm_net_math.md#L65-L82); [ROADMAP.md:457-460](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/docs/ROADMAP.md#L457-L460), "goto-elimination regression"); it got no number here and was not fixed.
- **Now:** `turnover_from_interior_new`, [turnover_timescale.f90:215-223](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/diagnostics/turnover_timescale.f90#L215-L223); `time_scale_height_above_base`'s first branch and its comment, [:345-353](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/diagnostics/turnover_timescale.f90#L345-L353).
- **What is wrong:** when the convection zone's innermost point already lies more than one pressure scale height above the interpolated base (`val_test > 0` at `cz_base_index`: a thin zone, or a coarse mesh there), `time_scale_height_above_base` sets the turnover time to H_P/v_c there and leaves `spline_taucz_done` false. `time_bottom_cell_crossing` then runs and overwrites it with the bottom cell's width over v_c at its middle, another quantity. The comment says so ("This leaves spline_taucz_done false, so time_bottom_cell_crossing runs next and overwrites the result") instead of fixing it. The value feeds the wind's Rossby number and the deuterium cap of the next step, and the history column.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the F77's: a unique zone is timed at H_P/v_c, also when its innermost point is the place.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: `spline_taucz_done = .true.` in the first branch (the flag then wants the name `timescale_done`); a check on a synthetic profile in a turnover test, with this as its mutation; a measurement of which decks take the branch.
- **Round 3 (2026-11-18):** now in `turnover_walk.f90`, `time_scale_height_above_base` ([e18b04f7](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/e18b04f7)): the innermost-point branch calls `time_innermost_point` and returns with `timed` false; the fix is `timed = .true.` after that call. test_turnover's check "innermost point above H_P: the bottom cell's crossing time (M324)" holds today's value; with the fix its expected value is `scale_height_time`, and its mutation turnover_walk-06, which is the fix, becomes its inverse.
- **Corrected (2026-11-18, round 3):** "Kind B (every model that takes it)" is Kind A for the shipped decks: measured in scratch (the core3 agent's patch `scratch_r3_core3/patches/M324_fix_and_count.patch`, which also counts each time the branch is taken), `--set all` ALL IDENTICAL, 35 pins OK, and the counter fires in none of the 56 decks. It can go in as an A commit with test_turnover's new expected value.

### M325. Each card's first step runs with the turnover time zeroed after the starting model computed it

- **Status:** open. The core_b evaluation's finding 2, confirmed by reading (no run). It acts at the first step of every card; what it moves was not measured. Kind B (decks with a deuterium cap in a surface convection zone, and rotating decks whose wind law reads the turnover time); size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. The 2002 zero stayed in MAIN after the 2017 initialization went into STARIN ([starin.f:905-907](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/starin.f#L905-L907), called at [main.f:290](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L290); then [:412-414](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L412-L414)):
  ```fortran
        CALL GETTAU(HCOMP,HR,HP,HD,HG,HS1,HT,FP,FT,TEFFL,
       *            HSTOT,BL,M,LC,ENVR)
        TAUCZ0 = TAUCZ
  ...
  C MHP 08/02 STORE STARTING CZ PROPERTIES
           JCZ = JENV
           TAUCZ = 0.0D0
  ```
- **Now:** `read_starting_model` computes the turnover time and its step-start copy, [starting_model.f90:193-199](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L193-L199); `begin_kind_card` zeroes the current member after it, [run_driver.f90:384-387](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/run/run_driver.f90#L384-L387); the readers during the step: the deuterium cap ([burn_step.f90:82-83](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/step/burn_step.f90#L82-L83), [:699](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/step/burn_step.f90#L699); [structure_equations.f90:138](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/structure/structure_equations.f90#L138); `cap_deuterium_rate`, [reaction_rates.f90:201](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/net/reaction_rates.f90#L201)) and the wind ([evolve_rotation.f90:438-441](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/rotation/evolve_rotation.f90#L438-L441); [magnetic_braking.f90:580-584](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/rotation/magnetic_braking.f90#L580-L584)); the refresh at the step's end, [step_driver.f90:652-659](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/step/step_driver.f90#L652-L659); the header that says otherwise, [turnover_timescale.f90:29-30](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/diagnostics/turnover_timescale.f90#L29-L30).
- **What is wrong:** nothing computes the turnover time again before the card's first step ends. During that step the deuterium cap reads the current member, finds 0 and is off (`turnover_timescale <= min_cap_turnover_time` returns), and the wind interpolates between the start value and the end value 0: half the starting model's turnover time at the step fraction 0.5. In every later step the two members are equal, so the first step of each card is the only one that differs, on every card, a card that continues the model in memory included.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the starting model's value stands in both members until the first step replaces it, as STARIN's initialization meant.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: drop the assignment in `begin_kind_card`, and correct turnover_timescale.f90's header, which says the mid-step readers take the `_prev` copies (the deuterium limiter reads the current member). A measured commit.
- **Round 3 (2026-11-18):** measured in scratch, not committed (the core1 agent's B list B1; patch `scratch_r3_core1/patches/M325_drop_turnover_zero.patch`: the zero in `begin_kind_card` and its four comment lines go; turnover_timescale.f90's header lines on the readers corrected). `--set all` at e4fcec1a plus the patch: 8 of the 56 decks move, 5 of them pinned, all rotating (the wind reads the turnover time; no non-rotating deck moves, so the deuterium cap's first step changes no result in the set). cm_rot_base, cm_rot_settle_he and cm_rot_solid: 22 models both, log L 1.140137 -> 1.140135, the first model's total J 4.53327e49 -> 4.53318e49; Test_solarGS98_difrotmixper18p4d0p1: 854 both, log L -0.000044 -> -0.000043; Test_solar_GS_rot_gray_OPALSCV_SF2_GS98_OP_CF10: 454 -> 453 models, log L 0.000261 -> 0.000256; the 3 Msun rotating TAMS deck 2.145662 -> 2.145658; rv_nodisk -0.138874 -> -0.138871; o24_rescale_rotating -0.146107 -> -0.146818 (age 0.13693 -> 0.13006 Gyr: path-sensitive, a mixed region one shell deeper at log line 6013). The first card's starting J moves at the 2e-5 level (the wind's first step), and the rest follows. Recommended: make it (`notes/R3_B_LIST.md`). Since [5cf0a168](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/5cf0a168) the starting model's turnover time is `begin_kind_card`'s call (`initialize_turnover_timescale`), right after `read_starting_model`.

### M326. The core extension divides 0 by 0 for one added point, the default factor's case, and never shifts the density profile

- **Status:** fixed in part in round 3 (2026-11-18, [adf2900e](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/adf2900e), the core3 agent; byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins): the one-point case and the control check; open: the density shift (B). At the registration: open. The core_b evaluation's finding 3, both parts confirmed by reading (no run). Latent for part a: all 213 shipped deck files that set `extend_core_inward` set `core_mass_reduction_factor` to 10 (a count over the 1,198 deck files), which gives 13 points. Kind A for part a and a control check (only runs that now give NaN change); B for the density shift. Size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes, both ([starin.f:375](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/starin.f#L375), [:390-401](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/starin.f#L390-L401) with no `HD`, [:405-409](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/starin.f#L405-L409)):
  ```fortran
            MCORE = INT(DLOG10(FCORE)/HPTTOL(2))+1
  ...
            RHOC = HD(1)
            DEL = (HT(2)-HT(1))/(HP(2)-HP(1))
            FACD = HP(MP1)-HD(MP1)-HT(MP1)
  ```
- **Now:** `extend_core_toward_center`: the count, [starting_model.f90:605-606](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L605-L606); the shift, [:620-632](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L620-L632); the gradient and the density offset, with the comment that names the 0/0, [:635-648](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L635-L648); the new points' density, [:683-684](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L683-L684); the defaults, factor 1.0 ([controls_buffer.f90:1203](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/io/controls_buffer.f90#L1203)) and spacing 0.08 ([controls_buffer.f90:548](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/io/controls_buffer.f90#L548)).
- **What is wrong:**
  - **Part a.** The number of points added is N = `int(log10(core_mass_reduction_factor)/chi_grid_scale(ichi_dm_max)) + 1`: 1 for any factor below 10^0.08 = 1.20 at the default spacing, the control's default of 1.0 included, so `extend_core_inward = .true.` alone gives it. With N = 1 the shift copies old point 1 into slot 2 and leaves slot 1 as it was, so `actual_gradient = (logT(2)-logT(1))/(logP(2)-logP(1))` is 0/0 and the new centre's log T is NaN. The comment says it ("for N = 1, slot 2 has already been overwritten and del is 0/0"). io checks neither control.
  - **Part b.** The shift moves log m, log R, L, log P, log T, the flags, the composition and omega, and not log rho ("logRho is not moved"). After an extension by N points, `logRho(k)` for N < k <= nz is the density of old point k, N points further out than the rest of point k, and the top N points hold whatever the array held beyond the old model (the report does not say this last part). `density_estimate_offset` combines the old innermost point's P and T with old point N+1's density. The displaced profile stands until the first structure solve stores a density; the starting model's stitched profile and its turnover walk read it meanwhile.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** every profile of a point moves with the point, and a control value that cannot work is refused when the deck is read.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: take the central density, the gradient and the luminosity from the two innermost old points before the shift (identical for N >= 2); refuse `core_mass_reduction_factor <= 1` with `extend_core_inward` in io's `check_controls`; shift log rho with the rest, in a measured commit (the decks whose first card ages a model it reads with the extension).
- **Round 3 (2026-11-18):** on [a586a4e0](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/a586a4e0)'s kernel `core_extension.f90`, [adf2900e](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/adf2900e) reads the central density, the gradient and the innermost luminosity from the two innermost old points before the points move (the same values as before for two added points or more), and refuses `extend_core_inward` with `core_mass_reduction_factor` not above 1 where the control is used (`extend_core_toward_center`: "ERROR: core extension: extend_core_inward needs core_mass_reduction_factor above 1 (it is ...); run stopped", ierr = 1). test_model_kernels: one added point takes the old points' gradient (NaN before: mutation starting_model-01), thirteen points, a factor of 1 refused. Left: the check belongs in io's `check_controls` (io was not in round 3).
- **The density shift, measured in scratch (round 3, the core3 agent's B list; `scratch_r3_core3/patches/m326_density.patch`, `s%logRho(i+num_added) = s%logRho(i)` in the loop that moves the old points):** every deck that extends the core moves from its first model, 29 of the 56 (the 12 testsuite solar decks, the 15 rv_ decks, o24_rescale_rotating, a run_standard_solar_model deck), 13 pins. On 6 decks (all moved, 3 pins): the first model's log L by 1.3e-3 to 1.7e-3 dex (Test_solarGS98_base 0.799058 -> 0.797402); at 4.568 Gyr Test_solarGS98_base log L 0.000094 -> 0.000086, log Teff 3.761358 -> 3.761357, 822 -> 821 models; Test_solarGS98_dif 0.000054 -> 0.000061; Test_solarM22M_dif 0.000119 -> 0.000121; the rotating decks' starting J by 1.3e-5 (rv_basic unchanged to six decimals at its end, rv_ref log L -0.137502 -> -0.137506, o24_rescale_rotating -0.146107 -> -0.145598, path-sensitive). Recommended: make it.

### M327. The stitched model swallows an envelope-integration failure after its ERROR line

- **Status:** fixed in part in round 3 (2026-11-18, [0f352187](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/0f352187), the core3 agent; byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins: no compared deck fails there); open: the owner's choice between the stop and a warning (B). At the registration: open. The core_b evaluation's finding 4, confirmed by reading (no run; the pins would show whether a deck fails there). Kind A where no deck fails there, B for a run that now continues past the error. Size S.
- **In the original F77?** No: the stitched model is 2026's, and these lines came with [b116224d](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/b116224d) (2026-08-25).
- **Now:** `build_stitched_model`, [stitched_model.f90:174-183](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/diagnostics/stitched_model.f90#L174-L183); its header, which promises `ierr = 1` only for a missing column, [:96-102](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/diagnostics/stitched_model.f90#L96-L102); the errors `atm_get` reports, [envelope_integration.f90:379-382](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration.f90#L379-L382), [:416-419](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration.f90#L416-L419).
- **What is wrong:** the stitch re-integrates the envelope and atmosphere at the converged model with the fixed output steps. When `atm_get` fails (the output step sizes needing more steps than the kernel allows, an EOS or opacity failure inside a step, an underflowing step), the stitch keeps the interior alone and returns `ierr = 0`:
  ```fortran
        if (jerr /= 0) then
           s%stitched%n_ie = s%stitched%n_ext
           call fill_stitched_arrays(s, ierr)
           return
        end if
  ```
  `atm_get` has reported the failure by then, so the run prints an ERROR line and goes on: that model's profile and pulse files have no envelope or atmosphere, `photosphere_logP` keeps the previous model's value, and the turnover walk runs on the interior.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** core/README section 3: "a procedure that can fail returns ierr". An error that was reported stops the run, or is a warning that says what the output lacks.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: return `jerr` (a positive code stops the run with exit 1, the negative one ends it as the solver's does); or, if an interior-only stitch is wanted for a model whose envelope cannot be output, a warning that says so and the fallback in the header.
- **Round 3 (2026-11-18):** `build_stitched_model` still fills the interior-only grid and now returns `atm_get`'s code, so a positive one stops the run and `envelope_termination` ends it as the solver's does; its header says so ([0f352187](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/0f352187)). test_stitched builds the stitched model with an atmosphere step that needs more than the kernel's 2000 steps and gets ierr = 1 (mutation stitched_model-07). No compared deck prints an envelope-integration ERROR (a grep of the 56 baseline logs and terminal outputs), so all are byte-identical. Left for the owner: a run that used to go on past that ERROR line with interior-only profile and pulse files now stops at that model; the alternative is a warning ("the output envelope failed; this model's files hold the interior alone") with ierr = 0. The agent recommends the stop (core/README §3: a reported error stops the run).

### M328. The star calibration reports a crossing at the second model of every pass when the model starts above R*

- **Status:** fixed in round 3 (2026-11-18, [30e79cdc](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/30e79cdc), the core1 agent; byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins: no deck calibrates to a star). At the registration: open. The core_b evaluation's finding 5, confirmed by reading (no run). Kind A (a calibration that starts below R* is unchanged: its second model is stored without a crossing either way); size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: SETSCAL's `ALRI = 0` ([setscal.f:58](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/setscal.f#L58)), MAIN's skip of the first model ([main.f:919-926](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/main.f#L919-L926)) and CHKSCAL's two tests ([chkscal.f:52-66](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/chkscal.f#L52-L66)):
  ```fortran
        IF(ALR.GT.ALRI) THEN
           IF(.NOT.(ALR.GT.SR.AND.ALRI.LE.SR)) THEN
  ```
- **Before the fix** (at the registration): `setup_star_calibration`'s `r_rsun_prev_model = 0`, [calibration.f90:507](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/run/calibration.f90#L507); `check_star_calibration`'s tests, [:243-259](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/run/calibration.f90#L243-L259); the skip at each even card's first model, [stop_conditions.f90:169-176](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/run/stop_conditions.f90#L169-L176).
- **What is wrong:** the check is skipped at each even card's first model, so nothing stores that model, and at the second model the "previous radius" is the 0 of the setup. If the model's radius is above R*, the test `r_current > target .and. r_prev <= target` holds: the calibration reports "Just passed R*" and interpolates log L and the age between this model and (R = 0, with log L and age as the star's members were left). The crossing path does not store the model either, so the next pass's second model does the same: every pass ends at its second model, until card 50's "NOT converged". The header says the check works for a crossing "in either direction"; a track that starts above R* and contracts to it (a pre-main-sequence target) can never be calibrated.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** each pass compares models of its own track, from its first model on.
- **Proposed at the registration:** at the first model of an even card, store that model's L, age and radius as the previous model (a small `store_calibration_model(s)` that `check_stop_conditions` calls instead of skipping); a check in test_run_contracts, a pass that starts above R* and crosses it downward.
- **What we did:** round 3 (2026-11-18, [30e79cdc](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/30e79cdc)): the first model of each even card is stored as the previous model (`store_calibration_model`, which `check_star_calibration` also uses for a model that did not cross), so a pass compares models of its own track from its first model on; a calibration that starts below R* is unchanged. The radius is one function (`model_radius_rsun`); stop_conditions takes the cards per cycle from calibration. test_run_contracts gains three checks through `check_stop_conditions` (no crossing at the second model of a pass that starts above R*; the downward crossing between its own models at the interpolated age; the next pass starts from its own first model), mutations calibration-10 to -12, caught. Byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins.

### M329. The turnover walk's three-shell test reads the convective flags beyond the walk's last point

- **Status:** fixed in round 3 (2026-11-18, [1a231147](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/1a231147), the core3 agent; byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins). At the registration: open. The core_b evaluation's finding 6a, confirmed by reading. Kind A; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes ([tauintnew.f:90](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/tauintnew.f#L90)):
  ```fortran
        IF(.NOT.(LCZ(IMAX).AND.LCZ(IMAX+1).AND.LCZ(IMAX+2)))THEN
  ```
- **Before the fix** (at the registration): the test, [turnover_timescale.f90:196-203](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/diagnostics/turnover_timescale.f90#L196-L203); the caller's json-sized locals, filled up to `num_points` only, [:47-51](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/diagnostics/turnover_timescale.f90#L47-L51), [:76-87](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/diagnostics/turnover_timescale.f90#L76-L87); the scan that finds the base, up to `num_points`, [:250-256](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/diagnostics/turnover_timescale.f90#L250-L256).
- **What is wrong:** the test reads `convective_flag(cz_base_index+1)` and `(+2)`. A base found at the walk's last or next-to-last point reads elements that nothing set: `.false.` under gfortran's `-finit-local-zero` (the walk then ends as a radiative envelope), undefined without it, and outside the array when `num_points` is json.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a point beyond the walk's last is not part of the model.
- **Proposed at the registration:** treat a point beyond `num_points` as radiative; a case with a zone at the walk's last points in the turnover test M324 proposes.
- **What we did:** round 3 (2026-11-18, [1a231147](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/1a231147), in [e18b04f7](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/e18b04f7)'s kernel `turnover_walk.f90`): the three-shell test, the restart after it and the scan's start read the flags through `convective_at`, for which a point beyond the walk's last is radiative. test_turnover walks 38 of 40 points with convective flags beyond the walk and gets no zone; without the guard it times a zone of four points (mutation turnover_walk-16). Byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins.

### M330. The rezone adds a point outside the outer one without testing the arrays' size

- **Status:** fixed in round 3 (2026-11-18, [dfe22f68](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/dfe22f68), the core3 agent; byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins). At the registration: open. The core_b evaluation's finding 6b, confirmed by reading. Latent: it needs a model of exactly json (5000) points whose surface is hotter than `rezone_env_logt1`, whose default is 9.0 ([controls_buffer.f90:620](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/io/controls_buffer.f90#L620)). Kind A; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes ([hpoint.f:103-104](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/hpoint.f#L103-L104)):
  ```fortran
        ELSE IF(HT(M).GT.TENV1.AND.ISTORE.NE.0) THEN
  	 M = M + 1
  ```
- **Before the fix** (at the registration): `check_envelope_temperature_range`, [rezoning.f90:197-201](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/model/rezoning.f90#L197-L201); the test the other steps make, [:631](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/model/rezoning.f90#L631), [:736](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/model/rezoning.f90#L736), [:829](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/model/rezoning.f90#L829).
- **What is wrong:** `s%nz = s%nz + 1` with no test against json, where `place_points_along_chi` and the two jump steps test and stop. A model of json points that takes the branch writes element json + 1 of seven arrays.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the same "needs more than json" error as the other steps.
- **Proposed at the registration:** that error, before the increment.
- **What we did:** round 3 (2026-11-18, [dfe22f68](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/dfe22f68)): `check_envelope_temperature_range` reports "ERROR: rezone: the new mesh needs N points, more than json" and returns ierr = 1 before it adds a point to a model of json points. test_model_kernels calls it on a star of json points (mutation rezoning-02). Byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins.

### M331. A NULL path from a C host reaches strlen

- **Status:** fixed in round 3 (2026-11-18, [8bbe4ce7](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/8bbe4ce7), the core1 agent; byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins). At the registration: open. The core_b evaluation's finding 6c, confirmed by reading. The documented interface is not affected: the header offers empty strings for the defaults, and pyyrec passes them. Kind A; size S.
- **In the original F77?** No: the C entry is 2026's, and its `strlen` test came with M271's fix ([350c9186](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/350c9186), 2026-11-12).
- **Before the fix** (at the registration): `yrec_run`, [yrec_capi.f90:58-59](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/run/yrec_capi.f90#L58-L59); the header's "Empty strings fall back to the CLI defaults", [:15](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/run/yrec_capi.f90#L15).
- **What is wrong:** `c_strlen` is called on both arguments before anything else, so a C host that passes NULL for "use the default" crashes there.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** an entry point for C hosts takes the idiom C hosts use, or refuses it with a status.
- **Proposed at the registration:** `c_associated` first, a NULL read as an empty path.
- **What we did:** round 3 (2026-11-18, [8bbe4ce7](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/8bbe4ce7)): `yrec_run` reads a NULL pointer as an empty string (`c_string_length` tests `c_associated` first), which the entry takes as the default deck name. test_run_contracts checks that `yrec_run(NULL, NULL)` returns what `yrec_run("", "")` returns (capi-10, caught: the mutant crashes). Byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins. Found on the way: an empty path does not give the default deck name the header promises when the host was started with arguments (M384).

- **Round 3 (2026-11-18), step/ and run/ (core1):** step_driver's three stale comments (the divergence stop's message, `structure_change_limit`, the rates of change `dlog_temperature_dt` and its siblings) corrected; shell_physics' doubled banner and calibration's header list corrected ([3e8be5b8](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/3e8be5b8)); the timestep recipe's missing lines and two new recipes (a kernel with its test program, a stage of the step), each traced in a scratch copy, are in core/README.md §6.
- **Round 3 (2026-11-18), model/ and diagnostics/ (core3):** observables' header and `renormalize_luminosity_breakdown`'s (what it writes and who reads it; [0ea2528f](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/0ea2528f), [5cf0a168](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/5cf0a168)); turnover_timescale's header (the deuterium limiter reads the current member; [e18b04f7](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/e18b04f7)); the stray second contract pairs under `read_starting_model` and `rezone` ([5cf0a168](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/5cf0a168), [d23918da](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/d23918da)); model_rescaling's `find_shell_boundaries` and `card_z_ramp_*` names ([fceae36c](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/fceae36c)); starting_model's `model_diverged_flag`, the read step's "sets the total mass", the always-true test ([5cf0a168](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/5cf0a168), [a586a4e0](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/a586a4e0)); `rezoning_theta_term.f90.txt`'s branch ([d23918da](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/d23918da)); `n_pulse_cols = 35`: column 35 is a spare, no writer reads it ([0ea2528f](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/0ea2528f)).
- **Round 3 (2026-11-18), the README:** core/README.md's mutation sentence now says what the manifests show (each mutation caught by the check it names, per program), and the coverage figures are the agents' measures of 2026-11-18 (§5), merged by the closing commits. ### M334. The MHD reader reads a composition record past its arrays before it checks the count, and every failure has one anonymous message

- **Status:** open. The eos evaluation's finding 1, confirmed by reading. Latent: no MHD tables ship. Kind A; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes to both: RABU reads the count and that many triples in one statement and tests after ([rabu.f:16-20](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/rabu.f#L16-L20)), and MHDST1's stops are bare:
  ```fortran
        READ(IR   ) NCHEM,(ATWT(IC),ABUN(IC),ABFRCS(IC),
       1       IC=1,NCHEM),GASMU
        IF(NCHEM0.LT.NCHEM) THEN
           STOP
  ```
- **Now:** `rabu`, [mhd_table_reader.f90:346-351](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/eos/mhd/mhd_table_reader.f90#L346-L351); the columns it fills, 6 elements each ([mhd_eos_tables.f90:90-92](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/eos/mhd_eos_tables.f90#L90-L92), `mhd_nchem0` at [:27](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/eos/mhd_eos_tables.f90#L27)); `read_mhd_tables`' one message, [:45-51](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/eos/mhd/mhd_table_reader.f90#L45-L51).
- **What is wrong:**
  - `rabu` reads `num_chem` and, in the same statement, that many triples; the test `nchem0 < num_chem` comes after. A table whose header says 7 elements or more writes past the three 6-element columns it was handed (into the next composition's column, or the next component of `mhd`) before `ierr = 1` comes back; under `-fcheck=all` it is a bounds stop.
  - Whatever fails in `mhdst`, `mhdst1`, `rabu` or `rtab` (the file holds 22 `ierr = 1` statements; the report counts 17 sites), the user reads "eos_init: an MHD table is corrupt or does not match its layout": not which of the eight files, and not which check (the variable count, the table kind, the composition flag, the companions' X spacing or T grids, the sizes, a short record).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a reader checks a count before it reads by it, and an error names the file and the check (M136's and M291's rule).
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: read the count alone, check it, `backspace` and read the record; `mhdst1`, `rabu` and `rtab` return a reason code and `read_mhd_tables` writes one line with the file and the reason; a test_eos check with a 7-element synthetic header.

### M335. Two table-shape assumptions that no eos reader checks: SCV rows that never shorten with T, and one T6 grid for the first OPAL block's columns

- **Status:** open. The eos evaluation's finding 2, confirmed by reading. Latent: the shipped tables satisfy both (the report's count of the SCV H table: 63 rows of 30 to 76 points, never shorter with T); only a user's table can trigger it. Kind A; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: SETSCV and READCOEOS check neither.
- **Now:** the SCV reader's row checks, [scv_table_reader.f90:75-107](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/eos/scv/scv_table_reader.f90#L75-L107); `find_scv_cell`'s columns "at the cell's first row (the one with the fewest points)", [scv_eos.f90:752-753](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L752-L753); the edge weight's step from the first row, [:116-118](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L116-L118), beside the parameter `scv_min_log10_gas_pressure` ([:44](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L44)); the OPAL reader's comparison of a later block with the first, [opal_table_reader.f90:229-235](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/eos/opal/opal_table_reader.f90#L229-L235), and the one grid the interpolation uses, column 1's ([:140](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/eos/opal/opal_table_reader.f90#L140)).
- **What is wrong:**
  - SCV: the lookups bound a cell's columns by the count of its first row and then read rows idtt+1 to idtt+3 at those columns. That holds only if the rows' point counts never fall as T rises. The reader checks 4 <= npts <= 76 and that the He and Z tables share the H table's grid (M136), not that `nptsx` is non-decreasing, that `tlogx` increases, or that a row's first log P_gas and its step are the first row's. A table with a row shorter than the one below gives a density from entries never read, with ierr = 0.
  - OPAL: a later X block's rows are compared with the first block's, column by column (M291), but within the first block column j's T6 rows are never compared with column 1's, whose grid the interpolation uses for every column.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a reader refuses a table whose shape the lookup does not handle (M136, M291).
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: in `read_scv_rows`, ierr = 1 with the row named when a row is shorter than the one before, a log T does not increase, or a row's first log P_gas or step differs from the first row's; in `read_table_blocks`, each T6 compared with column 1's once column 1 is in. One test_eos check each.

### M336. SCV's envelope-table path and its general path interpolate the same tables two ways: up to 5e-4 dex in log rho at the composition where one hands over to the other

- **Status:** open. The eos evaluation's finding 3, confirmed by reading; the size is the test's own tolerance and comment, not measured here. Kind A to state it, B to make the paths one (size S; M).
- **In the original F77?** Yes: EQSCVE hands over to EQSCVG at the same tolerance.
- **Now:** the handover, [scv_eos.f90:235-240](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L235-L240), at `scv_composition_tolerance` = 1e-5 ([:44-45](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L44-L45)); the test that accepts the difference, [test_eos.f90:1793-1795](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/eos/test/test_eos.f90#L1793-L1795), [:1816-1817](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/eos/test/test_eos.f90#L1816-L1817); "Kept by decision", which names O2 only, [README.md:94](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/eos/README.md#L94).
- **What is wrong:** a zone within 1e-5 of the envelope's X and Z gets the envelope table through a natural spline with smoothing across cells; a zone farther off gets the three tables through 4-point Lagrange interpolation without smoothing. The two are not the same function of (T, P): test_eos accepts them 5e-4 dex apart in log rho and records 3e-4 at log T 4.13. So the density steps by that much where a zone's composition crosses the tolerance, and c_P and grad_ad are built differently on the two sides. It can matter where a zone under SCV differs from the surface: below a settling envelope in a deck without OPAL, or outside the OPAL table. No list says so.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** one equation of state at one (T, P, X, Z), or a statement of the step where there are two.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed: first the statement (eos/README section 3's "Kept by decision") with the measured size over the SCV-only decks; then a decision: one interpolation for both paths (the general path through the same spline and smoothing, the envelope table kept as its cache), a measured change.
