### M338. kap's copy of the envelope Z is the run plan's at kap_init and never follows the model, so a single-Z OPAL 1992 or LAOL 1989 deck is refused at its first interior lookup

- **Status:** fixed in round 3 (2026-11-18, [4486bdfb](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/4486bdfb), the kap agent; byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins). At the registration: open. The kap evaluation's finding 1, confirmed by reading (no run). Latent: no shipped deck file sets `use_opal92_tables` or `use_laol89_tables` (a count over the 1,198 deck files), and OPAL 1995 skips the test. Kind A for the shipped decks; size S.
- **In the original F77?** No. GETOPAC compared with the live ZENV of COMMON /COMP/, which STARIN set from the model and RSCALE on a rescale ([getopac.f:101-102](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/getopac.f#L101-L102)):
  ```fortran
        ELSE IF((Z.GT.0.12D0) .OR. ((ABS(Z-ZENV) .GT. OPTOL)
       *   .AND..NOT.L2Z .AND. .NOT.LOPAL95))THEN
  ```
  The copy came with [50f40772](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/50f40772) (2026-08-21), which gave the EOS a setter for the places the mixture changes, and kap none.
- **Before the fix** (at the registration): `kap_init` stores its argument, [kap_lib.f90:293-294](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/kap_lib.f90#L293-L294), in the state's member ([opacity_tables.f90:276-279](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/opacity_tables.f90#L276-L279)); `interior_opacity`'s test, [:186-193](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/kap_lib.f90#L186-L193); the caller passes the star's member, [settings_install.f90:72-73](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/setup/settings_install.f90#L72-L73); the run plan sets that member only for a card with a positive rescale Z, [run_setup.f90:57-67](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/run/run_setup.f90#L57-L67); the model's Z arrives later, with a call that tells kap the X alone ([starting_model.f90:1201-1213](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L1201-L1213)), and a Z rescale tells the EOS alone ([model_rescaling.f90:200](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/model/model_rescaling.f90#L200), [settings_install.f90:140-147](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/setup/settings_install.f90#L140-L147)); `kap_update_surface_tables` takes no Z ([kap_lib.f90:398-415](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/kap_lib.f90#L398-L415)).
- **What is wrong:** `interior_opacity` refuses a zone whose Z differs from kap's copy by more than `metal_fraction_match_tolerance` (1e-8) when the interior family has one table and does not interpolate in Z (OPAL 1992 or LAOL 1989 without `use_two_z_tables`). Nothing updates the copy after `kap_init`, when the star's envelope Z is the run plan's: unset (0 in a fresh process) unless a card rescales Z. So such a deck, without a Z ramp or Z diffusion and without a card that rescales Z to the model's own Z, fails at its first interior lookup ("no interior opacity at Z = ...: the OPAL 1992 table is at the envelope's Z = 0.00000"), and a deck whose second card rescales Z fails the same way after it. test_kap passes the table's Z as the envelope Z in every configuration.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the F77's: the test compares a zone with the envelope Z the model has now.
- **Proposed at the registration:** give kap the envelope Z where it changes (a `kap_set_envelope_z`, or `kap_update_surface_tables(X, Z, ierr)`, called from `install_surface_x_settings` and `install_surface_z_settings`), and drop the argument from `kap_init`. A test_kap check: a single-Z OPAL 1992 load, the envelope Z moved, a lookup at the new Z succeeds and one at the old Z returns ierr. (The "read-time envelope Z" question of section 1's decisions is about the same member.)
- **What we did:** round 3 (2026-11-18, [4486bdfb](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/4486bdfb)): `kap_lib` gains `kap_set_envelope_metal_fraction`, and setup's `install_surface_z_settings` calls it beside `eos_set_mixture`, so kap's envelope Z follows the run plan's Z, the first card's model and a Z rescale; `kap_init` keeps its argument (the run plan's Z is installed before it). test_kap: "kap_set_envelope_metal_fraction: one Z table serves the new Z only" (a single OPAL 1992 table at 0.0188, the envelope moved to 0.02: a zone at 0.02 has an opacity, one at 0.0188 returns ierr), mutation `envelope-z-follows`; check_boundaries lets only settings_install call the setter. Not run end to end: no shipped deck uses OPAL 1992 or LAOL 1989. Byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins.

### M339. OPAL 1995's surface table puts the X = 1 − Z table at X = 1, and at Z = 0.04 or 0.10 reads an X = 0.95 slot that was never built

- **Status:** fixed in round 3 (2026-11-18, [dc2f0912](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/dc2f0912), the kap agent; byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins). At the registration: open. The kap evaluation's finding 2, confirmed by reading against the 3D path's stencil. Latent: it needs an envelope X above 0.8 (Y below 0.2 − Z), a pure-hydrogen or test composition. Kind A for the shipped decks; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: OP95XTAB took its nodes from XXG, whose tenth entry is 1.0 ([op95xtab.f:44-72](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/op95xtab.f#L44-L72); [ll95tbl.f:37-38](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/ll95tbl.f#L37-L38)), where GETOPAL95 took `A(4) = 1.0D0 - ZZ` ([getopal95.f:385](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/getopal95.f#L385)); its `ZTAB.LE.0.04D0` and "USE TABLES 6-9" branches are the same. Round 1 fixed this defect in Alexander 2006 (M225).
- **Before the fix** (at the registration): `build_opal95_surface_table`, [opal95_opacity.f90:203-233](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/opal95/opal95_opacity.f90#L203-L233); `grid_x(10)` = 1.0, [opacity_tables.f90:153-155](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/opacity_tables.f90#L153-L155); the reader's check that the tenth table is at X = 1 − Z, [opal95_reader.f90:65-69](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/opal95/opal95_reader.f90#L65-L69); the fixed-Z table builds slot 9 only below Z = 0.04, [:129](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/opal95/opal95_opacity.f90#L129); the 3D and 4D paths' stencil, which has it right, [:509-543](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/opal95/opal95_opacity.f90#L509-L543).
- **What is wrong:** the surface table interpolates the fixed-Z table in X with the nodes `grid_x(...)`. For an envelope X above 0.8:
  - X > 0.9 at Z below 0.04: tables 7-10 with nodes 0.8, 0.9, 0.95, 1.0, where the fourth table is at 1 − Z (0.98 at Z = 0.02);
  - 0.04 < Z < 0.10: tables 6, 7, 8 and 10 with the fourth node 1.0, where the table is at 1 − Z (0.94 at Z = 0.06);
  - Z = 0.04 exactly (the first branch's `<=`) or Z = 0.10 (the "tables 6-9" branch): the stencil takes slot 9, which is built only below Z = 0.04, so it holds the initial zeros.

  `locate_opal95_x_stencil` sets the fourth node to 1 − Z and drops the tables that do not exist. So at such a composition the 2D path (every zone at the surface composition) and the 3D path a hair off it disagree, with ierr 0. test_kap's "the new 2D path is the old 3D path" checks X = 0.65 only.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** one X stencil at a Z for every path: the tables that exist, the node 1 − Z.
- **Proposed at the registration:** build the surface table with `locate_opal95_x_stencil`'s rule (one routine for the X stencil at a Z), and extend the 2D-against-3D check to X = 0.92, and to Z = 0.06 with X = 0.85.
- **What we did:** round 3 (2026-11-18, [dc2f0912](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/dc2f0912)): one rule, `opal95_x_tables_at_z` (the X tables that exist at a Z and the X each is at, the tenth at 1 − Z), for the surface table's build and the 3D and 4D paths' stencils; the surface build keeps its own search for the first table, so an envelope X up to 0.8 gives the same table bit for bit. test_kap: the 3D path exact at a node of the X = 1 − Z table (X = 0.98, Z = 0.02); the rebuilt surface table against the 3D path at X = 0.92 (3.7e-4 before, 2e-16 after) and at Z = 0.06, X = 0.85 (4.0e-5 before); the 2D path against the 4D path at Z = 0.04, X = 0.85 (0.27 dex before). Mutations `opal95-x-1mz-node`, `opal95-surface-x-above-0.9`, `opal95-surface-x-weights`, `opal95-surface-no-x095`. (At X = 0.8 exactly and 0.04 <= Z < 0.10 the surface table now takes the lookups' tables 6, 7, 8, 10 where it took 5 to 8: the same value at a node.) Byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins.
- **Corrected (2026-11-18, round 3):** "never built" is the fixed-Z table's slot 9, which is built below Z = 0.04 only; the table files themselves hold an X = 0.95 table at Z = 0.04 (TABLE #114 of GS98.OP17), which no path uses (M378).

### M340. The conductive opacity is NaN with ierr 0 for a gas with no electrons (from M278's rewrite)

- **Status:** fixed in round 3 (2026-11-18, [d7bcc742](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/d7bcc742), the kap agent; byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins). At the registration: open. The kap evaluation's finding 3, confirmed by a run on a scratch build of 1179afbf (`t_cond.f90`): `compute_conductive_opacity` at log rho −3, log T 3.7, X = 1, Z = 0 and `ion_fraction` = 0 returns κ_c = NaN with `got_conductive_opacity` true and ierr 0; with Z = 0.02 it returns 7.87e6. Latent for the shipped decks (their Z is positive). Kind A; size S. **This is in the code round 2B changed:** the 0/0 came with M278's fix ([95ae332b](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/95ae332b), 2026-11-14).
- **In the original F77?** In another form. Its unnormalized weights gave log10(0), so κ_c = 0 and κ = 0 ([condopacpint.f:32-34](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/condopacpint.f#L32-L34), [:57](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/condopacpint.f#L57)):
  ```fortran
            CONDL = -LOG10(WtH1*CONDX + WtHe4*CONDY + WtOx*CONDZ)
  ```
  The 0/0 is M278's normalization.
- **Before the fix** (at the registration): the weights over `electron_sum`, and `electrons_per_amu`, [conductive_opacity.f90:125-134](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/conductive/conductive_opacity.f90#L125-L134); the shifted densities, [:150-155](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/conductive/conductive_opacity.f90#L150-L155); the mixture, [:173-174](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/conductive/conductive_opacity.f90#L173-L174); `eos_result`'s default `ion_fraction` = 0, [eos_results.f90:38](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/eos/eos_results.f90#L38).
- **What is wrong:** the weights are divided by `electron_sum` and each species' density is shifted by `log10(electrons_per_amu)`, with no guard. For Z = 0 and no ionized H or He (a neutral gas; `ion_fraction`'s default) both are 0: the weights are 0/0 and the shift is log10(0) (a trap under the devel flags). The routine returns NaN for κ_c with `got_conductive_opacity` true and ierr 0, which `add_conduction` turns into a NaN opacity. With Z > 0 the metals' term keeps the sum positive; a Z = 0 model with a cool, neutral surface would reach it.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a gas without electrons does not conduct: no conductive opacity, as outside the table's reach.
- **Proposed at the registration:** return `got_conductive_opacity` false when `electron_sum` is not positive; a test_kap check at X = 1, Z = 0, `ion_fraction` = 0, with its mutation.
- **What we did:** round 3 (2026-11-18, [d7bcc742](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/d7bcc742)): `compute_conductive_opacity` returns no conduction (`got_conductive_opacity` false, as outside the table's reach) when the electron sum is not positive, before the shares are divided by it; kap_eval then takes Hubbard & Lampe's fit where it applies. test_kap: "Potekhin conduction: none for a gas without free electrons" (X = 1, Z = 0, ion_fraction 0), mutation `conductive-no-electrons`. Byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins.

### M341. Where a species' shifted density is clamped at the conductive table's edge, the returned density derivative is not the value's (from M278's rewrite)

- **Status:** open. The kap evaluation's finding 4, confirmed by a run on a scratch build of 1179afbf (`t_cond.f90`), the returned dln κ_c/dln ρ against a centred difference of log κ_c (X = 0.7, Z = 0.02): −1.097 against −1.000 at log ρ −5.5, log T 4 with H 0.1% ionized; −1.113 against −1.000 with H 10% ionized; −1.077 against −1.017 at log ρ −5.95, log T 5, fully ionized; equal to five digits at log ρ −3 and −2. Kind B (round-off in κ's derivatives, where conduction is negligible); size S. **This is in the code round 2B changed:** each species' own density came with M278's fix ([95ae332b](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/95ae332b)).
- **In the original F77?** No: CONDOPACPINT read the three tables at the zone's density.
- **Now:** the comment and the clamps, [conductive_opacity.f90:144-155](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/conductive/conductive_opacity.f90#L144-L155); the derivatives, [:175-185](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/conductive/conductive_opacity.f90#L175-L185).
- **What is wrong:** each species' table is read at log ρ + log10((A/Z) Y_e), clamped into the table. The comment says "d log rho_i/d log rho = 1, so the derivatives keep their form", which is false where a clamp binds: K_i is then constant in ρ, but the returned derivative still subtracts the table's slope at the clamp. For hydrogen the shift is log10(Y_e) <= 0, so its density is clamped from log ρ = −6 up to −6 − log10(Y_e): about 0.1 dex for an ionized gas, several dex where hydrogen is partly ionized (3 dex at Y_e = 1e-3), which is the outer envelope of every deck. Conduction is negligible there (κ_rad/κ_c of 1e-9 to 1e-7, M299's figures), so κ's derivative moves at round-off. test_kap's two derivative checks are at a fully ionized point (log ρ 2.93) and below −6, neither in the band.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a returned derivative is the derivative of the returned value (test_kap's rule for every family).
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: with M299's fix, which rewrites these lines: drop a clamped species' slope from the weighted mean (or state the band in kap/README's "Kept by decision" beside M299's), and a derivative check at log ρ = −5.5 with a partly ionized mixture.
- **Round 3 (2026-11-18):** M299 and M341 measured together in scratch, not committed (the kap agent's B list item 1; patch `scratch_r3_kap/patches/m299_m341_trial.patch` in the work directory): below the table the branch takes the mixture's derivatives (the 1/K-weighted mean) as the branch inside it does, and `species_conductivities` returns a zero density slope for a species whose own density is clamped at the table's edge; the smooth end in place of the stop at log R = 0 (M299's second half) is not in the trial. On 24 decks (the 16 configuration-matrix decks, cm_accretion, Test_solar_noGS_norot, Test_solarGS98_base and _dif, the 0.03 Msun ZAMS deck, the 1 Msun pp deck, ZAHB, rv_basic) all 24 move, and their 20 pins: Test_solarGS98_base log L -1.1e-5 dex, log Teff -1.3e-6, 821 models for 822; Test_solarGS98_dif log L +1.9e-5, log Teff +6.0e-6, 817 for 816; Test_solar_noGS_norot +2.2e-11; the configuration-matrix decks 1e-12 to 5e-11; Test_m0030_feh0_noGS_ZAMS -6.9e-9; ZAHB 1.7e-12; rv_basic -5.1e-11. Largest column changes: Li7 59% (a trace abundance in cm_env_overshoot), logRho 1.8e-4 relative, the rest below 1.4e-6. Every deck moves because conduction is evaluated in every zone's mixture branch; the solar decks' 1e-5 is the convergence path (one model fewer or more). Recommended: adopt both parts as measured; decide the stop at log R = 0 separately (`notes/R3_B_LIST.md`).

### M342. The Alexander lookups extrapolate beyond their tables with ierr 0, where kap/README says kap_get returns ierr for a point off its tables

- **Status:** decided in round 3 (2026-11-18, [ea8c054a](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/ea8c054a), the kap agent): documented; the lookups stay as they are, because a refusal would stop a shipped deck. At the registration: open. The kap evaluation's finding 5, confirmed by reading; how far the decks' lookups go off the tables was not counted. Kind A for the README; a refusal is A only if no deck goes off the tables. Size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: GETALEX06 and YALO3D clamp the index and interpolate, with no range test and no STOP ([getalex06.f:26](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/getalex06.f#L26); [yalo3d.f:31-44](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/yalo3d.f#L31-L44)).
- **Now:** Alexander 2006's stencils and its linear extrapolation above the top log R only, [alex06_opacity.f90:199-227](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/alex06/alex06_opacity.f90#L199-L227), [:240-247](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/alex06/alex06_opacity.f90#L240-L247); `compute_alex94_opacity`, without an ierr or a message argument, [alex94_opacity.f90:124-125](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/alex94/alex94_opacity.f90#L124-L125), and `lookup_alex94`, which always returns 0, [:314-329](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/alex94/alex94_opacity.f90#L314-L329); the README's rule, [README.md:66](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/README.md#L66), and its statement of OPAL 1995's low side only, [:83](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/README.md#L83).
- **What is wrong:** the two Alexander families have no range test in log T or at low log R: the stencil is clamped to the last four nodes and the cubic Lagrange weights extrapolate (Alexander 2006 below log T 2.7 and below log R −8; only above the top log R is the extrapolation linear). `build_alex94_fixed_z_table` accepts any Z. OPAL 1995 extrapolates in log R without limit on both sides, which the README states for the low side only. So "`kap_get` returns ierr for a point off its tables" does not hold for the molecular families.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a README's error rule is true of every family, or names the exceptions (M208's reasoning for the Fermi-Dirac table).
- **Proposed at the registration:** either refuse a point more than one node step off the table in log T and log R, after a count over the 56 decks of how far the lookups go, or say in "Kept by decision" which families extrapolate, where and how, and correct the rule.
- **What we did:** round 3 (2026-11-18): counted with an instrumented build on 16 of the 56 decks, one or more of each kind: only the 0.03 Msun chain goes off a table, Alexander 2006 above its top log R (1.0): m0030gs98z018804_prems up to log R 2.98, m0030gs98z018804_Dbl 3.03, Test_m0030_feh0_noGS_ZAMS 3.79, at log T 3.37 to 4.00; no counted deck goes below Alexander 2006's first log R or log T, below OPAL 1995's first log R or past an OPAL 1995 row's last filled column. A refusal would stop a shipped deck, so kap/README's error rule now names the families that extrapolate instead of returning ierr, where and how ("Kept by decision", first item; [ea8c054a](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/ea8c054a)), and test_kap pins the rule above the Alexander tables' top log R ("linear from the last two", both families). The count found that the derivatives there are not the value's: M375. Byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins.

### M343. What kap_init still accepts: a table file whose Z is not the control's, a non-positive LAOL tolerance, a Kurucz 1990 file without rows, and no interior family

- **Status:** fixed in round 3 (2026-11-18, [493ebf1b](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/493ebf1b), the kap agent; byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins); (d)'s message corrected, and `kap_init` still accepts settings without an interior family, kept by decision (the other packages' tests boot with kap off). At the registration: open. The kap evaluation's finding 6, each part confirmed by reading. Latent: no shipped deck uses OPAL 1992, LAOL 1989 or two Z tables. Kind A; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes for (a) to (c): SETLLO reads GRIDZ and uses it for GRIDY alone ([setllo.f:54-55](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/setllo.f#L54-L55)); GTLAOL and GTPURZ take `LOG(TOLLAOL)` unchecked at each lookup ([gtpurz.f:31](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/gtpurz.f#L31)); SETKRZ's `IPUT.LT.1` test is inside its row loop, so a file without rows ends with `NUMTM = 0` ([setkrz.f:51-67](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/setkrz.f#L51-L67)). (d)'s message is 2026's.
- **Before the fix** (at the registration): `check_kap_settings`' three checks, [kap_lib.f90:344-389](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/kap_lib.f90#L344-L389); OPAL 1992's header Z, "a read-list target that is never used afterwards", [opal92_reader.f90:34-35](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/opal92/opal92_reader.f90#L34-L35), [:65](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/opal92/opal92_reader.f90#L65); LAOL 1989's `zlot` and `zhit`, [laol_reader.f90:78-80](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/laol89/laol_reader.f90#L78-L80), [:104](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/laol89/laol_reader.f90#L104); the tolerance's ln, [:51-52](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/laol89/laol_reader.f90#L51-L52), [:167](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/laol89/laol_reader.f90#L167); the Kurucz reader's row count, [kurucz_reader.f90:139](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/kurucz90/kurucz_reader.f90#L139); the order of `interior_opacity`'s tests, [kap_lib.f90:186-198](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/kap_lib.f90#L186-L198), and the unselected descriptor's name, 'none' ([opacity_source.f90:95](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/kap/opacity_source.f90#L95)).
- **What is wrong:**
  - (a) The Z a table file states is read and thrown away: `opal_table_z1/2` and `laol_table_z1/2`, the blend's abscissae, are never compared with it. A deck that pairs `Z0200.OPALN` with `opal_table_z1 = 0.0188` blends in Z from the wrong node, with ierr 0. The OPAL 1995 and both Alexander readers check every header against their grids.
  - (b) `laol_extrapolation_tolerance <= 0`: the pure-Z table of every deck takes its ln, a floating-point trap under the devel flags and no extrapolation otherwise.
  - (c) A Kurucz 1990 file with its header lines and no row: `num_temps = 0`, `kap_init` returns 0, and the run fails at the first molecular lookup.
  - (d) No interior family at all (without the pure-Z table): every lookup above the molecular window fails, and with M338 the message is the wrong one, since the Z test comes before `interior%selected`: "the none table is at the envelope's Z".
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a setting or a table that cannot work is refused at `kap_init`, with a message that names it (M236's rule).
- **Proposed at the registration:** compare the file's Z with the control's in the two readers (an error naming both); three lines in `check_kap_settings`; `num_temps == 0` an error in the Kurucz reader; `interior%selected` tested first in `interior_opacity`.
- **What we did:** round 3 (2026-11-18, [493ebf1b](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/493ebf1b)): (a) the OPAL 1992 reader (each X table's header) and the LAOL 1989 reader (zlot and zhit) compare the Z the file states with the control the table is for, through `opacity_table_files`' `table_z_differs`: an error naming both beyond 1e-4 (the files state Z rounded: Z01895.OPALN states 0.0190, Z0190AG91.DBGLAOL 0.01903); (b) the LAOL and pure-Z loads refuse a `laol_z_tolerance` that is not positive (`check_extrapolation_tolerance`); (c) the Kurucz reader refuses a file without rows; (d) `interior_opacity` tests `interior%selected` first, so the reason without an interior family is that. test_kap: five checks (the two table Zs and the no-family reason by their messages), mutations `opal92-table-z`, `laol-table-z`, `laol-tolerance`, `kurucz-no-rows`, `no-interior-family-first`.
- **Corrected (2026-11-18, round 3):** the proposed "three lines in `check_kap_settings`" were not the place: only a family knows it needs the LAOL tolerance, and a family that is selected but not first is not loaded, so the loads refuse it; and the table-Z test needs a tolerance, because the files state Z rounded.

### M345. The Kurucz and Castelli/Kurucz lookup has no per-row log g limit: a point below a row's first valid column is extrapolated with ierr 0

- **Status:** open. The atm evaluation's finding 1, confirmed by a run on a scratch build of 1179afbf (`t_kurucz.f90`, `atmk1990p00.tab`): 40 of the 51 rows at or below log Teff 4.5 start above log g 0; at log Teff 3.93 the stencil's rows 20 to 23 are valid from log g 1.0, 1.0, 1.5 and 1.5, and the lookup returns ierr 0 at log g 1.0 (log P 0.693), 0.5 (−0.032) and −0.4 (−0.323). Latent for the shipped decks: the 12 Kurucz decks are dwarfs and solar models, and no deck uses choice 5. Kind A for them (a deck that reaches it stops instead of extrapolating); size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: SURFP tests only `TEFFL.LT.3.5D0 .OR. GL.LT.-0.5D0` ([surfp.f:25](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/surfp.f#L25)), under a comment that promises to quit "MORE THAN ONE TABLE POINT FROM THE DATA", and takes "DESIRED LOG G BELOW 2ND TABLE ENTRY -USE FIRST 4 POINTS" ([surfp.f:104-116](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/surfp.f#L104-L116)).
- **Now:** `outside_table`, [kurucz_atmosphere.f90:99-110](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/tables/kurucz_atmosphere.f90#L99-L110); `pressure_in_row`'s top branches, [:133-152](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/tables/kurucz_atmosphere.f90#L133-L152), and its spline branch, [:155-173](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/tables/kurucz_atmosphere.f90#L155-L173); the Allard lookup's per-row limit, [allard_atmosphere.f90:125-128](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/tables/allard_atmosphere.f90#L125-L128).
- **What is wrong:** `outside_table` refuses log g < −0.5 for the whole table. Inside a row, a log g below the row's second valid column takes "the first four" valid columns and evaluates the natural spline there; numerics' `splint` continues its end cubic outside the nodes. So a point below the row's first valid column is extrapolated, down to log g −0.5, with ierr 0; above log Teff 4.5 the linear and 3-point branches do the same from the top two or three columns. The Allard lookup has the limit (`row_log_g_min`), the Kurucz one does not, and M234's fix did not add it; test_atm's checks stay inside the rows. A post-AGB crossing or a yellow supergiant with choice 3 would reach it; with choice 5, which never switches to gray, the hot rows are reached too: atmk1990p00's row at log Teff 4.49 is valid from log g 3.5 (run), eight column widths above the table's edge, and the report counts 46 rows that start above log g 0 in atmk2004p00.tab (not counted again).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the header's promise: a point more than one table step from the data is outside the table.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: in `pressure_in_row`, `surface_pressure_outside` for a log g more than one column width below the row's first valid column, in all three branches; a check in test_atm on atmk1990p00's row 22 with its mutation; the limit in the header and in atm/README section 3. Confirm on the 56-deck set that no deck reaches it.

### M346. Four unguarded paths of the Allard reader: the header skip, row ranges used before they are checked, a blank record, and a report format narrower than the table

- **Status:** open. The atm evaluation's finding 3, confirmed by reading. Error paths: no shipped file reaches any. Kind A; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Partly: the header skip without a status ([alfilein.f:140](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/alfilein.f#L140), [:235](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/alfilein.f#L235)) and the order of ALTABINIT's steps are the F77's; the formats are the port's.
- **Now:** `skip_records`, [allard_table_reader.f90:193-199](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/tables/allard_table_reader.f90#L193-L199), called in both passes ([:182](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/tables/allard_table_reader.f90#L182), [:188](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/tables/allard_table_reader.f90#L188)); `find_table_ranges`' steps 2 to 4, [:355-401](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/tables/allard_table_reader.f90#L355-L401), with the columns' default 0 ([atm_tables.f90:80](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/atm_tables.f90#L80)); the first pass's read, [:226](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/tables/allard_table_reader.f90#L226); the report's formats, [atm_messages.f90:292](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/atm_messages.f90#L292), [:313](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/atm_messages.f90#L313), against `allard_max_g` = 25 ([atm_tables.f90:59](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/atm_tables.f90#L59)); `header_format`, [:51](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/tables/allard_table_reader.f90#L51).
- **What is wrong:**
  - `skip_records` reads with no `iostat`, the only read of atm's two readers without one: a file in the Allard layout that is shorter than its header count ends the run in "Fortran runtime error: End of file" instead of ierr.
  - `find_table_ranges` uses each row's `first_column` and `last_column` (step 3) before it checks them (step 4). A row with no valid entry keeps both at their default 0, so `log_g(first)` is `log_g(0)` and `log_g(last-1)` is `log_g(-1)`: out of bounds, an abort under the devel flags, and otherwise a refusal with garbage ranges in the printout.
  - A blank record inside the data reads as Teff 0, log g 0, [Fe/H] 0, [α/Fe] 0 with `iostat` 0; at the default composition it becomes a row at log Teff = log10(0).
  - `log_allard_tables` formats a refused table with `20(...)` and `1P20E16.8`, so a refused table of 21 or more log g columns would end in a runtime error in the report itself.
  - `header_format = '(i2,x,a)'`: `x` without a count is a compiler extension.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a table that cannot be read returns ierr with its message (M221's rule).
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: `skip_records` returns ierr through `report_allard_read_failure(path, 'its header')`; step 4's row check before step 3; a record with Teff <= 0 refused; the formats sized by `allard_max_g`; `1x`. One synthetic file each in test_atm.

### M347. Stale or inexact atm text and two recipes' gaps: the choices listed by hand in two messages, a reader format for two row counts, three README passages, a dead entry and six dead fields

- **Status:** open (doc). The atm evaluation's findings 4, 5, 6, 7 and the text items of 8, each checked against the code. Kind A (B for test_atm's pinned lines if the lists are generated). Size S.
- **In the original F77?** No for the texts and the lists (2026; the lists came with [12210cb9](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/12210cb9), 2026-11-11, one day after the recipes were traced). The reader's two formats are SETUPS's, and the dead fields are the COMMON blocks'.
- **Now:** each place is named below.
- **What is wrong:**
  - [atm_messages.f90:329](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/atm_messages.f90#L329) and [:347](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/atm_messages.f90#L347) list the choices by hand ("(0 Eddington gray, 1 Krishna-Swamy, 2 HSRA, 3 Kurucz, 4 Allard, 5 Castelli/Kurucz)", "(3 Kurucz, 4 Allard, 5 Castelli/Kurucz)"). "Add a T-tau relation" lists no edit in atm_messages and "Add a table" names only `note_choice_switch` ([README.md:92-104](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/README.md#L92-L104)): a seventh choice added by either works, while the message for an eighth says the choices are 0 to 5.
  - [kurucz_table_reader.f90:26-27](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/tables/kurucz_table_reader.f90#L26-L27), [:68-72](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/tables/kurucz_table_reader.f90#L68-L72): the reader takes one of two fixed log Teff formats by row count. The Castelli one skips the "LOG G:" label only when the list ends on a full line, so it reads a table of 76 rows, or of a multiple of 4 below that; another count (61, say) is refused as unreadable. The recipe's step 3 says "the reader, with its row count" and names neither the row-count parameter's home ([atm_tables.f90:43](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/atm_tables.f90#L43)) nor the format.
  - [README.md:36](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/README.md#L36), "At accretion": without the Allard tables, "or when the point is outside the tables, core takes the photosphere of the last envelope integration (O19)". Since round 2B a failed lookup takes the gray atmosphere's photosphere ([mass_change.f90:259-279](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/step/mass_change.f90#L259-L279)). [:31](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/README.md#L31): the kernel integrates the gray relation "for that integration"; core latches the choice (M321). [:75-86](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/README.md#L75-L86): the coverage is of 2026-11-10, before round 1B's rewrite of atm_messages, and its list of lines not run quotes the "Impossible failure" records, a text that commit removed.
  - `atm_allard_teff_max` ([atm_lib.f90:204-207](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/atm_lib.f90#L204-L207)) is exported and in `PUBLIC['atm']`, but only test_atm calls it; its name says "max" and it returns `log_teff_last`, where the table's `log_teff_max` is another number. `allard_table`'s `is_old_nextgen`, `num_feh`, `num_alpha`, `feh(:)`, `alpha(:)` and `log_teff_first` are never read, and `feh` and `alpha` never written ([atm_tables.f90:70-76](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/atm_tables.f90#L70-L76), [:88](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/atm_tables.f90#L88)), under a comment that says the values are "counted".
  - Small items: `log_teff`/`log_g` in atm_lib and allard_atmosphere against `log10_teff`/`log10_gravity` in kurucz_atmosphere, for the same two quantities; `atm_init` returns on an unknown choice before it resets the tables ([atm_lib.f90:82-90](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/atm_lib.f90#L82-L90)), so "each atm_init starts clean" does not hold after a refused choice; test_atm's section titles keep the F77's routine names ("surfp lookups", "kcsurfp lookups"); [:72-73](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/atm/atm_lib.f90#L72-L73)'s comment breaks mid-line; atm_choices.f90 and atm_tables.f90 hold no I/O and are in neither of `check_boundaries`' kernel lists.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** comments and docs describe the code as it is now; a recipe names every place a newcomer must touch, or the code has one home for it.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: both lists built from `atm_choices` (or the two lines named in both recipes); one log Teff format for any count and the row-count parameter named in the recipe, with a test_atm check on a synthetic table of 61 rows; the three README passages; the dead fields removed and the entry renamed or made the test's.

### M348. find_convection_zones and homogenize_convection_zones write convective_flag(num_zones+1): one element past the arrays for a model of exactly json shells

- **Status:** open. The convection evaluation's finding 1, confirmed by reading. Latent: it needs a model of exactly 5000 shells. Kind A; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes ([convec.f:55](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/convec.f#L55), with `LC(JSON)`):
  ```fortran
        LC(M+1) = .FALSE.
  ```
- **Now:** the two writes, [convection_zones.f90:93](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/convection/convection_zones.f90#L93), [:298](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/convection/convection_zones.f90#L298); the header and the README that call it a sentinel "callers' own scans read", [:47-48](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/convection/convection_zones.f90#L47-L48), [README.md:45](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/convection/README.md#L45); the callers' json-sized arrays, [star_info_lib.f90:542](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/state/star_info_lib.f90#L542), [composition_step.f90:113](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/step/composition_step.f90#L113); a model may have json shells, [model_files.f90:714](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/io/model_files.f90#L714).
- **What is wrong:** every caller's flag array has json (5000) elements, and a model may have exactly json shells. For such a model the write lands one element past the array: in the star, on whatever follows `convective_flag`; in the composition step, past the local `deep_mix_flag`. A devel build stops on it. The dummy is assumed-shape, so nothing in the kernel says the array must be longer than the model. No reader needs the element: the directory's own scans stop at `num_zones`, and the report found no caller that reads element nz + 1.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a kernel writes inside the arrays it is given.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: drop the two writes, or guard them with `num_zones < size(convective_flag)`; correct the README and the header; a check with a flag array of exactly `num_zones` elements under the devel flags.

### M349. The overshoot merge is not the union when the upper region reaches below the lower region's first shell

- **Status:** open. The convection evaluation's finding 2, confirmed by reading (`merge_overlapping_zones` is private, so it was not run). No pinned deck is known to reach it; not measured. Kind B (models with a thin zone within the envelope's overshoot); size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes ([convec.f:129-141](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/convec.f#L129-L141)):
  ```fortran
           MXZONE(J+1,1) = MXZONE(J,1)
  ```
- **Now:** `merge_overlapping_zones`, [convection_zones.f90:228-235](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/convection/convection_zones.f90#L228-L235), under a header that calls the merged region "their union" ([:208-216](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/convection/convection_zones.f90#L208-L216)); the surface zone's edge moved down by `extend_by_overshoot`, [overshoot.f90:128-134](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/convection/overshoot.f90#L128-L134).
- **What is wrong:** the merge gives the merged region region k's first shell and the higher of the two last shells, so it is the union only when region k+1 starts at or above region k's first shell. Downward overshoot can put region k+1's first shell below it: a surface convection zone whose α_env H_P reaches past a thin intermediate zone that does not itself overshoot. Example: zones [18-19] and [22-40], the envelope's edge moved to 14: the merge gives [18-40], and shells 14 to 17 leave the mixed region, though `overshoot_bottom` = 14 still marks them for the adiabatic gradient. If the envelope's edge passes below region k−1's top as well, that pair is never compared again (the loop moves forward only). M285 fixed the same defect at the top (`max` of the two last shells), and its "a merge is the union of the two regions" is the rule this case breaks.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a merge is the union of the two regions (M285's).
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: `merged = [min(bounds(k,1), bounds(k+1,1)), max(bounds(k,2), bounds(k+1,2))]`, stepping k back one row after a merge that lowered the first shell; a check and its mutation.

### M350. Semiconvection's propagation limit never applies to the first shell above the core

- **Status:** open (decision). The convection evaluation's finding 6, confirmed by reading; test_convection states it ("a 1 s timestep adds only the first shell"). No pinned deck reaches semiconvection. Kind B to change, A to document; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: SCONVEC's loop starts at `JMR + 1` and tests the distance before it evaluates a shell ([sconvec.f:168](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/sconvec.f#L168), [:172-179](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/sconvec.f#L172-L179)).
- **Now:** `extend_core_edge`'s loop, [semiconvection.f90:133-158](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/convection/semiconvection.f90#L133-L158); its header, [:78-85](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/convection/semiconvection.f90#L78-L85).
- **What is wrong:** the loop starts at `outside + 1` and tests the distance before it evaluates a shell, so its earliest exit leaves `new_edge = outside`: once the first shell is unstable with the core's composition, it joins the core whatever v_p dt is. The header's step 2 reads as if a small enough timestep moved nothing. Semiconvection runs on several passes of a step, each from the zones found afresh, so the core's mixed edge is at least one shell out on every pass that runs it.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the authors' choice: the limit applies to every shell, or the header and the README say the first shell is exempt.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed: test the first shell's weighted distance against v_p dt as well (B, decks with semiconvection), or state the exemption in the header and in convection/README section 3's "Kept by decision" (A).

### M351. Stale or inexact convection text: pressure_scale_height's export and README sentence, and the coverage figure

- **Status:** open (doc). The convection evaluation's findings 7 and 8, checked against the code (a search for the function's callers). Kind A (B to merge a formula whose gravity differs). Size S.
- **In the original F77?** No: 2026 documents and exports.
- **Now:** the export, [convection_lib.f90:16](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/convection/convection_lib.f90#L16), [:23](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/convection/convection_lib.f90#L23); the README's sentence, [README.md:7](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/convection/README.md#L7), and its coverage paragraph, [:78](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/convection/README.md#L78); H_P computed by hand outside the directory, [turnover_timescale.f90:341-342](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/diagnostics/turnover_timescale.f90#L341-L342), [:357](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/core/diagnostics/turnover_timescale.f90#L357) and [stability_coefficients.f90:187](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/rotation/seculr/stability_coefficients.f90#L187).
- **What is wrong:**
  - `pressure_scale_height` is exported, and the README lists "the pressure scale height ... that core's light-element burn and rezone and rotation's sub-steps use". No code outside the directory calls it: the three users take `envelope_overshoot_depth`, and test_convection is its only outside caller. `check_boundaries`' facade list does not name it, since function references are not checked (M304).
  - The coverage figure (97.8% of 465 lines, 2026-11-10) was measured before round 1B's eight commits changed the code it covers; its per-file percentages describe code that is gone.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a README says who uses what; a coverage figure is of the code it stands beside.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. The report's third docs item, two stale rows of docs/TARGET_ARCHITECTURE.md's routine table (`oversh` and `hsubp`, now overshoot.f90's; microdiff's routines), was corrected with this registration. Proposed fix: make `pressure_scale_height` private to overshoot.f90 and correct the sentence, or have the two outside formulas call it where the gravity agrees; rerun the coverage command and replace the figures.

### M352. change_zone divides by a zone's Z: with Z = 0 and the metals settling, the CNO tracers become NaN at the first settling step

- **Status:** open (frozen: element_diffusion's measured fixes wait for the owner). The convection_diffusion evaluation's finding 3, confirmed by reading. Latent: a zero-metallicity model with settling; the decks were not scanned for one. Kind A (byte-identical for every model with Z > 0); size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes ([microdiff_etm.f:28](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/microdiff_etm.f#L28), [:87](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/microdiff_etm.f#L87), [:118](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/microdiff_etm.f#L118); [equal_to_model.f:29](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/equal_to_model.f#L29), [:80](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/equal_to_model.f#L80), [:99](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/equal_to_model.f#L99)):
  ```fortran
              ZZ2 = ZZ/HCOMP(3,I)
  ```
- **Now:** `change_zone`, [diffusion_grid.f90:298-300](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/element_diffusion/diffusion_grid.f90#L298-L300).
- **What is wrong:** the CNO tracers are scaled by `z_ratio = z_new/xa(i_metals)`. With Z = 0 in a zone and the metals settling (`use_diffusion_z`, which `diffuse_lithium` also turns on, M181), the metals' change is zero, so `z_new = 0`, the ratio is 0/0, and the seven tracer slots `i_c12:i_o18` become NaN. A devel build stops on the division.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a zone without metals has no tracers to scale; its abundances stay finite.
- **What we did:** recorded. Proposed fix, for the round that takes up element_diffusion's B list: leave the tracers alone when `xa(i_metals) <= 0`; a check on a Z = 0 model.

### M353. The original settling routines scale D1 and D2 by constant_mixing_coeff and constant_settling_reduction but not their derivatives, and D2's A_H is the fit's when Burgers' equations are solved

- **Status:** open (frozen). The convection_diffusion evaluation's finding 4, confirmed by reading; it belongs with M243-M246 and M288, for the same retire-or-fix decision. No deck runs these routines; only test_element_diffusion's pins see it. Kind B (test pins only); size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes ([setup_grsett.f:235-244](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/setup_grsett.f#L235-L244), [:264-269](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/setup_grsett.f#L264-L269)):
  ```fortran
              COD1(I) = CSTMIXING*FAC*HQPR(I)*X*(AP+AT)
              COD2(I) = CSTMIXING*FAC*AC
              QCOD1X(I) = FAC*HQPR(I)*(AP+AT+X*(QAPX+QATX))
  ...
                 COD1Z(I) = CSTDIFFMIX*CSTMIXING*FAC*HQPR(I)*ZZ*(AP+AT)
                 QCOD1Z(I) = CSTMIXING*FAC*HQPR(I)*(AP+AT)
  ```
- **Now:** `gravitational_settling_setup`, [original_settling.f90:320-329](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/element_diffusion/original_settling.f90#L320-L329), [:344-351](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/element_diffusion/original_settling.f90#L344-L351).
- **What is wrong:**
  - `constant_mixing_coeff` multiplies D1 and D2 but not their X derivatives, and `constant_settling_reduction` multiplies the metals' D1 but not its Z derivative. With the factors at 0.5 and 0.8 (the test's case "constant mixing 0.5, settling reduction 0.8"), the Lax-Wendroff midpoint correction and the implicit step's D2 correction are 2 and 1.25 times too large.
  - With Burgers' equations solved (`use_thoul_fit` off), only A_P and A_T come from the solution; D2's A_H and all three X derivatives are still the fit's polynomials, so D2 ignores `coulomb_log_choice` 4's pairwise logarithms.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a coefficient's derivative is the derivative of the coefficient the step uses.
- **What we did:** recorded, with M243-M246 for the same decision (retire the original routines, or fix and test them).

### M354. A one-zone settling region is returned as found, and the grid's size is then computed from 0/0

- **Status:** open (frozen). The convection_diffusion evaluation's finding 5, confirmed by a run on a scratch build of 1179afbf (`t_region.f90`: a 10-zone model with a helium-rich convective core, zones 1 to 3, under an envelope whose Y is below `helium_diffusion_min` = 0.5): `find_settling_region` returns zone_begin = zone_end = 3 with `region_found`, and `size_equal_grid` then returns 2 points at a spacing of 0. Latent: the default minimum is 1e-3, which every envelope exceeds. Kind A; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: MICRODIFF_SETUP sets IBEGIN from the core and the X search and IEND from the envelope and the Y search, and never compares the two ([microdiff_setup.f:64-101](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/microdiff_setup.f#L64-L101)).
- **Now:** `find_settling_region`'s Y search, [settling_region.f90:72-81](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/element_diffusion/settling_region.f90#L72-L81); `size_equal_grid`, [diffusion_grid.f90:68-77](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/element_diffusion/diffusion_grid.f90#L68-L77).
- **What is wrong:** `zone_end` moves inward to the first zone with Y above the minimum and is returned with `region_found` without being compared with `zone_begin`. When Y exceeds the minimum at the core's top zone and nowhere above it, the region is one zone: `size_equal_grid` then has `span = 0` and `narrowest = 0`, and takes `int(0/0)` for the point count and `mod(0, 0)`. Corrected from the report, which says the grids are built from NaN: the conversion of a NaN to an integer is undefined, and on the build here (gfortran, arm64) it gives 0, so the grid is two coincident points at zero spacing; another platform gives another count, and a devel build traps. A search that passes below `zone_begin` (a core without hydrogen under such an envelope) gives a negative span instead.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a region needs two zones: a no-region verdict otherwise, as for a fully convective model.
- **What we did:** recorded. Proposed fix, for the round that takes up element_diffusion's B list: a no-region verdict when `zone_end <= zone_begin`; a check.

### M355. element_diffusion text: the settings table omits M289's case, and solve_diffusion_term keeps a midpoint change and a zero derivative that it multiplies together

- **Status:** open (doc; frozen). The convection_diffusion evaluation's finding 10, checked against the code. Kind A (passing no derivative is byte-identical for finite changes). Size S.
- **In the original F77?** No for the table (2026); the dead work is what M253's fix ([8aac54fa](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/8aac54fa)) left of the F77's iteration.
- **Now:** the settings table's row, [README.md:85](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/element_diffusion/README.md#L85); `solve_diffusion_term`, [microdiff_run.f90:164-173](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/element_diffusion/microdiff_run.f90#L164-L173), and its replay of the pass count, [:190-197](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/element_diffusion/microdiff_run.f90#L190-L197).
- **What is wrong:**
  - The table says `settling_num_iterations` and `settling_tolerance` decide "only the messages" in microdiff. With `settling_num_iterations < 1` there is no implicit solve at all, so the diffusion term D2 is dropped (M289); the table should say so while M289 is open.
  - `solve_diffusion_term` fills `change_mid` with the drift's midpoint change and a `zero_derivative` array, and passes both to `implicit_diffusion_coeffs`, which multiplies them: dead work that reads as if the coefficients were corrected. The loop after it replays the F77's pass count so that the messages match.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a table of what each setting does includes the case where it changes the result; code that does nothing is not written out.
- **What we did:** recorded. Proposed fix, with the frozen round's other texts: the table's cell; no derivative passed to `implicit_diffusion_coeffs` from microdiff (an optional argument), and the replay dropped when the messages are reworded.

### M356. The OPAL 2006 EOS's edge weight jumps at every inner corner of the table's ragged edge

- **Status:** fixed (the convergence round, 2026-11-17). The first cause of O3's and M294's stops.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. EQBOUND06 (LLP 10/16/06) forms the weight as the product of a density ramp, set only in the last tabulated density cell of the point's T6 row, and a T6 ramp, set only in the last tabulated T6 cell of its density column ([eqbound06.f:81-100](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqbound06.f#L81-L100)):
  ```fortran
        IF(l .EQ. nra(k)) THEN
          LRAMP = .TRUE.
          DRampF = (rho(l)-D)/(rho(l)-rho(l-1))
        ENDIF
  ...
        IF(k .EQ. nta(l)) THEN
          LRAMP = .TRUE.
          TRampF = (T6-T6a(k))/(T6a(k-1)-T6A(k))
        ENDIF

        FAC = DRampF * TRampF
  ```
- **Before the fix** (at [1179afbf](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/tree/1179afbf/src)): `find_ragged_edge_ramp`, [opal_eos.f90:895-1014](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/1179afbf/src/eos/opal/opal_eos.f90#L895-L1014).
- **What was wrong:** the table's high-density edge is a staircase: the highest tabulated density column steps down as T6 falls (`opal06_density_index_edge`). Take a T6 row where it steps from column j to j-1. Just below the row the cell at column j-1 is the last of its row, and the weight is the density ramp, (ρ_j-1 − ρ)/(ρ_j-1 − ρ_j-2), anywhere from 0 to 1; just above the row the same column is neither the last of its row nor the last of its column, and the weight is 1. So the weight jumps along the whole edge the two cells share, and with it the blended EOS, by the difference between OPAL and SCV there. Measured along a 0.03 Msun model (X = 0.71962, Z = 0.016492): the weight goes 1 → 0.062 at log T 4.6767, 1 → 0.22 at 4.5280, and four more between 4.40 and 4.29; log ρ jumps by up to 1.7e-2, ∇_ad by up to 0.067 and c_P by up to 31%. A fully convective star of 0.03 to 0.15 Msun runs along this staircase from log T 4.8 to 4.2; a shell that a Newton iteration moves across one of the lines changes its residual by that much, and the iteration cycles (O3's "two-cycle"; at the 0.03 Msun deck's failing step the corrections repeat with period 5, no convective flag flips, and the triangle is not refitted).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** an equation of state is continuous in (T, P) at fixed composition; Newton's method needs a continuous residual.
- **What we did:** the weight is the bilinear interpolant, in the point's cell, of node weights that are 1 at a node whose four cells are all tabulated and 0 at the others. In every cell but those with an inner corner of the staircase this is the product the code had, and it is still formed that way (so a model that meets no inner corner is unchanged to the last bit); in an inner-corner cell, where the product gave 1, it is 1 − (1 − u) w (u, w the cell's fractions in T6 and ρ, the corner at u = 0, w = 1). `test_eos` checks the blended quantities either side of the T6 row 0.0475 at two pressures of an inner-corner cell (2 checks, 2 mutations).
  - Measured on the 56-deck set and the 35 pins against the round's starting baseline: RESULT: 1 NOT IDENTICAL; pins 34 OK, 1 DIFF: `examples/run_from_dbl_to_zams/Test_m0030_feh0_noGS_ZAMS` (.log, its pin, .mod), the set's one fully convective low-mass deck: 52 models both; first visible change at model 2 (9.6e-6 in log Teff, log L and log R); the final model at 1.2791e-2 Gyr against 1.2160e-2 (its timesteps differ, the last by 14%), log L -2.75106 against -2.73605 (-1.0e-3 from the base's track at that age), log Teff -4.7e-4. The other 55 decks are byte-identical: none meets an inner-corner cell.
  - On the stopped decks (scratch runs, each deck as shipped; before -> after): Test_m0060_feh0_noGS_ZAMS model 44 -> its stop (198 models), Test_m0p05feh+0p0GS98_allard_15Gyr 72 -> its stop (15 Gyr, 396), Test_m0p1feh+0p0GS98_allard_ZAMS 139 -> its stop (216), SamplelowerMS_m0p15feh+0p0GS98_kurucz_ZAMS 188 -> its stop (212); Test_m0040 17 -> 33 and Test_m0050 30 -> 47 (M357 is what stops them next); Test_m0p03feh+0p0GS98_allard_15Gyr 84 -> 359 (1.1 Gyr, where it leaves the Allard table); Test_m0030_feh0_noGS_ZAMS with its 50-model cap lifted 81 -> 803.
  - Pins re-seeded: `Test_m0030_feh0_noGS_ZAMS.log`; `expected_test_eos.out` gains the two checks' lines.

### M357. The OPAL density search gave up on a jump of the table's own pressure, and the point fell back to the Yale/SCV result

- **Status:** fixed (the convergence round, 2026-11-17). The second cause of O3's stops.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. RHOOFP06 ran regula falsi for 10 tries and returned -999 ([rhoofp06.f:92-120](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/rhoofp06.f#L92-L120)); M41 made it 30 and gave the fallback its run-log line.
- **Before the fix** (at [229ae4b1](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/tree/229ae4b1/src)): `opal_density_search`, [opal_eos.f90:305-460](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/229ae4b1/src/eos/opal/opal_eos.f90#L305-L460).
- **What was wrong:** the search looks for the density at which the table's interpolated pressure equals P to 5e-8. Near the table's high-density edge the interpolation changes stencil from one density to the next, and its pressure jumps there, by 1e-5 to 4e-4. For a P inside such a jump no density matches: the bracket closes on the density of the jump, the 30 steps run out, the search reports "no convergence ... falling back", and the blend takes the Yale/SCV result for that point alone, 2.7% away in density and 0.014 in ∇_ad (measured at log T 5.9776 of a 0.04 Msun model, shell 412 of 982), while the shells either side take OPAL. A shell that the iteration moves in and out of the jump's pressure window makes the corrections alternate (an exact 2-cycle of ±1.78e-4 in log P in that model, the step after model 33). The eight low-mass decks logged 5 to 63 such fallbacks each.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** where the table brackets the pressure it has an answer, the density at which its pressure crosses P; a pressure mismatch of 1e-4 at that density is the table's own, and far smaller than the 2.7% of another equation of state.
- **What we did:** after the 30 regula falsi steps the search goes on by bisection while the pair brackets P, to the same tolerance; when the bracket has closed (to 1e-14 of the density) it returns that density, with a note the run log gets once per run ("the table's pressure jumps across the density that gives P ... that density is taken"). A pair that does not bracket P still falls back, with its line. Searches that converged before take the same steps as before. `test_eos` scans 401 pressures across the jump at T6 = 0.94974 (1 check, 2 mutations). The jump of the interpolated pressure itself is not touched (it is the interpolation scheme's).
  - Measured on the 56-deck set and the 35 pins against M356's snapshot: RESULT: 1 NOT IDENTICAL; pins 34 OK, 1 DIFF: `examples/run_from_dbl_to_zams/Test_m0030_feh0_noGS_ZAMS` (.log, its pin, .mod): 52 models both, no progress line changes, the final model's age +1.5e-9 (relative), log L -1.8e-9, log Teff -5.1e-10; its log loses six "falling back" lines and gains the note. The other 55 decks are byte-identical: none logged a fallback.
  - On the stopped decks, each as shipped (before -> after, both with M356): Test_m0040_feh0_noGS_ZAMS model 33 -> its stop (central X, 251 models), Test_m0050_feh0_noGS_ZAMS 47 -> its stop (227); no deck of the eight logs a fallback any more. `test_low_mass_decks.py` (new, in CI's list) runs the six decks that now reach their stops (Test_m0040, m0050 and m0060_feh0_noGS_ZAMS, Test_m0p05feh+0p0GS98_allard_15Gyr, Test_m0p1feh+0p0GS98_allard_ZAMS, SamplelowerMS_m0p15feh+0p0GS98_kurucz_ZAMS) and requires exit 0, the stop the deck asks for and no fallback line: 10 to 40 s a deck, under 3 minutes in all.
  - Pins re-seeded: `Test_m0030_feh0_noGS_ZAMS.log`; `expected_test_eos.out` gains the check's line.

## 21. Found by the validation tier and the convergence round (2026-11-17)

Two rounds that ended on 2026-11-17 found defects they did not fix. The physics validation tier (`docs/PHYSICS_VALIDATION.md`; merged in [8c66ff29](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/8c66ff29)) checks the output files against the structure equations, GYRE, the Sun, MESA and the release paper; it listed twelve defects and surprises, V1 to V12, and holds seven of them as strict expected failures of `test_validation_*.py`. The convergence round (section 20; merged in [078df658](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/078df658)) listed seven more, D1 to D7, in its hand-back. One item is the round's integrator's (the tests' table roots). These items are those findings, in the rounds' order: the validation tier's (M358-M367), the convergence round's (M368-M373) and the test harness's (M374), all open. Each entry records what is wrong, the input that shows it, the proposed fix, its kind (A, byte-identical on every deck and pin; B, a change of results or of pinned text) and its size (S, M or L).

- **How they were checked.** Every item was read again in the code at 078df658, and against the F77 at 6cd56739, before its entry was written. The validation tier's numbers are its tests' (each entry names the test and the measured value) and were not run again, with one exception, M358. Run for the registration, on a build of 078df658 in the registration's own worktree (`scratch_reg/` in the work directory): the standard solar deck with its solver tolerances changed row by row, with the contract test's own fixture and closure measure (M358; `v1/closure*.py`, eight runs); the Monte Carlo deck's controls read in a tree without the deck's output directory (M373; with the convergence round's `src/test_controls`, whose source is 078df658's); counts over the shipped decks (M358, M366, M371: 1,179 `.inlist`, 17 `.nml2` and 4 `.nml1` files); the centre's sound-travel time and N² of a stored model (M362, M363); and the repository's three GS98 opacity files at the MESA comparison's nodes (M365). Where the check corrected a round's account (a cause, a count, a sign, a place), the entry gives the corrected account and says so: M358, M362, M364, M366, M367, M368, M371, M373 and M374.
- **Not given a number.** D4, the shipped 25 Msun starting model that the current code cannot start from, is M316's open part, diagnosed in its entry: no second entry. M317, which the tier found again (two of its expected failures name it), stays as it is. V4's points are the 81 that O22's fix met and recorded: M361 is the entry, and O22's gets a dated line.
- **One entry for one defect.** The tier's naming and documentation matters (V7, V11, V12 and its note on two history columns) are one entry, M367; the convergence round's two deck matters (its questions 1 and 5, D5) are one, M372. V8 is a question about a table's provenance, entered as such (M365).
- **Not entered.** The tier's notes that are not defects: `eps_neu` is zero throughout the solar models, so its luminosity check does not exercise that term's sign (a coverage note), and the bands of its MESA comparison.
- Current-code links point at [078df658](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/tree/078df658/src).

### M358. A model is accepted without a solve when its residuals are within solver_tolerances(5,·): the standard solar deck's luminosity equation is open by 4.6e-4 of L

- **Status:** open, the authors' decision ("Decisions needed"). The validation tier's V1, held by a strict expected failure: `test_validation_contract.py`, `test_luminosity_equation_is_converged` ((L − ∫ε dm)/L up to 4.6e-4 on the main sequence, against the 2e-5 a converged model meets). Its cause is corrected here from the tier's account by runs made for the registration: not the corrections' tolerances (rows 1 to 4) but the residual test (row 5). Kind B: the standard solar deck's pin and test_mesa_baselines' files for it (CI's solar-regression job runs the deck twice and compares the two runs, and test_physics' bands are 0.02 dex: neither holds a number that moves); size S for the deck, M if the test changes.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. CRRECT accepts a model on its residuals from the second pass on ([crrect.f:134-144](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/crrect.f#L134-L144)):
  ```fortran
  C CHECK ON SIGNIFICANCE OF R.H.S. EQUATIONS FOR P AND T
  C N.B.  DOES NOT CHECK DIFFERENCES IN BOUNDARY EQUATIONS
  	 IF(ITER.GT.1) THEN
  	    IF(HMAX(1).LE.HTOLER(5,1) .AND. HMAX(2).LE.HTOLER(5,2) .AND.
       *      HMAX(3).LE.HTOLER(5,1) .AND. HMAX(4).LE. HTOLER(5,2)) THEN
  ...
  	       LFINI = .TRUE.
  	       RETURN
  ```
  and 128 of the import's 129 example decks set `HTOLER(5,2) = 2.5E-5`. The standard solar deck came with the YREC team's [4861b739](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/4861b739) (2025-04-18), with `HTOLER(5,1) = 3.0D-7` and `HTOLER(5,2) = 2.5E-5`, as today.
- **Now:** `accept_small_residuals`, [henyey_iteration.f90:257-290](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/core/structure/henyey_iteration.f90#L257-L290) (the test, [:273-277](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/core/structure/henyey_iteration.f90#L273-L277)); the control's default, [controls_buffer.f90:584-587](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/io/controls_buffer.f90#L584-L587); the deck, [Test_solar_noGS_norot.nml2:44-53](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/examples/run_standard_solar_model/Test_solar_noGS_norot.nml2#L44-L53); a sibling's values, [Test_solarcal_noGS_norot.nml2:44-53](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/examples/run_standard_solar_model/Test_solarcal_noGS_norot.nml2#L44-L53).
- **What is wrong:**
  - From the second pass of an iteration level on, `accept_small_residuals` declares the model converged, without a solve, when the largest residual of each difference equation is within row 5 of `solver_tolerances`: P and R against (5,1), T and L against (5,2). The L residual is absolute, in Lsun, for each pair of shells. A residual of one sign in a few hundred shells adds up: the model that is written satisfies hydrostatic equilibrium to 1.3e-6 and its luminosity equation, L(fit) − L(1) − ∫(ε_nuc + ε_ν + ε_grav) dm, to 3.7e-4 to 4.6e-4 of L on the main sequence, with L(1)/(ε(1) m(1)) = 1.00055. The tier found that it scales with the time step (steps 4 times smaller: 9e-5): what is accepted is the residual the composition step leaves.
  - Corrected from the tier's account, which named the corrections' tolerances (rows 1 to 4: 6e-7 to 9e-7 in this deck, 6e-9 in the other three solar examples and the testsuite). Measured for the registration on the deck, with the contract test's fixture (six models) and closure measure; log L at 4.568 Gyr is given against the shipped deck's −4.107e-5:

    | `solver_tolerances` | Closure (magnitude) of the three main-sequence models, 0.9, 2.2 and 3.4 Gyr | log L at 4.568 Gyr |
    |---|---|---|
    | as shipped | 3.7e-4, 4.2e-4, 4.6e-4 | |
    | rows 1-4 times 0.01 (6e-9 to 9e-9) | the same, to every digit printed | 0 (to 1e-8) |
    | rows 1-4 times 100 (6e-5 to 9e-5) | the same (the pre-main-sequence models differ: −7.4e-4 for −1.5e-4 at 2 Myr) | −1.5e-6 |
    | row 5 times 0.01 (3e-9, 2.5e-7: the other solar decks' values) | 7.6e-5, 8.3e-5, 9.1e-5 | +1.31e-4 |
    | rows 1-5 times 0.01 (the other solar decks' whole set) | 2.0e-7, 2.9e-7, 9.1e-5 | +1.31e-4 |
    | row 5 times 0.001 | 5.4e-10, 5.9e-9, 5.7e-9 | +1.42e-4 (log Teff +1.95e-5, log R +3.19e-5) |
    | (5,1) alone times 0.001 | 5.6e-9, 5.9e-9, 5.7e-9 | +1.42e-4 |
    | (5,2) alone times 0.001 | 5.4e-10, 5.9e-9, 4.5e-6 | +1.42e-4 |

    So row 5 alone reproduces the tier's +1.4e-4 dex. Rows 1 to 4 do nothing on the main sequence (Newton's last correction is far below either value). The two row-5 values act as one test, so tightening either defeats the shortcut. And the other solar decks' values do not close the equation on this deck's time steps: 9e-5 at 3.4 Gyr. (The tier measured 8.9e-7 on `Test_solarGS98_dif`, which has those values and 822 models.)
  - The row-5 values are not this deck's alone. Of the 1,196 shipped decks (`.inlist` and `.nml2`), (5,2) is 2.5e-5 in 1,021, of which 929 also have (5,1) at 3e-7 or above (866 the pair 3e-5 and 2.5e-5); it is 2.5e-7 in 170 and 2.5e-6 in 4, and one deck sets neither. What their models' luminosity equations are open by was not measured.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the model that is written satisfies its four equations to the same order. A pinned solar model should not move by 1.4e-4 dex in log L, five times the solar calibration's own tolerance (3e-5), when a convergence shortcut is switched off.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Two fixes, the authors' choice:
  - the deck: row 5 a thousand times tighter in `Test_solar_noGS_norot` (its siblings' values are not enough). Its log L at 4.568 Gyr moves by +1.42e-4 dex, to +1.01e-4: L/Lsun − 1 = +2.3e-4, where the shipped deck has −0.9e-4 and the release paper asks 1e-4 of its solar models, so the deck's X and mixing length would be calibrated again. Its pin and test_mesa_baselines' files are reseeded. The 1,020 other decks with its (5,2) stay as they are;
  - the code: a residual test that bounds what the equation needs (the L residuals summed over the model, or relative to L; or one corrector pass before a model is accepted), which moves every deck, each to be measured.
  With either, the expected failure turns into XPASS and its mark is removed.

### M359. The stitched model keeps the envelope's repeat of the fitting point when its radius lands above the interior's: two points 1e-6 R apart, the outer one denser

- **Status:** open. The validation tier's V2, held by a strict expected failure: `test_validation_contract.py`, `test_no_density_inversion_at_the_fit` (5 of the deck's 6 models). Confirmed by reading. Kind B for the profile and pulse files of a model where it fires (one point fewer; test_mesa_baselines' profile files are pinned), byte-identical for the run itself; size S.
- **In the original F77?** No. The stitched model is 2026's: [1694dbc4](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/1694dbc4) (2026-08-23, "Extend MESA-mode profiles and pulse files through envelope + atmosphere") wrote the test as it is today.
- **Now:** `build_stitched_model`, [stitched_model.f90:185-197](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/core/diagnostics/stitched_model.f90#L185-L197):
  ```fortran
  ! envelope: env_points runs fitting point -> photosphere (envint
  ! inverts it), so it appends directly. Its innermost point repeats
  ! the fitting point (to re-integration roundoff, so its radius can
  ! even land marginally BELOW the last interior point's) -- skip any
  ! envelope point not strictly outside the interior, keeping the
  ! extended radius strictly monotonic for GYRE.
        do i = 1, s%env_points%num_env_points
           if (s%stitched%n_ext >= max_ext) exit
           if (s%env_points%env_log10_radius(i) <= s%logR(s%nz)) cycle
  ```
- **What is wrong:** the envelope integration's first point repeats the fitting point. The comment takes the two to differ by round-off, and the repeat is skipped only when its log R is not above the interior's. They differ by the envelope triangle's interpolation error instead: the surface boundary condition is interpolated in the triangle, and the tier measured jumps at the fitting point of 5.1e-6 in ln r, 2.0e-4 in ln T and 3.3e-4 in ln ρ (a triangle 10 times smaller gave jumps 100 times smaller). In 5 of the 6 models the repeat's radius is above the interior's, by dr/r = 1e-6 to 5e-6, so it is kept: two points 1e-6 R apart, the outer one with ln ρ higher by 1.1e-4 to 3.3e-4 and ln T lower by 0.7e-4 to 2.0e-4. That is a density inversion over one interval. It is harmless where the layer is convective (N² is the thermal form there, M361 apart); where the fitting point is radiative the centred N² of the pair and of its two neighbours is differenced across it (not measured: the six models' fitting points are convective).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the files hold the fitting point once, and the density does not rise outward at the join.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: skip the envelope's first point by its index (it is the repeat by construction) and keep the radius test for the points after it; the join's own jump, which is the triangle's, then lies across a 0.05 dex interval of pressure. The expected failure's mark is removed with it.
- **Round 3 (2026-11-18):** now in `stitched_kernels.f90`, `map_extended_grid`, the envelope loop's radius test ([0ea2528f](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/0ea2528f)). The fix is `if (i == 1 .or. envelope_log_radius(i) <= interior_top_log_radius) cycle`; test_stitched's check "index map: an envelope first point above the interior's top is kept (M359)" then expects n_ie = 7, n_ext = 10 and index(6) = 2; mutation stitched_kernels-04 is the fix.

### M360. In an atmosphere layer that is convectively unstable the files' nabla is the adiabatic gradient, while the temperature follows the T(tau) relation

- **Status:** open, a decision on what the column means. The validation tier's V3, held by a strict expected failure: `test_validation_contract.py`, `test_atmosphere_gradient_everywhere` (15% in nabla just above the photosphere of the deck's 2 Myr model, Teff 4436 K; none at the solar age; in the atmosphere's radiative layers the column agrees with dln T/dln P to 3.1e-3). Confirmed by reading. Kind B for the atmosphere rows of the profile and pulse files of cool models; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. ENVINT stored the same choice for its pulsation atmosphere file ([envint.f:334-341](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/envint.f#L334-L341)):
  ```fortran
  CFROM FIRST LINES OF TPGRAD
  	    DELR = QO*B*DEXP(CLN*(QPL-HSTOT-4.0D0*QTL+CLSUNL-CGL+
       *           CDELRL))*FTL/FPL
  	    IF (DELR-QDELA .LE. 1.0D-6) THEN
  	      DEL = DELR
  	    ELSE
  	      DEL = QDELA
  	    END IF
  ```
- **Now:** `store_atmosphere_gradients`, [envelope_integration_kernel.f90:665-683](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L665-L683); the atmosphere points' columns, [stitched_model.f90:832-833](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/core/diagnostics/stitched_model.f90#L832-L833); the thermal N² they enter, [:860-863](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/core/diagnostics/stitched_model.f90#L860-L863).
- **What is wrong:** the atmosphere's temperature is the T(τ) relation's; no convection is computed there. The gradient stored with each atmosphere point is the radiative one (the diffusion formula) where it is at most ∇_ad + 1e-6, and ∇_ad where it is larger. So where a layer of the atmosphere is unstable by that test, the files' ∇ is ∇_ad while dln T/dln P of the same file's T and P is the relation's. The pulse files' nabla has it, and through it the thermal N² there (zero, which then takes the centred difference: M361's test).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a file's ∇ is the gradient of its own T and P.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed, for the authors to choose: (a) the column is dln T/dln P of the T(τ) relation the atmosphere integrates, with ∇_rad kept in its own slot (the atmosphere rows of cool models' files change); (b) the column stays and is described as the Schwarzschild gradient of a layer the atmosphere does not model, and the expected failure becomes a documented exception.
- **Round 3 (2026-11-18):** measured for the decision (the core2 agent's B list item 4). Option (b), the gradient the temperature has: for the Eddington gray relation that is grad_rad exactly (with L = 4 pi R^2 sigma Teff^4 and g = G M/R^2 both are kappa P/(4 g (tau + 2/3))), so the fix is `gradient = radiative_gradient` for choice 0; for Krishna Swamy and HSRA it needs a small function of t_tau_relations' q(tau) (`ttau_dlogt_dlogtau`). With the kernel on the test deck's microphysics (gray): at 5777 K, log g 4.44 and at 4436 K, log g 3.6 no atmosphere point is unstable, so (a) and (b) write the same; at 3800 K, log g 3.5 one point of 26, the photosphere, has grad_rad 5.1% above grad_ad. It moves the atmosphere rows of cool models' profile and pulse files (nabla and the N^2 built from it), no .log, no pin; the contract test's expected failure would pass. The agent recommends (b) for the three analytic relations.

### M361. N² is positive through part of a convective core: where nabla equals nabla_ad exactly, the rule's `>= 0` test takes the centred difference

- **Status:** open. The validation tier's V4, held by a strict expected failure: `test_validation_contract.py`, `test_brunt_is_not_positive_in_convection` (80 points of the 32 Myr model's convective core, N² up to +5e-11 s⁻², 6e-5 of g²ρ/P). O22's fix met the same points (the 81 left in its profile 3) and recorded them without an entry. Confirmed by reading. Kind B for the files' N² and the history's `delta_Pg` (neither is a default column, and no compared or pinned file holds them); size S.
- **In the original F77?** No. [67b36131](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/67b36131) (2026-08-30, "Keep thermal N2 inside convective zones (hybrid Brunt computation)") wrote the switch as `>= 0`.
- **Now:** the thermal value, [stitched_model.f90:860-863](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/core/diagnostics/stitched_model.f90#L860-L863); `difference_brunt_n2`'s comment and test, [:882-902](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/core/diagnostics/stitched_model.f90#L882-L902) (the test, [:893](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/core/diagnostics/stitched_model.f90#L893)); `delta_Pg`'s walk, [observables.f90:349-363](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/core/diagnostics/observables.f90#L349-L363).
- **What is wrong:** N² is the thermal form g²ρδ(∇_ad − ∇)/P where that is negative and the centred density difference elsewhere, and the test for "elsewhere" is `N2 >= 0`.
