Where convection is efficient YREC sets ∇ = ∇_ad exactly, so the thermal N² is exactly 0, the test passes, and the point gets the centred difference of a near-adiabatic stratification: cancellation noise of either sign, which the comment above the loop says the rule avoids ("CONVECTIVE zones keep the first-pass thermal value"). `delta_Pg`'s walk starts at the first N² > 0, so a positive point inside a convective core opens a cavity that is not there.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** N² is not positive inside a convection zone; the rule's comment says so.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: the centred difference only where the thermal value is positive (`> 0`), or by the point's convective flag; a point with ∇ = ∇_ad keeps 0. The expected failure's mark is removed with it, and the contract test's mutation of the rule covers it.
- **Round 3 (2026-11-18):** now in `stitched_kernels.f90`, `difference_brunt_n2` ([0ea2528f](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/0ea2528f)): `brunt_n2(j) >= 0.0d0` becomes `> 0.0d0`. test_stitched's check "N^2: a thermal value of exactly zero takes the difference (M361)" then expects 0 at point 8; mutation stitched_kernels-09 is the fix.

### M362. delta_Pg and delta_nu leave out the part of their integrals inside the innermost mesh point: delta_Pg is 6.1% too large on the standard solar model

- **Status:** open. The validation tier's V5, held by a strict expected failure: `test_validation_gyre.py`, `test_delta_pg_against_gyre` (the history's 1641.50 s; the same integral with the centre's part 1547.11 s; GYRE's l = 1 period spacing, n_g = 120 to 200, on a file with the centre resolved 1546.79 s: +6.1%). `delta_nu`'s part is added by the registration, from the code and a stored model. Kind B for the two history columns (neither is a default column, and no compared or pinned file holds them); size S.
- **In the original F77?** No. [bf3d5070](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/bf3d5070) (2026-08-29, "Add delta_nu and delta_Pg asymptotic seismic observables").
- **Now:** `compute_seismic_observables`: the sound-travel sum, [observables.f90:321-338](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/core/diagnostics/observables.f90#L321-L338); the buoyancy sum, [:340-368](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/core/diagnostics/observables.f90#L340-L368); the columns' descriptions, [history_columns.list:105-106](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/defaults/history_columns.list#L105-L106).
- **What is wrong:**
  - `delta_Pg`: the sum runs over points 2 to n_ie − 1, each with N/r times half the span to its neighbours, so it starts at (r_1 + r_2)/2. N is proportional to r at the centre, so the part inside is N there: 6% of the integral for r_1 = 0.0097 R. With `extend_core_inward` (`Test_solarGS98_dif`, r_1 = 0.0043 R) it is +2.7% (1568.5 s for 1527 s). MESA's own `delta_Pg` is 0.4% from GYRE on MESA's file.
  - `delta_nu`: the trapezoid starts at point 1, so r_1/c(r_1) is not in it, though the comment says ∫ from 0 and the column list "center -> photosphere". On the standard solar deck's 3.4 Gyr model that is 13.8 s of 3341 s: the column is 0.41% too large (149.65 for 149.03 μHz; computed for the registration from the model's GYRE file). It is small beside M367's 5%, but the tier's comparison of the integral through the atmosphere with GYRE (−0.17%, tolerance 0.6%) would read about −0.6% with it.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the integrals run from the centre, as their descriptions say.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: the centre's terms in closed form, N at (r_1 + r_2)/2 for the buoyancy sum when point 2 is in the cavity, and r_1/c(r_1) for the acoustic radius. The expected failure's mark is removed with it; the tier's re-derivations of the two columns follow.
- **Round 3 (2026-11-18):** now in `stitched_kernels.f90`, `acoustic_radius` (add r_1/c_1 when c_1 is positive) and `buoyancy_radius` (add N/r at point 2 times (r_1 + r_2)/2 when point 2 is in the cavity), with observables' two comments ([0ea2528f](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/0ea2528f)). test_stitched's four checks of the integrals hold today's values and change with the fix: "(r_n - r_1)/c (M362)" expects r_n/c; "an interval without a sound speed" gains r_1/c; "a times the span the sum covers (M362)" expects a (r_n + r_(n-1))/2; "the innermost cavity only" expects a (r_6 + r_5)/2.

### M363. The pulse files' innermost point is at r = 0.0097 R: GYRE's l = 1 period spacing comes out 2.4% low, and that point's N² is a copy of its neighbour's

- **Status:** open. The validation tier's V6, held by a strict expected failure: `test_validation_gyre.py`, `test_g_modes_do_not_depend_on_the_centre_fill` (GYRE on the file as written 1510.36 s; with 30 points added inside r_1 by the expansions about the centre 1546.79 s: −2.4%; with `extend_core_inward` −1.2%, 1509.2 for 1526.8 s; the p modes move by 0.002 μHz). Confirmed by reading. Kind B for the pulse files (more points), the model unchanged; size M.
- **In the original F77?** Yes, for the mesh: the innermost shell is at 1e-4 of the mass (the release paper, section 3.1: "The inner fitting point is set at 10⁻⁴ M_tot ... close to 0.01 R_tot"), and WRTMOD's pulse model wrote the mesh as it was ([wrtmod.f:215-231](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/wrtmod.f#L215-L231)). The GYRE, FGONG and GSM writers are 2026's and write the mesh too.
- **Now:** `build_pulse_points`, [stitched_model.f90:725-746](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/core/diagnostics/stitched_model.f90#L725-L746) (the files' first point is the mesh's); the end points' N², [:903-906](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/core/diagnostics/stitched_model.f90#L903-L906); `extend_core_inward`, [starting_model.f90:569-600](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L569-L600) (M326: its default factor divides 0 by 0).
- **What is wrong:**
  - A pulsation code needs the model down to the centre. Given a first point at 0.0097 R (MESA's solar model: 9e-4 R), GYRE fills the centre itself, and its g-mode periods depend on how: the l = 1 period spacing of the standard solar model comes out 2.4% low.
  - The innermost point's N² is the second point's, copied, where N² is proportional to r² (on the standard solar deck's 3.4 Gyr model N²(1)/N²(2) = 1 for (r_1/r_2)² = 0.970: 3% high).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a pulse file that a pulsation code can use for g modes without a treatment of its own.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: the writers add points inside r_1 by the expansions about the centre (P, T and ρ quadratic in r, m as r³, L as m, N² as r²), as the tier's test file does; or the decks that write pulse files set `extend_core_inward`, which halves the error (after M326). N²(1) = N²(2) (r_1/r_2)² either way.
- **Round 3 (2026-11-18):** the end points' N^2 is now `stitched_kernels.f90`'s `difference_brunt_n2` (`brunt_n2(1) = brunt_n2(2)`; times (r_1/r_2)^2 with the fix, and test_stitched's check "N^2: the end points copy their neighbours (M363)" changes); the points inside r_1 are `build_pulse_points`' (stitched_model.f90) with `map_extended_grid` (a region before the interior), or the writers' (io/pulsation_output.f90) ([0ea2528f](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/0ea2528f)).

### M364. The testsuite's rotating solar deck gives 2.09 dex of Li7 depletion, where the release paper says 2.3 dex within 1%

- **Status:** open, the authors' decision: a recalibration ("Decisions needed"). The validation tier's V9, held by a strict expected failure: `test_validation_rotation.py`, `test_published_lithium_depletion` (2.086 dex, the log of the initial over the final surface Li7/H; the paper's period, 25.412 d for 25.4, and its L, R and Z/X are reproduced). The paper's sentence and the decks' values were read for the registration; that the deck "no longer" gives the paper's number, as the tier has it, is not established (below). Kind B: the deck's pin and the tier's own landmarks (`validation/rotation/omega_landmarks.txt`); size S, a calibration.
- **In the original F77?** Not determined. The deck is the YREC team's (the testsuite, [f080aa50](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/f080aa50), 2025-11-13, and [3f057e31](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/3f057e31), 2026-02-23), with its `mixing_velocity_scale`. No run of it with the code of its time is in the repository (the pins are untracked, and each result-changing fix re-seeded them), so whether it gave 2.3 dex then is not known. That the fixes since moved it is likely: N6's alone moved the rotating example deck's surface Li7 by −0.113 dex.
- **Now:** [Test_solarGS98_difrotmixper18p4d1p0.inlist:311](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/testsuite/Test_solarGS98_difrotmixper18p4d1p0.inlist#L311) (`mixing_velocity_scale = 0.371`); the paper (`YREC_Public_Data_Release_Paper_revised.pdf`, section 3.1): "Solar models including rotation also reproduce the solar equatorial rotation rate (25.4 days) and the difference between the meteoritic and the current solar surface ⁷Li abundance (2.3 dex) within 1 percent. These are achieved by varying the scaling constant in the magnetized wind and the efficiency of mixing relative to angular momentum transport, respectively."
- **What is wrong:** the deck gives 2.086 dex for 2.3 ± 0.023: 0.21 dex short. The repository's three other rotating solar decks carry mixing efficiencies of their own (0.115 in `Test_solarGS98_difrotmixper18p4d0p1`, 0.780 in `Test_solarGS98_difrotmixsolidper18p4d1p0`, `FC = 0.519` in `examples/run_standard_solar_model/Test_solar_GS_rot_gray_OPALSCV_SF2_GS98_OP_CF10`); none of them was measured.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a deck that stands for the paper's calibration reproduces it.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed: the authors recalibrate `mixing_velocity_scale` on the current code (the paper's `solar_rot_calibrated.py`), for the four decks, each measured and its pin re-seeded; the expected failure's mark is removed with the testsuite deck's.

### M365. Which Opacity Project data is GS98.OP17? It is 0.7 to 1.6% above MESA's OP_gs98 at log T 6.2 to 6.8 (a question for the authors)

- **Status:** open, a question for the authors and not a code defect. The validation tier's V8, measured in its MESA comparison (`sample_cases/solar_vs_MESA/README.md`; no test fails on it: the comparison's bands hold it). The file was read for the registration. No kind until it is answered (a changed table is Kind B for every deck that reads it).
- **In the original F77?** The import holds the file: its `input/opacity/opal95/GS98.OP17` is the blob of today's `input/opacity/atomic/legacy/opal95/GS98.OP17` and `input/opacity/atomic/op05/GS98.OP17`.
- **Now:** [input/opacity/atomic/op05/GS98.OP17](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/input/opacity/atomic/op05/GS98.OP17); the comparison, [sample_cases/solar_vs_MESA/README.md](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/sample_cases/solar_vs_MESA/README.md).
- **What is known:**
  - At the nodes the two codes' tables share (X = 0.7, Z = 0.02, log R = −1.5 and −2), YREC's table equals MESA's `OP_gs98` at log T ≥ 7.0 and is 0.7 to 1.6% higher between log T = 6.2 and 6.8. Along the two solar-age models, at equal temperature, YREC's opacity is higher by 0.3% at log T = 7.0, rising to 3.1% just below the convection zone.
  - It is more than half of YREC's offset from MESA: MESA with its opacity raised by 2.5% between log T = 6.3 and 6.75 loses 0.0059 dex in log L at X_c = 0.6 (63% of the 0.0094 dex offset; 73% at X_c = 0.35; 54% of 0.0141 at 4.568 Gyr).
  - The file does not name its source. Its header reads "Updated OPAL Rosseland mean opacity tables (date 20050312)", in OPAL's Type 1 layout, with the composition label 200503120009. Beside it are `GS98.OP17.old` (another blob; equal to it at the comparison's nodes to the three decimals of the tables) and `GS98.OPAL17` (up to 0.02 dex away there).
  - Not determined: which Opacity Project release the file holds and how it was put on the OPAL grid, and which of the two tables is the data as published.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a table's provenance is recorded with it, so that a difference from another code's can be traced.
- **What we did:** recorded. Proposed: the authors say how the file was made (the release, the mixture, the tool), and that goes into a note beside the table; if the table is replaced, that is a measured change for every deck that reads it.

### M366. 319 shipped decks build the fixed-Z opacity table at a Z their model does not have, so the table is never used

- **Status:** open (decks). The validation tier's V10, which named two decks; counted for the registration over the 1,183 `.inlist` and `.nml1` deck files. No effect that matters: the tier measured 1.2e-6 dex in log L at 4.568 Gyr between a table at 0.016232 and one at the model's 0.016492 (the benchmark deck, in scratch). Kind B at that size where a deck's value changes, Kind A for a comment; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes, in its decks: the import's `examples/run_from_dbl_to_zams/Test_m0030_noGS_ZAMS.nml1` and its siblings set `ZOPAL951 = 0.016232` with `RSCLZ(1) = 0.016492`.
- **Now:** the lookup's choice of table, [opal95_opacity.f90:417-431](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/kap/opal95/opal95_opacity.f90#L417-L431), and its tolerance, [opacity_tables.f90:82](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/kap/opacity_tables.f90#L82); a deck, [Test_solar_noGS_norot.nml1:27](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/examples/run_standard_solar_model/Test_solar_noGS_norot.nml1#L27) and [:66](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/examples/run_standard_solar_model/Test_solar_noGS_norot.nml1#L66).
- **What is wrong:**
  - The fixed-Z table ("Generate a surface mixture table with this Z. Speeds up models without diffusion") is used only where the point's Z is within 1e-4 (relative) of the table's. 319 decks (316 `.inlist`, 3 `.nml1`: 156 under `examples/`, 139 under `sample_cases/`, 22 in `testsuite/`, 2 under `src/`) rescale to a positive Z that differs from their table's by more: 0.016492 with a table at 0.016232 (139 decks), 0.01822371 with 0.018126 (92), 0.018804 with 0.018777 (56), and eleven other pairs (32). In them no lookup can take the table (without diffusion the model's Z stays where the rescale put it; with it, it moves): every lookup interpolates in Z as well, and the table is built and not used.
  - M224's status line says `opal95_single_table_z` "is 0 in every shipped deck". It is positive in 1,182 of the 1,183; what was latent there is a value between 0.08 and 0.10.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a setting does what its comment says, or the comment says what it does.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed, the authors' choice: each deck's table at its model's Z (a change of 1e-6 dex, measured per deck, its pin re-seeded), or the values kept and the decks' comment corrected.

### M367. Output documentation: delta_nu is not the observed large separation, the GYRE and GSM files carry no G, the atmosphere's heights are plane-parallel, and two history columns state no unit

- **Status:** fixed in part in round 3 (2026-11-18, [05d5bf20](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/05d5bf20) (the tests agent, io) and [c7cb92ae](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/c7cb92ae) (the core2 agent, the envelope kernel); byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins); open: stitched_model's header and observables' "int_0^R" (M362). At the registration: open (doc). The validation tier's V7, V11 and V12 and its note on `cz_bot_radius`, each read in the code. Kind A; size S.
- **In the original F77?** No, for the columns and the files: [bf3d5070](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/bf3d5070) (2026-08-29) added `delta_nu`, [9df62b7e](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/9df62b7e) (2026-08-20) the GYRE file. The atmosphere's depth step is the F77's ([envint.f:330-331](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/envint.f#L330-L331), "SEE J.P. COX PRINC. OF STELL. STRUC. P590").
- **Now:** [history_columns.list:28-29](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/defaults/history_columns.list#L28-L29) and [:105](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/defaults/history_columns.list#L105); FGONG's G, [pulsation_output.f90:86](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/io/pulsation_output.f90#L86); the default G, [physical_constants.f90:59-62](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/state/physical_constants.f90#L59-L62); io's README, [README.md:92](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/io/README.md#L92); the depth step, [envelope_integration_kernel.f90:653-663](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L653-L663); the two columns' values, [history_output.f90:253-254](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/io/history_output.f90#L253-L254).
- **What is wrong:**
  - `delta_nu` (V7) is 142.68 μHz on the standard solar model, 5.1% above GYRE's radial large separation of the same model at n = 15 to 25, 135.77, because the sound-travel integral stops at the photosphere (through the atmosphere the file holds it is 137.83; MESA's `delta_nu` has the same definition, 141.89 for its model). The column list says "asymptotic p-mode large separation [uHz] (sound-travel-time integral, center -> photosphere)", so the tier's "the description does not warn" is half right: it names the photosphere and does not say that the number is 5% above what one observes, which bf3d5070's own message knew ("the known ~5% above the observed 135"). `delta_nu_rho` is the column within 0.5%.
  - G (V12): the GYRE text and GSM formats have no G (FGONG has it). YREC's default, 6.67252e-8, is 2.7e-4 from GYRE's, so a user who does not set `&constants G_GRAVITY` gives GYRE a model that is out of equilibrium by 2.7e-4. io's README says so since the tier; `pulse_format`'s description, which a deck writer reads, does not.
  - The atmosphere's heights (V11) are 0.1 to 0.6% of a step from hydrostatic equilibrium (6e-6 R over the atmosphere): the gravity is the photosphere's (plane-parallel; 2.5e-3 at the top) and the depth step is dτ over the mean of ρκ (1e-3). The contract test's tolerance holds it; the files' description does not state it.
  - `cz_bot_radius` and `cz_bot_mass` are in Rsun and Msun, with no comment in the column list; the tier first read the radius as r/R.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a column's description lets a user compare it with an observation or hand the file to another code.
- **What we did:** recorded. Proposed fix: the column list's three lines (the generated files follow), `pulse_format`'s description (the G to give GYRE), and a sentence on the plane-parallel atmosphere in stitched_model's header and io's README.
- **Round 3 (2026-11-18), io:** `history_columns.list` says that `delta_nu` is about 5% above the observed large separation and why (the integral stops at the photosphere; the innermost point; MESA's is the same; `delta_nu_rho` or a pulsation code for a comparison), and gives `cz_bot_mass` and `cz_bot_radius` their units; `pulsation_output.f90`'s header and its GYRE and GSM writers say that the two formats carry no G, which G the model is in equilibrium for and what to give GYRE; `pulse_format`'s description (and with it `physics.defaults` and `controls_registry.md`) says the same; `G_cgs`'s description gave the default as 6.6726e-8 and now gives 6.67252e-8 (M400) ([05d5bf20](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/05d5bf20)).
- **Round 3 (2026-11-18), the envelope:** `store_atmosphere_point`'s comment states the plane-parallel gravity (2.5e-3 at the top), the trapezoid in tau (1e-3) and the measured 0.6% of a step (6e-6 R) ([c7cb92ae](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/c7cb92ae)). Left: stitched_model's header (core/diagnostics) and observables.f90's "int_0^R" (M362).

### M368. Beyond SCV's high-pressure edge the blend joins a Saha solution 0.45 dex denser: the density rises outward across the ramp

- **Status:** open. The convergence round's D1; its scan was read again for the registration (the work directory's `scratch_b2_conv/scan/eos_d_m0030rr.txt`), which corrects the hand-back's place and sign. No shipped deck reaches it within its stop: `Test_m0030_feh0_noGS_ZAMS` does with its 50-model cap lifted, at model 782 (67 Gyr). Kind B for a model that reaches it; size M, and physics for the authors.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. Outside SCV's table the Saha result stood ([eqscve.f:36-39](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqscve.f#L36-L39), M88's quote); the step at the edge became a ramp with M88's fix ([a0039581](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/a0039581), 2026-11-12).
- **Now:** `scv_edge_weight`, [scv_eos.f90:81-123](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/eos/scv/scv_eos.f90#L81-L123) (the hand-back has it in blended_eos.f90, which calls it).
- **What is wrong:** SCV's tables end at log P_gas = 11.4 on the rows up to log T = 3.70 (13.6 above), and the weight takes SCV out over 0.2 dex below a top that is linear in log T between the rows. Beyond it the equation of state is the Saha solution, which at these pressures gives a gas without ionization (∇_ad = 0.400) 0.45 dex denser than SCV's. Along the 0.03 Msun model at 67 Gyr, going outward: at log T = 3.7189, log P = 11.719 the blend has log ρ = −0.289 and ∇_ad = 0.198 (SCV's); at log T = 3.7097, log P = 11.679 it has log ρ = +0.157 and ∇_ad = 0.400 (Saha's). The density rises by 0.45 dex while the pressure falls by 0.04 dex: the hand-back's "slope dln ρ/dln P about 10" is −11 along the model, continuous, and a density inversion. The solve cycles there, with 190 to 290 convective flags flipping at each iteration.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** along a model the density falls with the pressure; where one table ends, what takes over describes the same matter.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed: the authors decide what holds beyond SCV's high-pressure edge below log T = 3.7 (a stop with a message, as M42's for β ≤ 0, or an equation of state with pressure ionization); a `test_eos` check that the density is monotonic in pressure across the ramp then pins it. Nothing until then: no shipped deck reaches it within its stop.

### M369. The OPAL 2006 interpolant's pressure jumps in density, by 1e-5 to 4e-4, near the table's high-density edge

- **Status:** open. The convergence round's D2, the half of M357 that its fix left: the density search now takes the jump's density, and the jump stays. Shown by `test_eos`'s check "OPAL 2006: the density search finds a density at every pressure across a jump of the table's" (T6 = 0.94974) and by the note each low-mass run logs once. Confirmed by reading. Kind B for the low-mass decks that meet it; size M.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. ESAC06 chooses its stencil from the coverage sums ([esac06.f:340-389](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/esac06.f#L340-L389)).
- **Now:** `interpolate_opal_eos`, [opal_eos.f90:533-850](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/eos/opal/opal_eos.f90#L533-L850) (the stencil's choice, [:689-712](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/eos/opal/opal_eos.f90#L689-L712)); the search's note, [:452-463](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/eos/opal/opal_eos.f90#L452-L463).
- **What is wrong:** near the table's ragged edge the stencil shrinks or shifts where a larger one would take an empty entry. The choice changes from one density to the next, and the interpolated pressure with it, by 1e-5 to 4e-4 at isolated densities. For a pressure inside such a jump no density matches; M357 returns the jump's density, so the pressure the EOS implies differs from the one asked for by that much, and the other interpolated quantities change with the stencil too (not measured).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** an interpolant that is continuous in its arguments.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: blend the two stencils across the cell where the choice changes (as the interpolator blends its overlapping quadratics inside the table), or keep the smaller stencil wherever either is allowed; measured on `test_low_mass_decks`' six decks and `Test_m0030_feh0_noGS_ZAMS`'s pin.

### M370. The OPAL density search returns "not in the table" without a message when any trial density falls outside the table

- **Status:** open. The convergence round's D3, confirmed by reading; not measured further (the round saw alternating "lookup does not cover" and "outside the edge" states along a 0.04 Msun model between log T = 5.55 and 5.90, where both give SCV, so no jump was traced to it). Kind B where it changes which equation of state a point takes, Kind A elsewhere; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. Every trial call of RHOOFP06 leaves by the error exit ([rhoofp06.f:74-75](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/rhoofp06.f#L74-L75), [:82](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/rhoofp06.f#L82), [:88](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/rhoofp06.f#L88), [:96](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/rhoofp06.f#L96)):
  ```fortran
        rhog1=rho(nra(klo))*pnr/pmax
        call esac06 (x,ztab,t6,rhog1,1,0,*999)
  ```
- **Now:** `trial_pressure`, [opal_eos.f90:478-492](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/eos/opal/opal_eos.f90#L478-L492), and its four uses, [:405](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/eos/opal/opal_eos.f90#L405), [:414](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/eos/opal/opal_eos.f90#L414), [:421](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/eos/opal/opal_eos.f90#L421) and [:436](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/eos/opal/opal_eos.f90#L436).
- **What is wrong:** the search's bracket starts from a guess (the row's highest density scaled by P over the pressure there), shrinks by 0.2 or grows by 5, and then moves by regula falsi and bisection. A trial density that the interpolator calls outside the table ends the search with `opal_rho_not_found` and ierr = 0, and no line. Whether a point near the edge takes OPAL then depends on where the guesses land, not on whether the table holds the answer.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the search fails only when the table does not bracket the pressure, and says so when it gives up.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: a trial outside the table pulls that end of the bracket back toward the last trial inside it; a run-log line when the search gives up for that reason; a `test_eos` check at a point near the edge, with its mutation.

### M371. The OPAL 1995 and 2001 edge ramp takes the table's edge from the row below the point: by reading, the weight steps at every T6 row where the edge column changes

- **Status:** open, latent: no shipped deck sets `use_opal95_eos` or `use_opal2001_eos` (0 of 1,196, counted). The convergence round's D6, which it listed as not examined; read for the registration, and by that reading it is M356's kind of jump. Not run. Kind B for a deck on those tables; size M.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. EQBOUND01 has the edge's interpolation in T6 commented out ([eqbound01.f:49-57](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/eqbound01.f#L49-L57)):
  ```fortran
  C DEFINE TABLE EDGE IN RHO BY LINEAR INTERPOLATION.
        DLIM = RMX(KT+1)
  C      DLIM = RMX(KT+1)+FT*(RMX(KT)-RMX(KT+1))
  ```
- **Now:** `find_opal_ramp`, [opal_eos_tables.f90:529-562](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/eos/opal_eos_tables.f90#L529-L562) (the edge and the ramp's start from row `t_row_index+1`, [:529-535](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/eos/opal_eos_tables.f90#L529-L535)); the edge columns, [:143-152](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/eos/opal_eos_tables.f90#L143-L152); its caller, [opal_eos.f90:266-288](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/eos/opal/opal_eos.f90#L266-L288).
- **What is wrong:** the edge density and the ramp's start are those of the row below the point, constant between two T6 rows, and both tables' edges are ragged (2001's edge column goes 159, 143, 137, 134 ...; 1995's 77, 76, 74 ...). Across a T6 row where the column changes, the edge density steps, so a point at a fixed density changes its weight by a jump: from a value in the ramp, or from 1, to outside the table (weight 0), or between two ramps. M356 made the 2006 table's weight continuous; these two were not touched.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** as M356: an equation of state continuous in (T, P).
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: M356's interpolant of node weights for the two vintages (or the edge linear in T6, the F77's commented line), with `test_eos` checks either side of a row where the edge steps; it moves no shipped deck.

### M372. Two 0.03 Msun decks' stops: the Allard deck asks for 15 Gyr and leaves its atmosphere tables at 1.1 Gyr, and the noGS deck's 50-model cap gives a reason that no longer holds

- **Status:** open, the authors' decisions ("Decisions needed"). The convergence round's questions 1 and 5 and its D5; the facts are in M294's and O3's entries, which stay as they are, and this is the open item for them. Kind B for the two decks' own outputs (`Test_m0030_feh0_noGS_ZAMS` is pinned); size S.
- **In the original F77?** No. The Allard deck is the YREC team's ([74ae5206](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/74ae5206), 2026-02-24); the cap and its comment are 2026's ([e16b304a](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/e16b304a), 2026-10-12, "examples: the 0.03 Msun deck gets a stop it can reach").
- **Now:** [Test_m0p03feh+0p0GS98_allard_15Gyr.inlist:42-46](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/testsuite/Test_m0p03feh+0p0GS98_allard_15Gyr.inlist#L42-L46) and its `atm_choice`, [:220](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/testsuite/Test_m0p03feh+0p0GS98_allard_15Gyr.inlist#L220); atm's message, [atm_messages.f90:157](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/atm/atm_messages.f90#L157); [Test_m0030_feh0_noGS_ZAMS.inlist:38](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/examples/run_from_dbl_to_zams/Test_m0030_feh0_noGS_ZAMS.inlist#L38).
- **What is wrong:**
  - `testsuite/Test_m0p03feh+0p0GS98_allard_15Gyr` asks for 15 Gyr with the Allard tables. Since M356 it runs to model 359 (1.107 Gyr) and ends with "atm_get_surface_pt: log Teff = 2.907046 is below the Allard tables (log Teff 2.908485 to 4.008774)", exit 1: a 0.03 Msun brown dwarf cools below 810 K. No solve fails. (Above the tables a run switches to the gray atmosphere; below them it stops.) The deck is in no test.
  - `examples/run_from_dbl_to_zams/Test_m0030_feh0_noGS_ZAMS` stops at 50 models, with the comment "the Newton solve fails later in the contraction in every YREC version (the original after about 210 models), so stop at 50". Since M356 and M357 it runs to model 782 (67 Gyr) with the cap lifted, where M368 stops it.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a shipped deck reaches the stop it names, and its comments describe the code it ships with.
- **What we did:** recorded, not changed. Proposed, the convergence round's recommendations: the Allard deck gets a stop it can reach (an age of 1 Gyr, or a `Teff_lower_limit` just above the tables' edge; a gray atmosphere below the tables is physics for the authors); the noGS deck's cap becomes an age and its comment is corrected, which moves its pin.
- **Round 3 (2026-11-18):** `Test_m0030_feh0_noGS_ZAMS`'s comment on its 50-model cap was corrected ([ee572e13](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/ee572e13), the tests agent): the solve no longer fails; with the cap lifted the deck runs to model 782 (67 Gyr), where M368 stops it. The cap stays (the decision is open). The deck's row of `src/io/test/expected_controls/hashes.txt` did not move: the hash is of the controls the deck reads, not of its text. The Allard deck's stop is unchanged.

### M373. test_controls' Monte Carlo test needs an untracked directory beside the deck, and writes into it

- **Status:** fixed in round 3 (2026-11-18, [202a0bd9](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/202a0bd9), the tests agent; byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins). At the registration: open (test). The convergence round's D7, which its hand-back left untraced as "a copy of the tree without .git"; traced and reproduced for the registration: the cause is not git but the directory `examples/run_config_matrix/output/`. Kind A; size S.
- **In the original F77?** No: the test is 2026's (M115's).
- **Before the fix** (at the registration): [test_controls.py:470-498](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/test_controls.py#L470-L498) (the read runs in the deck's directory, [:490](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/test_controls.py#L490)); the deck's relative names, [cm_monte_carlo.inlist:86-88](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/examples/run_config_matrix/cm_monte_carlo.inlist#L86-L88); `open_run_files`, [run_files.f90:102-115](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/io/run_files.f90#L102-L115); the ignore rule, [.gitignore:8](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/.gitignore#L8); CI's step, [ci.yml:143-147](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L143-L147).
- **What is wrong:** the test's "shipped" case expects ierr = 0 from a read of `cm_monte_carlo.inlist`, and the read opens the deck's Monte Carlo files, named `output/cm_monte_carlo.mc1` and `.mc2` relative to the deck's directory. That directory is ignored by git: it exists only once something has run the configuration matrix in the tree. In a fresh clone, a new worktree or a copy made without ignored files the read stops with "ERROR: cannot open the Monte Carlo summary file output/cm_monte_carlo.mc1 ... No such file or directory", ierr = 1, and the test fails (reproduced in the registration's worktree, which has no such directory; with the directory the same read gives ierr = 0). CI makes the directory in a step of its own, whose comment says why; a local run has no such step. Where the directory exists and the two files do not, the test leaves them there, empty, in the repository's tree.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a test passes in a fresh checkout and writes only under its temporary directory.
- **Proposed at the registration:** the test copies the deck and `mc_input.dat` to `tmp_path`, makes `output/` there and runs there; CI's step goes. M313 is the same deck's relative names met by coverage.py.
- **What we did:** round 3 (2026-11-18, [202a0bd9](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/202a0bd9)): `test_controls.py` reads every deck from a stand-in for the deck's directory (`harness.stand_in_directory`: a link to each file beside the deck and an empty `output/`, in a temporary directory), and the Monte Carlo range test does the same and checks that the shipped range's two files appear there; `devel_tests.py` runs its deck cases the same way. CI's step "Make the decks' output directories" is gone. Shown in a fresh clone with CI's sparse checkout: CI's pytest list at the parent commit gave `test_controls_every_deck` and the Monte Carlo range test failing and left six stray entries (the Monte Carlo pair's directory, four empty `.mod` files in `startmodels/`, exercise 2's `output/samplecases/`); at the branch's head the list passes (149 passed, 2 skipped, 6 xfailed, plain and with `YREC_TEST_TOLERANT=1`) and `git status --short --ignored` gains only Python's `__pycache__/` and `.pytest_cache/`.

### M374. Four test files and two tools read another tree's tables and starting models when the shell exports YREC_INPUT and YREC_START

- **Status:** fixed in round 3 (2026-11-18, [8d55689f](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/8d55689f), the tests agent; byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins). At the registration: open (test harness). The integrator's item, corrected after reading: the binary under test is not affected. Kind A; size S.
- **In the original F77?** No. conftest.py's `setdefault` is 2026's ([7f1fa4dd](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/7f1fa4dd), 2026-08-29).
- **Before the fix** (at the registration): [conftest.py:23-30](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/conftest.py#L23-L30); the files that pass the environment on without roots of their own, [test_controls.py:63](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/test_controls.py#L63), [test_structure.py:69](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/test_structure.py#L69), [test_envelope_integration.py:43](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/test_envelope_integration.py#L43) and [test_other_energy.py:33](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/test_other_energy.py#L33); the tools, [devel_tests.py:94-96](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/tools/devel_tests.py#L94-L96) and [mutate.py:122-124](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/tools/mutate.py#L122-L124); the validation tier's own fix, [validate_model.py:543-547](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/src/tools/validate_model.py#L543-L547); CI's one use, [ci.yml:266-269](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/078df658/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L266-L269).
- **What is wrong:**
  - conftest.py sets `YREC_INPUT` and `YREC_START` to its own tree "unless the caller already did". On a machine whose shell exports them for one tree (the owner's does, for the main tree), a pytest run in a second worktree leaves them pointing at the first. About twenty test files set their own tree's roots and are not affected. Four do not: `test_controls.py` (the decks' paths and the starting model it opens; the dump writes the roots as placeholders, so it passes either way), and `test_structure.py`, `test_envelope_integration.py` and `test_other_energy.py`, whose programs read the other tree's tables (the first and the last its starting models too); so do `devel_tests.py` and `mutate.py`, which use `setdefault` too. Nothing says so. The results are the same while the two trees' `input/` and `startmodels/` are (they are today); a branch that changes a table or regenerates a starting model (M316's open question) would be tested against the old files.
  - Corrected from the item as reported, which had the tests run the first tree's binary through `YREC_EXE`: no test, tool or workflow reads `YREC_EXE` at 078df658 (the validation tier's five files did, and [13c55097](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/13c55097) removed it before the merge). Every test runs its own tree's binaries. CI is not affected: its build-and-test job sets neither variable, and its solar job sets both to its workspace.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a test run tests its own tree, and says what it ran.
- **Proposed at the registration:** conftest.py sets both roots to its own tree unless an explicit opt-in names others, prints the binary's directory and the two roots in pytest's header, and warns when one is outside the repository; the four files and the two tools take the same roots.
- **What we did:** round 3 (2026-11-18, [8d55689f](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/8d55689f)): `src/tools/harness.py` holds the rule: `resolve` gives the repository's `input/` and `startmodels/` whatever the environment names, and the environment's `YREC_INPUT` and `YREC_START` only under the one opt-in, `YREC_TEST_EXTERNAL_ROOTS=1` (for a worktree without the 3 GB `input/`). conftest.py sets the two for every program a test starts, offers them as `INPUT_ROOT` and `START_ROOT`, and prints in pytest's header the binaries' directory, the two roots, whose they are, and each value of the environment that was not used. `devel_tests.py`, `mutate.py` and `validate_model.py` apply the same rule (the first two print the same lines). The twenty-four root test files that built `REPO / "input"` or `REPO / "startmodels"` themselves import the two names instead, so the opt-in and the header hold for every root test but `test_element_diffusion.py`, which is not to be edited and keeps its own tree's `input/`. `test_harness.py` (new, in CI's list) holds the rule: the function's cases, conftest.py imported by a fresh interpreter under an environment that names another checkout, the two tools' report, and a scan that no root test or tool builds its own tree's roots or keeps the environment's (`setdefault`). Shown on the owner's machine (the shell exports the main tree's two roots): with a clone's `input/eos/yale/FERMI.TAB` renamed, `test_envelope_integration.py` and `test_other_energy.py` passed before the fix (they read the main tree's table) and fail after it ("eos_init: cannot open the Fermi-Dirac table <clone>/input/eos/yale/FERMI.TAB"); with `YREC_TEST_EXTERNAL_ROOTS=1` they pass, and the header says "NOT this repository's". CI sets neither variable in its pytest and devel jobs and is unchanged but for the new file's name in the list. Not covered: `src/tools/coverage.py`'s test programs (M382).

## 22. Found in round 3 (2026-11-18)

Round 3 took the packages the eighth evaluation left under 8, kap and core, to its work lists (`audit/module-evaluation-8-2026-11-17/SUMMARY.md`, "What is left under 8"), with five agents in parallel on disjoint directories: kap, core1 (core/step and core/run), core2 (core/envelope), core3 (core/model and core/diagnostics) and tests (the test harness, the validation tier's sources, output descriptions). Every commit was byte-identical on the 56 decks, the 35 pins and the unit tests' pins; a defect fix that would move one went on the agent's B list, measured. The five hand-backs listed new defects; these items are those, in the agents' order: kap (M375-M382), core1 (M383-M387), core2 (M388-M393), core3 (M394-M398) and tests (M399-M401), with one of the round's integrator (M402) and one the closing agent found while merging the READMEs (M403). Four were fixed in the round (M388, M389 and M400 by their commits, M392 by its removal); the rest are open. Each entry records what is wrong, the input that triggers it, the proposed fix, its kind (A, byte-identical on every deck and pin; B, a change of results or of pinned text) and its size (S, M or L).

- **How they were checked.** Every item was read again in the code at the merged tree, [7ea92ace](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/7ea92ace), and against the F77 at 6cd56739, before its entry was written; the fixed ones at their parent commit, 2ff65f9d. The agents' measurements (probes, scratch decks, unit tests) are theirs and were not run again. Where the check refined an agent's account, the entry says so: M382, M386, M396 and M402.
- **One entry for one defect.** coverage.py's test programs without the tree's roots were found by the kap agent, the core2 agent and the integrator: M382. The integrator's first finding, compare_decks' version line in a tree without .git, is M301, open since round 1B: a dated line there, no new entry. The tests agent's two documentation corrections (a control's description, the tier's citations) are one entry, M400.
- **Not entered.** test_controls.py's one docstring line of about 150 characters (the tests agent's item 5: cosmetic). The atomic-weight tables that differ and `years_per_gyr` written four times (the core1 agent's B6): decisions and a constant, on `notes/R3_B_LIST.md` in the work directory. Claims of the brief or the evaluation that the agents found wrong are corrected in their entries (M322, M324, M339, M343, M202) and in `docs/ROADMAP.md`'s round 3 section.
- Current-code links point at [7ea92ace](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/tree/7ea92ace/src).

### M375. Above the Alexander tables' top log R the returned derivatives are not the returned value's

- **Status:** open. Found by the kap agent (hand-back §6, item 1) while counting M342. Measured with a probe (`scratch_r3_kap/probe/kap_probe2`, X = 0.70, Z = 0.016232, the returned derivatives against a centred difference of log κ): at log T 3.9954 and log R 1.2 to 3.74, dln κ/dln ρ 0.4154 for 0.3879 (7%), dln κ/dln T 7.07 for 7.15 (log R 1.2) to 3.61 for 3.69 (log R 3.74); at log T 3.62, 0.6130 for 0.6183 and 7.82 for 7.80; inside the table (log R 0.8) the two agree to four digits. **Reached by shipped decks:** the 0.03 Msun chain (Test_m0030_feh0_noGS_ZAMS up to log R 3.79 at log T 3.97 to 4.0; m0030gs98z018804_prems 2.98; m0030gs98z018804_Dbl 3.03: M342's count). Kind B (the low-mass decks' Jacobian; expected at the size of their convergence path); size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes. GETALEX06 extrapolates the value with the last two columns and keeps the Lagrange derivative ([getalex06.f:91-108](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/getalex06.f#L91-L108)):
  ```fortran
           QOPR(I) = FXRD(1)*CAPALEX06(II,ID) +
  ...
        IF(LINEAR)THEN
           DO I = 1,4
              II = IT+I-1
              OP(I) = OP(I)+(RR-R)*(CAPALEX06(II,NUMD)-
       *      CAPALEX06(II,NUMD-1))/(R0GR06(NUMD)-R0GR06(NUMD-1))
  ```
- **Now:** `alex_table_at_point`, [opacity_tables.f90:436-469](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/kap/opacity_tables.f90#L436-L469): the rows' value carried on with the secant, [:458-465](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/kap/opacity_tables.f90#L458-L465), and their d log κ/d log R the cubic's at the edge, [:453-456](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/kap/opacity_tables.f90#L453-L456); its header says so, [:425-435](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/kap/opacity_tables.f90#L425-L435). (Before [7df328b6](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/7df328b6) the same block was in `compute_alex06_opacity` and `compute_alex94_opacity`.)
- **What is wrong:** above the top log R column (1.0) each T row's log κ is extended linearly with the slope of its last two columns, but the row's d log κ/d log R stays the 4-point cubic's derivative at the edge, so dln κ/dln ρ (and through it dln κ/dln T at fixed ρ) is not the derivative of the value returned.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a returned derivative is the derivative of the returned value (test_kap's rule for every family).
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: where a row is extrapolated, its d log κ/d log R is the secant it is extrapolated with. test_kap's "above its top log R: linear from the last two" pins the value's rule for both families; a derivative check there would hold the fix.

### M376. OPAL 1995's log κ jumps where a T row passes from the cubic of its last four columns to the linear extrapolation

- **Status:** open. Found by the kap agent (hand-back §6, item 2). Measured with a probe (`scratch_r3_kap/probe/kap_probe`, OPAL 1995 alone, X = 0.70, Z = 0.016232, log κ just below and just above the handover, ierr 0): -6.6e-3 at log T 7.45, log R 0.0; -5.0e-3 at log T 7.65, log R 0.0; -1.7e-2 at log T 7.95, log R -0.5; +1.5e-3 at log T 8.60, log R -1.0. Reached where log R lies more than a column beyond a row's last filled column, at log T above 7.2 (dense helium cores, where conduction dominates); none of the 16 decks of M342's count reaches it. Kind B where reached; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: GETOPAL95's two regimes, a row whose second column is empty marked for linear extrapolation from its last column ([getopal95.f:143-157](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/getopal95.f#L143-L157), [:196-215](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/getopal95.f#L196-L215)).
- **Now:** `shift_rows_off_empty_corner`, [opal95_opacity.f90:414-456](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/kap/opal95/opal95_opacity.f90#L414-L456) (the rows marked, [:432-438](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/kap/opal95/opal95_opacity.f90#L432-L438)); `opal95_logr_weights`, [:466-499](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/kap/opal95/opal95_opacity.f90#L466-L499); `extrapolate_in_logr`, [:651-671](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/kap/opal95/opal95_opacity.f90#L651-L671).
- **What is wrong:** with the rows shifted at the high-R corner, a row whose point lies up to one column beyond its last filled column is evaluated by the cubic of its last four columns at the point (an extrapolation of the cubic), and a row whose point lies further is evaluated at its last column and carried on linearly with the cubic's slope there. The two rules meet one column beyond the last filled one and do not agree there, so log κ is discontinuous in log R by up to 0.017 dex.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** κ continuous in (ρ, T), as the solver needs.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed; kap/README's "Kept by decision, or open" states it. Proposed fix: one rule beyond a row's last column (linear from the last column with the cubic's slope there, from the column on), or the README's statement as it is.

### M377. OPAL 1992's refusal of an X off its tables' grid cannot be reached: the X is extrapolated with ierr 0

- **Status:** open. Found by the kap agent (hand-back §6, item 3) when finding 7e's check could not be written. Latent: no shipped deck uses OPAL 1992. Kind A to delete the dead branches, B to refuse an X outside the grid; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: YLLO3D tests `M1.LE.0` after the same sign flip ([yllo3d.f:49-53](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/yllo3d.f#L49-L53)):
  ```fortran
        CALL FINDEX(GRIDX,NUMX,X,M1)
        IF(M1.LT.0)M1=-M1
  ...
        IF(M1.LE.0)STOP ' ERROR IN X GRID'
  ```
- **Now:** `build_opal92_surface_rows`, [opal92_opacity.f90:176-183](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/kap/opal92/opal92_opacity.f90#L176-L183), and `compute_opal92_opacity`, [:274-283](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/kap/opal92/opal92_opacity.f90#L274-L283); `findex` returns -1 below the grid and -n at or above its last point, never 0 ([table_interpolation.f90:298-319](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/numerics/table_interpolation.f90#L298-L319)).
- **What is wrong:** both places take the absolute value of `findex`'s index and clamp it to 2 before testing `<= 0`, so the test never holds: an X below 0 or above 0.7 is extrapolated linearly from two tables with ierr 0, and `kap_update_surface_tables`' error return cannot be reached with any table `kap_init` accepts.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a test either can fire or is not there; an X a table cannot serve is refused (M236's rule).
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: delete the two dead branches and state the extrapolation in kap/README (A), or refuse an X outside [0, 1] (B).

### M378. OPAL 1995's X = 0.95 table at Z = 0.04 is read but never used

- **Status:** open. Found by the kap agent (hand-back §6, item 4) while fixing M339. The files hold it (TABLE #114 of `GS98.OP17`, X = 0.9500, Z = 0.0400; `num_x_at_z(10)` = 10), but the stencils treat Z >= 0.04 as without it. Consistent between the paths since M339, so no path disagrees with another; the comments' "X = 0.95 exists below Z = 0.04 only" (which the evaluation's finding 2 repeats) is inexact. Kind B to use it (X > 0.8 at Z = 0.04 only); size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: OP95XTAB's `ZTAB.LE.0.04D0` and GETOPAL95's `ZZ.GE.0.04D0` branches ([op95xtab.f:46](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/op95xtab.f#L46), [getopal95.f:352](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/getopal95.f#L352)).
- **Now:** `no_x095_from_z`, [opal95_opacity.f90:42](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/kap/opal95/opal95_opacity.f90#L42); the fixed-Z table's slot 9 built below Z = 0.04 only, [:117-129](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/kap/opal95/opal95_opacity.f90#L117-L129); the stencils' `z_here >= no_x095_from_z`, [:521](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/kap/opal95/opal95_opacity.f90#L521); `num_x_at_z`, [opacity_tables.f90:164-165](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/kap/opacity_tables.f90#L164-L165).
- **What is wrong:** at a Z row of exactly 0.04 with X >= 0.8 the 4D path takes tables 6, 7, 8 and 10 where 7 to 10 exist, so the X = 0.95 table there is loaded and never read.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a stencil takes the tables that exist at its Z.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed; kap/README's "Kept by decision" states it. Proposed fix: `>` where the stencils test 0.04, and slot 9 built at Z = 0.04 (B), or the comments corrected (A).

### M379. A lookup in Alexander 1994 at another Z rebuilds the surface table at the zone's X, not the envelope's

- **Status:** open. Found by the kap agent (hand-back §6, item 5). Latent: no shipped deck uses Alexander 1994. The values stay those of the zone's composition (the surface table is used at its own X only), so this is a cache that thrashes and an extrapolation rule that depends on the previous zone's X, with Z diffusion and Alexander 1994 together. Kind B to keep the envelope X; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: YALO3D calls ALXZTAB, then ALX8TH with the zone's X ([yalo3d.f:24-25](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/yalo3d.f#L24-L25)).
- **Now:** `compute_alex94_opacity`, [alex94_opacity.f90:143-146](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/kap/alex94/alex94_opacity.f90#L143-L146) (`build_alex94_surface_table(tbl, hydrogen_fraction)` with the zone's X); the extrapolation above the top log R at the surface X only, [:162-166](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/kap/alex94/alex94_opacity.f90#L162-L166).
- **What is wrong:** after one zone at another Z than the tables', the "surface X" is that zone's X until the next `kap_update_surface_tables`, and the linear extrapolation above the top log R, which applies at the surface X alone, follows it.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the surface table is the envelope's, as `kap_update_surface_tables` builds it.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: rebuild the surface table at the cached envelope X.

### M380. kap_eval's molecular result is undefined where no molecular family has a value

- **Status:** open. Found by the kap agent (hand-back §6, item 6): the mutation that drops the `have_molecular` test showed its content is whatever the stack held. No effect today: the result is not read then. Kind A; size S.
- **In the original F77?** No: kap_eval's steps are 2026's.
- **Now:** `evaluate_steps`, [kap_lib.f90:129-151](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/kap/kap_lib.f90#L129-L151); `molecular_opacity`, [:158-171](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/kap/kap_lib.f90#L158-L171); `kap_result`, no defaults, [opacity_source.f90:46-48](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/kap/opacity_source.f90#L46-L48).
- **What is wrong:** `molecular_result` is a local without a value; `molecular_opacity` returns without setting it when no molecular family is selected, when Kurucz 1990 has no value at the point, or on an ierr. The ramp reads it only under `have_molecular`, so a slip in that test would blend in undefined numbers without failing.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the code sets what it may read (M322's rule).
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: give it a defined value (κ = 0, or a default in `kap_result`), so that a slip fails loudly.

### M381. With OPAL 1995's rows shifted, a point below the first log R column would be extrapolated from an edge that branch does not set

- **Status:** open. Found by the kap agent (hand-back §6, item 7). Unreachable with the shipped tables: the corner needs log R near the top columns. Kind A; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: GETOPAL95 sets the low edge in the unshifted branch only ([getopal95.f:63-70](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/getopal95.f#L63-L70), [:196-215](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/getopal95.f#L196-L215)).
- **Now:** `opal95_logr_weights`, [opal95_opacity.f90:466-499](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/kap/opal95/opal95_opacity.f90#L466-L499) (`st%logr_lo_edge` set at [:478](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/kap/opal95/opal95_opacity.f90#L478) only); `extrapolate_in_logr` tests `extrap_lo` first, [:658-662](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/kap/opal95/opal95_opacity.f90#L658-L662).
- **What is wrong:** if a point were both below the table's first column and in a shifted stencil, its rows' weights would be taken at the point (not at the edge) and the extrapolation would read an unset `logr_lo_edge`.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** each branch sets what the next step reads, or the two cases are exclusive by construction.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: set the edge in both branches, or make the two exclusive by construction.

### M382. coverage.py runs the test programs without the tree's table roots and takes a failing one as a figure

- **Status:** open (tool). Found three times in round 3: by the kap agent (hand-back §6, item 8: kap/README's command without YREC_INPUT, test_kap exits 1 and the tool still prints kap's coverage, 43.6%, from the decks alone), by the core2 agent (hand-back §4: in a copy outside the repository, test_envelope_integration exits 1 at `open_run_files` and contributes nothing) and by the integrator. Refined by reading: with the owner's shell the programs inherit `YREC_INPUT` and `YREC_START` naming the main tree (M374's kind, which conftest.py's fix does not reach), and a program that takes arguments (test_run_contracts, test_stitched) cannot be run at all, which is why run/'s figure leaves out what test_run_contracts runs. Kind A (tooling); size S.
- **In the original F77?** No: coverage.py is 2026's.
- **Now:** `run_tests`, [coverage.py:67-70](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/tools/coverage.py#L67-L70), against `run_decks`, which sets the two roots, [:73-91](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/tools/coverage.py#L73-L91); the docstring promises the roots for the decks only, [:8-10](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/tools/coverage.py#L8-L10).
- **What is wrong:** `run_tests` runs each program with the caller's environment, so it reads whatever tree `YREC_INPUT` and `YREC_START` name, or none; a program that fails prints only "exit 1", and the table that follows looks complete. Programs with arguments have no way in.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a coverage figure is of this tree, and a failed run is a failure.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed (kap/README's command sets the two variables). Proposed fix: `run_tests` sets the two roots as `run_decks` does (through `harness.resolve`, M374's rule), exits nonzero when a program fails, and takes `--test-args`. The deck half's own defect is M313.

### M383. With accretion and a cool mixed-region base, the Li/Be burn returns before the accreted gas is mixed in

- **Status:** open. Found by the core1 agent (hand-back §6, item 1) while writing test_li_be_burn. Trigger: `use_extended_composition`, inflow, and a surface convection zone whose base is cooler than about 1e6 K (Be9's rate at or below 1e-32 per s at the start or the end of the step). Whether cm_accretion meets it was not measured. Kind B for an accreting model with a cool base; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: LIBURN skips the convection zone's block, its accretion lines included, below the threshold ([liburn.f:230](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/liburn.f#L230); the accretion at [:366-391](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/liburn.f#L366-L391)):
  ```fortran
        IF(RBE90(JENV0).LE.1.0D-32.OR.RBE9(JENV).LE.1.0D-32)GOTO 200
  ```
- **Now:** `burn_li_be_zones`' return, [li_be_burn.f90:178-180](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/core/step/li_be_burn.f90#L178-L180), before the accreted share is mixed, [:191-197](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/core/step/li_be_burn.f90#L191-L197); `mix_accreted_composition` leaves the light elements to this routine, [mass_change_kernel.f90:254-256](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/core/step/mass_change_kernel.f90#L254-L256).
- **What is wrong:** when the mixed region is too cool to burn Be9, the routine returns before the mixed-region block, so the accreted Li6, Li7 and Be9 never reach the zone: its mass grows and its abundances stay, as if the accreted gas had the zone's own.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the zone gains the accreted share whether or not anything burns.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: mix the accreted share in whether or not the region burns; test_li_be_burn's "the zone gains the accreted share" then needs no rate above the threshold.

### M384. An empty path given to the C entry runs the host's first command-line argument as the deck

- **Status:** open. Found by the core1 agent (hand-back §6, item 2) in test_run_contracts: `yrec_run("", "")` ran the deck the test program was started with. pyyrec passes the paths it is given. Kind A for the decks (the command-line program does not use the overrides); size S.
- **In the original F77?** No: the C entry and the overrides are 2026's.
- **Now:** `read_input`, [controls_reader.f90:102-109](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/io/controls_reader.f90#L102-L109); `yrec_run` sets the overrides from the C strings, [yrec_capi.f90:69-70](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/core/run/yrec_capi.f90#L69-L70), under a header that says "an embedded engine must not read the host process's command line" and that empty strings fall back to yrec8.nml1/.nml2, [:13-16](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/core/run/yrec_capi.f90#L13-L16).
- **What is wrong:** an empty override is "no override", and the read then takes `getarg(1)`, the host's own first argument, falling back to yrec8.nml1 only when there is none.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the header's: the embedded engine reads no argv, and an empty path is the default name.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: `yrec_run` sets the overrides to the default names when a path is empty; a test_run_contracts check with the test program started with an argument.

### M385. The composition's closure leaves Z negative when X + He3 exceeds 1

- **Status:** open. Found by the core1 agent (hand-back §6, item 3) while writing test_composition_kernels. No model reaches it (it needs X > 1 − He3 out of the burn or the settling). Kind A where no deck reaches it; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes ([mix.f:434-435](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/mix.f#L434-L435)):
  ```fortran
           HCOMP(3,I) = MIN(HCOMP(3,I),1.0D0-HCOMP(1,I)-HCOMP(4,I))
           HCOMP(2,I) = 1.0D0 - HCOMP(1,I) - HCOMP(3,I) - HCOMP(4,I)
  ```
- **Now:** `clip_and_close_abundances`, [composition_kernels.f90:97-112](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/core/step/composition_kernels.f90#L97-L112).
- **What is wrong:** after each species is clipped to [0, 1], Z = min(Z, 1 − X − He3) is negative when X + He3 > 1 (X clipped to 1 with any He3), and nothing clamps it; Y = 1 − X − Z − He3 is then 0 with a negative Z.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** every mass fraction in [0, 1] after the closure.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: clamp Z at 0 and take the excess from He3; a check in test_composition_kernels.

- **Status:** open (test). Found by the core1 agent (hand-back §6, item 4) when the summary's move to io (a2eef385) had to be checked with a scratch program (the .mc1 and .mc2 files identical before and after). cm_monte_carlo reads its samples and rewinds its files but writes empty .mc1 and .mc2 files. Kind A; size S.

### M387. A mutation manifest that goes stale is noticed only at the next mutate.py run

- **Status:** open (tool). Found by the core1 agent (hand-back §6, item 5): test_run_contracts' mutation monte_carlo-03 went stale when a2eef385 re-indented the read loop, and nothing failed until the next `mutate.py` run of that program (b6903701). Kind A; size S.

- **Now:** `mutate.py --check` verifies that every manifest's `old` text occurs once, without a build ([mutate.py:176](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/tools/mutate.py#L176)); `make check` does not run it ([Makefile:520-528](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/Makefile#L520-L528)), and CI's workflow names no mutate.py step.

### M388. The zone between the last shell and the first envelope point took X and Z with the difference reversed

- **Status:** fixed in round 3 ([5fca7c63](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/5fca7c63), 2026-11-18, the core2 agent; byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins). Found by the core2 agent while writing test_envelope_refit. Latent: both drivers integrate the envelope at the shell's X and Z, so the difference was zero. Kind A; size S.

  ```

### M389. The envelope rebuild's shift lost a point after dropping one

- **Status:** fixed in round 3 ([4ccfa705](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/commit/4ccfa705), 2026-11-18, the core2 agent; byte-identical on the 56 decks and the 35 pins).               NUMNEW = NUMNEW + 1
  ```
- **Before the fix:** `shift_envelope_points`, [envelope_rebuild.f90:245-260](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/2ff65f9d/src/core/envelope/envelope_rebuild.f90#L245-L260) at 2ff65f9d.
- **What was wrong:** a point within 1e-10 dex of the last kept mass was dropped, but the next kept point still went to its own slot less one, so the list kept a stale, unshifted slot and lost its last point.
- **What we did:** the kept points are written to consecutive slots (`shift_envelope_onto_shell`, `envelope_refit_kernel.f90`); test_envelope_refit's "a dropped point leaves the rest contiguous" with its mutation.

### M390. A thin envelope leaves the previous integration's envelope points in place

- **Status:** open. Found by the core2 agent (hand-back §6, item 3). Kind A unless a model moves from a thick envelope to a thin one in one run (none known); size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: ENVINT's thin branch jumps past the loop and leaves NUMENV as it was ([envint.f:410-421](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/envint.f#L410-L421)).
- **Now:** `integrate_envelope`'s thin branch, [envelope_integration_kernel.f90:725-731](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L725-L731), where the other branch resets the count, [:736](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L736); `integrate_atmosphere` resets its own, [:489](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L489).
- **What is wrong:** when the fitting mass lies above -1e-12 no envelope is integrated, and `env_points%num_env_points` keeps what the previous integration set, so a caller that reads the points (the stitched model) appends the last integration's envelope.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** an integration's output is its own.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: the thin branch sets `env_points%num_env_points = 0`; test_envelope_integration's thin case without the test's own reset. With M309.

### M391. An envelope point exactly at the requested fitting mass makes two zones at one mass in the starting model's refit

- **Status:** open. Found by the core2 agent (hand-back §6, item 4) while writing test_envelope_refit, which checks only that the accepted point is a zone. Trigger: a requested fitting mass bit-equal to a point of the fresh integration (not seen). Kind A where not met; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: STARIN's `.LE.`.
- **Now:** `append_envelope_shells`' accepted branch, [envelope_refit_kernel.f90:151-155](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/core/envelope/envelope_refit_kernel.f90#L151-L155); the starting model passes `.true.`, [starting_model.f90:1040](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L1040), the rebuild `.false.`, [envelope_rebuild.f90:94](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/core/envelope/envelope_rebuild.f90#L94).
- **What is wrong:** with `accept_point_at_fit_mass` a point at the fitting mass becomes a zone, and the next point is then interpolated onto the same mass (f = 0): two zones at one log m, the second a copy of the first, and a zero dm.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** one zone per mass, as the rebuild's `.false.` gives.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed (core/model's call). Proposed fix: `.false.` for both callers, or stop after the accepted point.

### M392. The fitted vertex's diagnostics line could not be written

### M393. The profile's mu_e_inv is 0 at the envelope and atmosphere points

- **Status:** open. Found by the core2 agent (hand-back §6, item 6) while tracing the README's recipe "record a quantity at each envelope point". The integrands have 1/μ_e from the EOS and drop it (the old `qemu`, which nothing read). Kind B (the profile files' envelope rows; no .log, no pin); size S.

### M394. The turnover walk never ends for a fully convective model on a walk with envelope points

- **Status:** open. Found by the core3 agent (hand-back §6, item 1): in a scratch run of 3,000,000 random profiles 127,648 did not end, under the old walker and the new alike. Latent: `compute_turnover_timescale` walks a fully convective interior on its own points (the base lies more than a dex below the surface). Kind A; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: `LALLCZ`, `I = 1`, `JCORE = 1`, then the core-separation test and `GOTO 50` ([tauintnew.f:63-70](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/tauintnew.f#L63-L70), [:82-85](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/tauintnew.f#L82-L85)).
- **Now:** `time_surface_convection_zone`'s search, [turnover_walk.f90:126-155](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/core/diagnostics/turnover_walk.f90#L126-L155); `find_cz_bases`' fully convective case, [:231-251](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/core/diagnostics/turnover_walk.f90#L231-L251); `zone_hugs_convective_core`, [:258-270](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/core/diagnostics/turnover_walk.f90#L258-L270).
- **What is wrong:** the scan runs off the top inside a convective region, so the zone's base and the "core top" are both point 1; the core-separation test (a log P difference of 0, below 1 dex) holds when the walk has envelope points, the search restarts at point 2, finds the same, and so on.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a fully convective model is one zone; the walk ends.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: no core-separation test for a fully convective model, with a check in test_turnover.

### M395. The turnover walk's spline ignores the spline's failure

- **Status:** open. Found by the core3 agent (hand-back §6, item 2). Whether a deck has such a stencil was not counted. Kind A if none does, else B; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes in shape: KSPLINE and KSPLINT returned no status ([tauintnew.f:173-180](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/tauintnew.f#L173-L180)); cspline's status is 2026's.
- **Now:** `spline_stencil_value`, [turnover_walk.f90:516-524](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/core/diagnostics/turnover_walk.f90#L516-L524); `natural_spline`'s optional status, [cubic_spline.f90:99-108](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/numerics/cubic_spline.f90#L99-L108).
- **What is wrong:** with two coincident stencil nodes away from the bracketing pair, or nodes that are not monotonic (r − r_base − H_P where H_P grows faster than r), cspline returns without setting the second derivatives and `splint` interpolates with what the array held (zeros under -finit-local-zero: a linear interpolation), with ierr 0.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a failed step returns its status (core/README §3).
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: pass `ierr` to `natural_spline` and return it; count the decks first.

### M396. A model read does not set the fitting point's mass fraction, so the starting model's stitched model has no envelope

- **Status:** open. Found by the core3 agent (hand-back §6, item 3) with test_stitched (`num_env_points = 0`). Refined by reading: the read sets the member when the card moves its fitting point (`has_senv0_array`, through `move_fitting_point`'s first step), and not otherwise, as in cm_base. What it feeds: the starting model's turnover time and base radius, the `_prev` copy the first step's wind starts from; bug_sweep's O4 fix took the missing envelope as given. Measured in scratch (`scratch_r3_core3/patches/fitfrac.patch`): eight decks ALL IDENTICAL, and nothing moves in the combined `--set all` with the core3 agent's other B patches (why it does not reach the output was not traced). Kind B; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes in shape: STARIN sets SENV only under LSENV0 ([starin.f:477-484](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/starin.f#L477-L484)); whether its starting-model turnover time integrated an envelope was not traced. Counted with the F77.
- **Now:** `reset_state_after_read`, [starting_model.f90:338-363](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L338-L363); the move only when requested, [:681](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L681), and its first step's write, [:755](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/core/model/starting_model.f90#L755); the kernel's thin test, [envelope_integration_kernel.f90:96](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L96), [:725](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration_kernel.f90#L725), fed from the member, [envelope_integration.f90:198](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/core/envelope/envelope_integration.f90#L198).
- **What is wrong:** `log_fit_point_mass_fraction` is written by `refresh_surface_bc`, `change_mass`, the rezone and the envelope refit. On a run's first card without a fitting-point move it is 0 when the starting model's stitched model is built, so the envelope kernel takes "no envelope to integrate": that stitched model is the interior and the atmosphere, and its turnover walk runs on the interior points alone (on a later card the member holds the previous card's value).
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** the member describes the model in memory.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: `s%log_fit_point_mass_fraction = s%log_mass(s%nz) - s%log_total_mass` in `reset_state_after_read`.

### M398. Of three equal kept points the rezone's sort leaves two

- **Status:** open. Found by the core3 agent (hand-back §6, item 5) while writing test_model_kernels, which pins today's behaviour (the fix is its mutation mesh_spacing-04). Three criteria must flag the same point (the convective core's edge, the hydrogen shell's base and a jump can). Kind A where `tol_dm_min` > 0 drops the extra point (count the decks first), else B; size S.
- **In the original F77?** Yes: HPOINT's loop ([hpoint.f:243-254](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/6cd56739/src/hpoint.f#L243-L254)):
  ```fortran
        IF(NFLAG(I).EQ.NFLAG(I-1))THEN
  ...
  	 IFLAG = IFLAG - 1
        ENDIF
        I = I + 1
  ```
- **Now:** `sort_kept_points`, [mesh_spacing.f90:94-131](https://github.com/parallelpro/yrec/blob/7ea92ace/src/core/model/mesh_spacing.f90#L94-L131).
- **What is wrong:** after a duplicate is removed the scan moves on to the next slot, so it does not compare the point that slid into the current one. A duplicate kept point gives `space_points_along_chi` a segment of zero length, one new point at the same log m as the last, which `remove_crowded_points` drops when `tol_dm_min` is positive, unless it is the mesh's last point.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** each point flagged once.
- **What we did:** recorded, not fixed. Proposed fix: do not advance after a removal (`i = i + 1` only when nothing was removed).

### M402. ZAHB_m1p0feh+0p0_TAHB may be bistable: two unrelated changes end it at the same model

- **Status:** open, a question for the measured round. The round's integrator's (from the core3 agent's B list and O1's entry). Kind: a deck's sensitivity, not a code defect; it decides how the measured round's stop rules read this deck.
- **In the original F77?** Not determined (no F77 run of the deck exists); counted with the F77, as M294 is.
- **Now:** the deck, `examples/run_from_zahb_to_tahb/ZAHB_m1p0feh+0p0_TAHB.inlist`.
- **What is wrong:** O1's convective L partial (the convergence round) and the luminosity renormalization's move into the step (the core3 agent's B list, which moves no other deck of the 56 and first changes this one at model 450 of card 3, in the timestep's sixth digit) both end the run on central Y at model 1429 instead of 1726, at 0.224451 Gyr instead of 0.243117 (7.68% younger). Two changes that share nothing reaching the same end suggests the deck has two outcomes and a perturbation picks one; then its 15% and 6% stop rules measure the deck, not a change's size.
- **Expected behaviour, and why:** a stop rule measures the change under test.
- **What we did:** recorded. Proposed: in the measured round, run the deck with a deliberate tiny perturbation (the timestep at one model by 1e-12, say) and see whether it too ends at 1429; if it does, judge changes on this deck by their first differing line, as for the path-sensitive decks, and not by its model count.
